whyB: 9 adds the two times; together they should finish faster, not slower.
whyD: 3 is Jose's time alone; Pedro's help makes it shorter.
explanationTl: Si Pedro 1/6 ng room kada oras, si Jose 1/3. Sabay: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 kada oras, kaya 2 hours.
stepsTl:
1. Pedro: 1/6 kada oras.
2. Jose: 1/3 kada oras.
3. Sabay: 1/6 + 2/6 = 1/2 kada oras.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/2 = 2 hours.
hintTl: I-add ang rates nila (bahagi ng trabaho kada oras), hindi ang oras.

text: If a = b + c and b=3, c=7, what is a?
steps: Replace each letter with its value: a = 3 + 7 = 10.
hint: Substitute the given values, then compute.
stepsTl: Palitan ang bawat letra ng value nito: a = 3 + 7 = 10.
hintTl: I-substitute ang values, tapos i-compute.

explanation: Same denominators, so add the numerators: 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4, which simplifies to 1/2.
steps:
1. The denominators are the same (4).
2. Add the numerators: 1 + 1 = 2, so 2/4.
3. Simplify: 2/4 = 1/2.
hint: When the denominators match, add only the numerators, then simplify.
whyB: 1/4 is just one of the addends; adding gives more than that.
whyC: 2/8 adds the denominators too; only the numerators are added.
whyD: 0/4 subtracts instead of adding.
explanationTl: Pareho ang denominator, kaya i-add lang ang numerators: 2/4, na pwedeng i-simplify sa 1/2.
stepsTl:
1. Pareho ang denominator (4).
2. I-add ang numerators: 1 + 1 = 2, so 2/4.
3. I-simplify: 2/4 = 1/2.
hintTl: Kapag pareho ang denominator, numerators lang ang i-add, tapos i-simplify.

text: What is the next number in the series: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, ...?
explanation: Each term goes up by 2, so 10 + 2 = 12.
steps:
1. Each term goes up by 2.
2. Next: 12.
hint: Write the difference between neighbours. If that isn't constant, try ratios or the differences of differences.
whyB: 11 adds only 1.
whyC: 13 adds 3.
whyD: 9 goes down instead of up.
explanationTl: Dagdag ng 2 bawat isa, kaya 10 + 2 = 12.
stepsTl:
1. Pare-pareho ang dagdag (2) bawat hakbang.
2. Kaya ang susunod ay 12.
hintTl: Isulat ang pagitan ng bawat numero. Kung hindi pare-pareho, subukan ang ratio.

text: The next in the sequence: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8?
explanation: Fibonacci: 5+8 = 13.

text: If a = b + c and b=5, c=5, what is a?
steps: Replace each letter with its value: a = 5 + 5 = 10.
hint: Substitute the given values, then compute.
stepsTl: Palitan ang bawat letra ng value nito: a = 5 + 5 = 10.
hintTl: I-substitute ang values, tapos i-compute.

text: After a 10% discount, a book costs ₱180. What was its original price?
explanation: ₱180 is 90% of the original price, so the original price = 180 ÷ 0.9 = ₱200.
steps:
1. After a 10% discount you pay 90% of the price.
2. 0.9 × original = ₱180.
3. Original = 180 ÷ 0.9 = ₱200.
Check: 10% of ₱200 = ₱20; ₱200 − ₱20 = ₱180 ✓
hint: ₱180 is what percent of the original price?
whyA: ₱198 adds 10% of ₱180; the 10% was taken from the original price, not from ₱180.
whyB: ₱190 just adds ₱10 back; the discount was ₱20.
whyC: ₱162 takes another 10% off ₱180 instead of going back to the original.
explanationTl: Ang ₱180 ay 90% ng original price, kaya original = 180 ÷ 0.9 = ₱200.
stepsTl:
1. Kapag 10% ang discount, 90% lang ng presyo ang binabayaran.
2. 0.9 × original = ₱180.
3. Original = 180 ÷ 0.9 = ₱200.
Check: 10% ng ₱200 = ₱20; ₱200 − ₱20 = ₱180 ✓
hintTl: Ilang percent ng original price ang ₱180?

text: What is the capital of the Philippines?
explanation: Manila is the capital of the Philippines under Presidential Decree No. 940 (1976). Quezon City was the official capital from 1948 to 1976.
hint: One option was a former capital; the current one is the historic city along the Pasig River.
whyB: Cebu City is the oldest Spanish settlement and a major city, but not the capital.
whyC: Davao City is the biggest city in Mindanao, but not the capital.
whyD: Quezon City was the capital from 1948 to 1976, until PD 940 restored Manila.
explanationTl: Manila ang capital ng Pilipinas, ayon sa Presidential Decree No. 940 noong 1976. Ang Quezon City ay naging capital mula 1948 hanggang 1976, kaya madalas yun ang trap.
hintTl: Isa sa choices ay dating capital lang. Alin ang capital ngayon?

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, a candidate for President must be a resident of the Philippines for at least how many years immediately preceding the election?
explanation: Art. VII, Sec. 2 requires the President to be a natural-born citizen, a registered voter, able to read and write, at least 40 years old on election day, and a resident of the Philippines for at least ten years immediately preceding the election.
hint: It is the longest residency requirement among national elective posts.
whyA: Two years is the residency requirement for Senators (Art. VI, Sec. 3).
whyB: Five years is not the residency rule for any national elective post in the Constitution.
whyD: Fifteen years is too long; no national post requires it.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 2, kailangan ng President na natural-born citizen, registered voter, marunong magbasa at magsulat, at least 40 years old, at resident ng Pilipinas for at least ten years bago ang election.
hintTl: Ito ang pinakamahabang residency requirement sa mga national na posisyon.

text: The present Philippine Constitution was ratified in a nationwide plebiscite held in what year?
explanation: The present Constitution was ratified in the plebiscite of February 2, 1987, and under Article XVIII, Section 27 it took effect immediately upon ratification. It was drafted by the 1986 Constitutional Commission under President Corazon Aquino.
hint: It is the year in the name we usually give the present Constitution.
whyB: 1973 is the Marcos-era Constitution that the present one replaced.
whyC: 1935 is the Commonwealth Constitution.
whyD: 1986 is when the Constitutional Commission drafted the text; ratification came the following year.
explanationTl: Ang present Constitution ay na-ratify sa plebiscite noong February 2, 1987, at ayon sa Article XVIII, Section 27, effective agad ito upon ratification. Ang 1986 Constitutional Commission ang nag-draft nito.
hintTl: Ito yung year na kasama sa tawag natin sa present Constitution.

text: Republic Act No. 6713 is known as the:
optionC: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
optionD: Act Defining and Penalizing the Crime of Plunder
explanation: RA 6713, approved in 1989, is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (Section 1 states its title). It sets norms of conduct (Section 4) and requires the Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (Section 8).
hint: Think of the law that sets the standards of behavior and the SALN requirement for government workers.
whyA: The Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act is RA 3019 (1960).
whyB: The Ombudsman Act of 1989 is RA 6770.
whyD: The Plunder Law is RA 7080.
explanationTl: Ang RA 6713 (1989) ay ang Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. Dito galing ang norms of conduct (Section 4) at ang requirement na mag-file ng SALN (Section 8).
hintTl: Isipin ang batas na nagtatakda ng tamang asal at ng SALN para sa mga government employee.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the three branches of the Philippine government are:
explanation: The 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in Congress (Art. VI, Sec. 1), executive power in the President (Art. VII, Sec. 1), and judicial power in the Supreme Court and lower courts (Art. VIII, Sec. 1).
hint: Think of who makes the laws, who carries them out, and who interprets them.
whyB: Elections are run by the COMELEC, a constitutional commission, not a separate branch of government.
whyC: The Constitutional Commissions (Art. IX) are independent bodies, not one of the three branches; the Executive is missing.
whyD: Local governments (Art. X) are political subdivisions, not a branch; the Legislative is missing.
explanationTl: Sa 1987 Constitution, ang legislative power ay nasa Congress (Art. VI, Sec. 1), ang executive power ay nasa President (Art. VII, Sec. 1), at ang judicial power ay nasa Supreme Court at lower courts (Art. VIII, Sec. 1). Kaya tatlo: Executive, Legislative, Judicial.
hintTl: Isipin mo: sino ang gumagawa ng batas, sino ang nagpapatupad, at sino ang nag-i-interpret?

text: Who is regarded as the national hero of the Philippines?
explanation: Jose Rizal is honored as the national hero; Rizal Day on December 30 marks his execution at Bagumbayan in 1896.
hint: He wrote Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo.
whyB: Bonifacio founded the Katipunan and is a national hero too, but Rizal is the one honored as THE national hero.
whyC: Aguinaldo was the first President, not the national hero.
whyD: Lapu-Lapu is honored as the first Filipino to resist Spanish rule.
explanationTl: Si Jose Rizal ang kinikilalang national hero; ang Rizal Day tuwing December 30 ay paggunita sa execution niya sa Bagumbayan noong 1896.
hintTl: Siya ang sumulat ng Noli Me Tangere at El Filibusterismo.

text: Which set of colors appears on the Philippine flag?
optionA: Blue, red, white and golden yellow
optionC: Red, white, green and golden yellow
optionD: Blue, white, black and golden yellow
explanation: Under RA 8491, Sec. 4, the flag is blue, white and red, with an eight-rayed golden-yellow sun and three five-pointed golden-yellow stars in the white triangle.
hint: Picture the sun and the three stars inside the white triangle.
whyB: There is no green on the flag; the sun and stars are golden yellow.
whyC: This drops the blue stripe and adds green, which is not on the flag.
whyD: The lower stripe is red, not black.
explanationTl: Sa RA 8491, Sec. 4, blue, white at red ang flag, may eight-rayed golden-yellow sun at tatlong five-pointed golden-yellow stars sa white triangle.
hintTl: Isipin ang araw at tatlong bituin sa loob ng white triangle.

text: Region VII of the Philippines is known as:
explanation: Region VII is Central Visayas, with Cebu City as its regional center; Western Visayas is Region VI and Eastern Visayas is Region VIII.
hint: The Visayas regions are numbered west to east: VI, VII, VIII.
whyB: Western Visayas is Region VI.
whyC: Eastern Visayas is Region VIII.
whyD: Northern Mindanao is Region X.
explanationTl: Ang Region VII ay Central Visayas, Cebu City ang regional center. Ang Western Visayas ay Region VI, at Eastern Visayas ay Region VIII.
hintTl: Ang Visayas regions ay naka-number mula west papuntang east: VI, VII, VIII.

text: Which is the largest island in the Philippines by land area?
explanation: Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines; Mindanao is the second largest.
hint: Metro Manila is located on this island.
whyB: Mindanao is the second-largest island, slightly smaller than Luzon.
whyC: Samar is the largest island in the Visayas but much smaller than Luzon.
whyD: Palawan is a long, narrow island, far smaller than Luzon.
explanationTl: Luzon ang pinakamalaking isla sa Pilipinas; pangalawa ang Mindanao.
hintTl: Nandito ang Metro Manila.

text: Philippine Independence Day is celebrated every:
explanation: Independence Day marks the proclamation of Philippine independence from Spain by Emilio Aguinaldo in Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898. The celebration was moved from July 4 to June 12 in 1962 and fixed by Republic Act No. 4166 (1964).
hint: Think of the 1898 proclamation in Kawit, Cavite.
whyB: July 4 is when the US recognized Philippine independence in 1946; it was celebrated as Independence Day only until 1961 and was renamed Republic Day.
whyC: August 31 is not Philippine Independence Day; National Heroes Day falls on the last Monday of August.
whyD: April 9 is Araw ng Kagitingan (Day of Valor), commemorating the Fall of Bataan in 1942.
explanationTl: June 12 ang Independence Day natin, kasi noong June 12, 1898 dineklara ni Emilio Aguinaldo ang independence mula sa Spain sa Kawit, Cavite. Dati July 4 ang celebration, pero inilipat sa June 12 noong 1962 at ginawang batas ng RA 4166 noong 1964.
hintTl: Alalahanin mo ang proclamation sa Kawit, Cavite noong 1898.

text: According to the Philippine Constitution, what is the minimum age to run for President?
explanation: Article VII, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution requires the President to be a natural-born citizen, a registered voter, able to read and write, at least 40 years of age on the day of the election, and a resident of the Philippines for at least ten years immediately preceding the election.
hint: It is older than the minimum age for Senators.
whyA: 35 is the minimum age for Senators (Art. VI, Sec. 3), not the President.
whyB: 30 is not the age requirement for President; it is too low.
whyD: 25 is the minimum age for members of the House of Representatives (Art. VI, Sec. 6).
explanationTl: Sa Article VII, Section 2 ng 1987 Constitution, dapat at least 40 years old sa araw ng election ang tatakbong President, bukod sa pagiging natural-born citizen, registered voter, marunong bumasa at sumulat, at 10 years resident ng Pilipinas.
hintTl: Mas mataas ito sa minimum age ng Senators.

text: RA 6713 refers to the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for:
explanation: RA 6713 (1989) is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees; Section 4 lists the norms of conduct, such as commitment to public interest, professionalism and justness.
hint: The law is about people who serve in government.
whyB: Private sector workers are covered by the Labor Code, not RA 6713.
whyC: Students are not the subject of RA 6713; it governs those in public service.
whyD: Military personnel are public servants too, but the law is not limited to them; it covers all public officials and employees.
explanationTl: Ang RA 6713 ay ang Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. Sa Section 4 nakalista ang norms of conduct, gaya ng commitment to public interest at professionalism.
hintTl: Tungkol ito sa mga taong nagtatrabaho sa gobyerno.

text: How many Senators are there in the Philippine Senate?
explanation: Article VI, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the Senate is composed of 24 Senators elected at large by the qualified voters of the Philippines.
hint: Half of them are elected every three years, 12 at a time.
whyB: 20 is not the constitutional number of Senators.
whyC: 30 is not the constitutional number of Senators.
whyD: 12 is the number of Senators elected in each regular election, not the total membership.
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 2 ng 1987 Constitution, 24 ang Senators, at elected at large sila ng buong bansa.
hintTl: Kalahati lang sa kanila ang ine-elect tuwing three years, 12 bawat election.

text: What does the Bill of Rights in the Constitution primarily protect?
explanation: The Bill of Rights, Article III of the 1987 Constitution, protects individual rights and freedoms, such as due process and free speech, against abuse by the State.
hint: It limits what the government can do to a person.
whyB: Economic policy is in Art. XII (National Economy and Patrimony), not the Bill of Rights.
whyC: Foreign relations are led by the President, with treaties needing Senate concurrence; not Art. III.
whyD: Military powers fall under the Commander-in-Chief clause, Art. VII, Sec. 18.
explanationTl: Ang Bill of Rights, Article III ng 1987 Constitution, ay nagpo-protect ng individual rights at freedoms, gaya ng due process at free speech, laban sa abuso ng State.
hintTl: Nililimitahan nito ang kayang gawin ng gobyerno sa isang tao.

text: Under RA 6713, what is a prohibited act for public officials?
optionB: Accepting gifts that create conflict of interest
explanation: Section 7(d) of RA 6713 prohibits public officials and employees from soliciting or accepting gifts or anything of monetary value in connection with any transaction affected by the functions of their office. Political neutrality, professionalism and responsiveness are norms of conduct required under Section 4, not prohibited acts.
hint: Three of the options are duties every public servant must follow.
whyA: Political neutrality is a required norm of conduct under Section 4(h), not a prohibited act.
whyC: Professionalism is a required norm of conduct under Section 4(b).
whyD: Responsiveness to the public is a required norm of conduct under Section 4(e).
explanationTl: Sa Section 7(d) ng RA 6713, bawal sa public officials at employees ang humingi o tumanggap ng regalo o anumang may halaga na konektado sa trabaho nila. Yung political neutrality, professionalism at responsiveness ay mga norms of conduct sa Section 4, ibig sabihin required yun, hindi bawal.
hintTl: Tatlo sa choices ay mga dapat gawin ng public servant. Alin ang hindi?

text: What branch of government includes the President and Vice President?
explanation: Under Article VII, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution, executive power is vested in the President; Section 3 provides for the Vice President, who belongs to the same Executive Department.
hint: Think of the branch that implements and enforces the laws.
whyB: The Legislative branch is Congress (Senate and House), which makes laws.
whyC: The Judicial branch is the Supreme Court and lower courts, which interpret laws.
whyD: Local governments are not a branch of the national government; they are political subdivisions under Article X.
explanationTl: Sa Article VII, Section 1 ng 1987 Constitution, ang executive power ay nasa President; sa Section 3 naman ang Vice President, na parte rin ng Executive Department.
hintTl: Isipin mo kung aling branch ang nag-i-implement at nag-e-enforce ng batas.

text: In peace education, 'positive peace' refers to:
optionA: The mere absence of war and violence
optionB: The presence of justice, equity and respect for human rights
optionC: A strong military that deters attack
explanation: Positive peace goes beyond the absence of war (negative peace): it means social justice, equity and respect for human rights that remove the causes of conflict.
hint: 'Positive' means something is present, not just missing.
whyA: The mere absence of war is 'negative peace'.
whyC: Military strength may deter war but does not create justice.
whyD: Economic growth alone does not ensure justice or rights.
explanationTl: Ang positive peace ay higit pa sa walang giyera (negative peace); ibig sabihin may social justice, equity at respeto sa human rights na nag-aalis ng ugat ng conflict.
hintTl: 'Positive' = may meron, hindi lang may nawala.

text: Which of the following is one of the norms of conduct of public officials and employees under Section 4 of RA 6713?
explanation: Section 4(A) of RA 6713 lists eight norms of conduct: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living. Professionalism is Section 4(A)(b).
hint: Recall the norm about performing duties with excellence, intelligence and skill.
whyB: RA 6713 requires the opposite, political neutrality: services are provided without partisanship.
whyC: Seniority is a factor in some personnel actions, but it is not one of the eight norms in Section 4.
whyD: The norms call for commitment to public interest above personal interest, not personal loyalty to superiors.
explanationTl: Sa Section 4(A) ng RA 6713, walo ang norms of conduct, at isa dito ang professionalism: dapat excellent, competent at skilled ang pagganap sa trabaho.
hintTl: Alalahanin mo yung norm tungkol sa pagtatrabaho nang may excellence at skill.

text: Under Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution, the State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a ____ ecology.
explanation: Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution states that the State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.
hint: The phrase pairs the idea of nature in equilibrium with the idea of human health.
whyB: 'Clean and green' is a popular campaign slogan, not the constitutional wording.
whyC: 'Safe and sanitary' sounds like health-code language, not Article II, Section 16.
whyD: 'Productive and sustainable' echoes development policy terms, not the exact constitutional phrase.
explanationTl: Sa Article II, Section 16, ang right ng tao ay sa isang 'balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.'
hintTl: Dalawang idea ang pinagsama: balanse ng kalikasan at kalusugan ng tao.

text: How many Representatives are in the House based on population?
explanation: The House has not more than 250 members, but can be more with party-list.

text: What are the 3 main branches of the Government of the Philippines?
optionD: The Legislature, The Senate, The Supreme Court
explanation: The 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in Congress (Art VI), executive power in the President (Art VII), and judicial power in the Supreme Court and lower courts (Art VIII).
hint: Think of separation of powers: one branch makes laws, one carries them out, one interprets them.
whyA: These are institutions, not branches; the Senate is part of Congress, so the legislature is counted twice.
whyB: These are forms of government, not branches of government.
whyD: The Senate is part of the Legislature, and the executive branch is missing entirely.
explanationTl: Separation of powers: Legislative (Congress, Art VI), Executive (President, Art VII), at Judicial (Supreme Court at lower courts, Art VIII).
hintTl: Isa ang gumagawa ng batas, isa ang nagpapatupad, at isa ang nag-i-interpret.

text: The Supreme Court is composed of a Chief Justice and how many Associate Justices?
explanation: Art. VIII, Sec. 4(1) of the 1987 Constitution: the Supreme Court is composed of a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices, 15 members in all.
hint: The full Court has 15 members; subtract the Chief Justice.
whyA: Twelve is too few; the Court has 15 members in total.
whyB: Thirteen would make only 14 members, one short.
whyD: Fifteen is the total membership including the Chief Justice, not the number of Associate Justices.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VIII, Sec. 4(1), ang Supreme Court ay may isang Chief Justice at fourteen Associate Justices, kaya 15 lahat.
hintTl: 15 ang buong Court; ibawas mo ang Chief Justice.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, who is the Commander-in-Chief of all armed forces of the Philippines?
optionC: Chief of Staff of the AFP
explanation: Art. VII, Sec. 18 of the 1987 Constitution makes the President the Commander-in-Chief of all armed forces of the Philippines.
hint: Civilian authority is supreme over the military; look for the highest civilian official.
whyA: The Defense Secretary is a Cabinet member under the President, not the Commander-in-Chief.
whyC: The AFP Chief of Staff is the top military officer but answers to the President.
whyD: The Senate President heads the Senate, part of the legislative branch.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 18, ang President ang Commander-in-Chief ng lahat ng armed forces ng Pilipinas.
hintTl: Mas mataas ang civilian authority kaysa military; sino ang pinakamataas na civilian official?

text: The executive power shall be vested in the _________.
explanation: Art. VII, Sec. 1 of the 1987 Constitution: the executive power shall be vested in the President of the Philippines.
hint: Executive means carrying out the laws; who heads the government?
whyB: The House of Representatives shares legislative power with the Senate (Art. VI, Sec. 1).
whyC: The Supreme Court holds judicial power (Art. VIII, Sec. 1).
whyD: Congress holds legislative power, not executive power.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 1, ang executive power ay nasa President of the Philippines.
hintTl: Executive = nagpapatupad ng batas. Sino ang head ng gobyerno?

text: The legislative power shall be vested in the _________ which shall consist of a Senate and a House of Representatives.
explanation: Art. VI, Sec. 1 of the 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in the Congress of the Philippines, which consists of a Senate and a House of Representatives (except the power reserved to the people by initiative and referendum).
hint: Look for the body with two chambers.
whyB: Batasang Pambansa was the legislature under the 1973 Constitution, not the 1987 one.
whyC: The Supreme Court holds judicial power (Art. VIII, Sec. 1).
whyD: The President holds executive power (Art. VII, Sec. 1).
explanationTl: Sa Art. VI, Sec. 1, ang legislative power ay nasa Congress of the Philippines, na binubuo ng Senate at House of Representatives.
hintTl: Hanapin ang body na may dalawang chamber.

text: The Senate shall be composed of how many senators elected at large by voters of the Philippines?
explanation: Article VI, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the Senate is composed of 24 senators elected at large by the qualified voters of the Philippines.
hint: Think of the number of senatorial slots on a full ballot, which is twice the number elected every three years.
whyA: 21 is not in the Constitution; it may come from confusing the count with the number of members of other bodies.
whyB: 22 is a guess just under the real figure; the Constitution fixes it at 24.
whyC: 23 is one short; the Senate has 24 seats, 12 elected every three years.
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 2 ng 1987 Constitution, 24 senators ang bumubuo sa Senate, at elected at large sila ng mga botante sa buong Pilipinas.
hintTl: Isipin mo kung ilan ang senador na binoboto every three years, tapos i-double mo.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, how long is the term of office of a senator?
explanation: Article VI, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the term of office of senators is six years, and no senator may serve more than two consecutive terms.
hint: A senator's term is twice as long as the term of a member of the House of Representatives.
whyA: 3 years is the term of a member of the House of Representatives (Art VI Sec 7), not a senator.
whyB: 4 years is not a term used for senators under the 1987 Constitution.
whyC: 5 years is not a constitutional term for senators; it may be confused with other fixed terms.
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 4, six years ang term ng senador, at hanggang two consecutive terms lang ang pwede.
hintTl: Doble ang term ng senador kumpara sa congressman.

text: The President and Vice-President of the Philippines are elected for a term of how many years?
explanation: Under Art. VII, Sec. 4 of the 1987 Constitution, the President and Vice-President are elected for a term of six years. The President cannot be reelected.
hint: It is the same length as a senator's term.
whyA: Three years is the term of members of the House of Representatives (Art. VI, Sec. 7).
whyB: Four years is the US presidential term, not the Philippine one.
whyC: Five years is not the term of any elected national official under the 1987 Constitution.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 4 ng 1987 Constitution, six years ang term ng President at Vice-President. Bawal nang ma-reelect ang President.
hintTl: Pareho ito ng term ng senador.

text: The members of the House of Representatives shall be elected for a term of _______.
explanation: Under Article VI, Section 7 of the 1987 Constitution, members of the House of Representatives are elected for a term of three years. They may not serve more than three consecutive terms.
hint: It is the shortest elective term in Congress.
whyB: Four years is not a term used for any national elective office in the 1987 Constitution.
whyC: Five years is not the term of Representatives; it is a guess between the House and Senate terms.
whyD: Six years is the term of Senators (Art. VI, Sec. 4), not Representatives.
explanationTl: Ayon sa Article VI, Section 7 ng 1987 Constitution, three years ang term ng mga miyembro ng House of Representatives. Hanggang three consecutive terms lang sila.
hintTl: Ito ang pinakamaikling term sa Congress.

text: Under Article VI, Section 28(3) of the 1987 Constitution, which of the following is NOT exempt from taxation?
optionA: A privately owned office building leased out for profit
explanation: Article VI, Section 28(3) of the 1987 Constitution exempts charitable institutions, churches and convents appurtenant thereto, non-profit cemeteries, and lands, buildings and improvements actually, directly and exclusively used for religious, charitable or educational purposes. A building leased out for profit is not among them.
hint: Ask whether the property is used for religious, charitable or educational purposes.
whyB: Churches and convents appurtenant thereto are expressly exempt under Sec. 28(3).
whyC: Charitable institutions are expressly exempt under Sec. 28(3).
whyD: Non-profit cemeteries are expressly exempt under Sec. 28(3).
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 28(3), exempt sa tax ang charitable institutions, churches at convents, non-profit cemeteries, at mga lupa o building na ginagamit actually, directly and exclusively para sa religious, charitable o educational purposes. Ang building na pinapaupahan para kumita ay hindi kasama diyan.
hintTl: Tanungin mo: ginagamit ba ito for religious, charitable o educational purposes?

text: The Congress, by a vote of ____ of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately, shall have the sole power to declare a state of war.
explanation: Article VI, Section 23(1) of the 1987 Constitution provides that Congress, by a vote of two-thirds of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately, has the sole power to declare the existence of a state of war.
hint: Declaring war is a grave act, so it needs a supermajority, the same fraction used to override a presidential veto.
whyB: One-half (a simple majority) is too low for an act as grave as declaring war.
whyC: Three-quarters is not used here; it is higher than what Section 23 requires.
whyD: Three-fifths is not the fraction in Section 23; the Constitution requires two-thirds.
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 23(1), kailangan ng two-thirds vote ng both Houses, in joint session pero voting separately, para mag-declare ng state of war ang Congress.
hintTl: Mabigat na desisyon ang pag-declare ng war, kaya supermajority ang kailangan. Pareho ito sa fraction para ma-override ang veto ng President.

text: It states that “no person shall be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law, nor any person be denied the equal protection of the laws.”
explanation: This is from Article III, the Bill of Rights.

text: Under Article II, Section 18 of the 1987 Constitution, the State affirms labor as:
optionC: an equal partner of capital in all enterprises
explanation: Article II, Section 18 states that the State affirms labor as a primary social economic force and shall protect the rights of workers and promote their welfare. Article XIII, Section 3 adds full protection to labor and promotion of full employment.
hint: The phrase pairs "social" and "economic" in one description.
whyA: Sounds plausible, but this phrase is not in Article II, Section 18.
whyC: The Constitution speaks of shared responsibility between workers and employers (Art. XIII, Sec. 3), not labor as an equal partner of capital in all enterprises.
whyD: Article XV, Section 1 calls the family, not labor, the foundation of the nation.
explanationTl: Sa Article II, Section 18, sinasabi na ina-affirm ng State ang labor bilang primary social economic force, at poprotektahan nito ang rights at welfare ng workers. Sa Article XIII, Section 3 naman yung full protection to labor at full employment.
hintTl: Yung phrase ay may "social" at "economic" na magkasama.

text: The national language of the Philippines is:
explanation: Article XIV, Section 6 of the 1987 Constitution states that the national language of the Philippines is Filipino, which shall be further developed and enriched on the basis of existing Philippine and other languages.
hint: The 1987 Constitution uses a name that is not tied to any single regional language.
whyA: English is an official language for communication and instruction (Art XIV Sec 7), not the national language.
whyC: Tagalog is a regional language that Filipino is largely based on, but the Constitution names Filipino, not Tagalog.
whyD: Cebuano is a major regional language, not the national language.
explanationTl: Ayon sa Article XIV, Section 6 ng 1987 Constitution, Filipino ang national language natin. Hindi Tagalog, kahit malaki ang base nito sa Tagalog.
hintTl: Yung pangalan na ginamit ng Constitution ay hindi pangalan ng isang rehiyon lang.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, how is the Speaker of the House of Representatives chosen?
optionB: Elected by a majority vote of all the Members of the House
optionC: Elected by the people in a nationwide vote
optionD: The longest-serving Member automatically becomes Speaker
explanation: Article VI, Section 16(1) of the 1987 Constitution provides that the House of Representatives elects its Speaker by a majority vote of all its Members. The Senate elects its President the same way.
hint: Each chamber of Congress picks its own presiding officer.
whyA: The President has no power to appoint the leaders of Congress; that would violate separation of powers.
whyC: Only the President, Vice-President and senators are elected nationwide; the Speaker is chosen by fellow Members.
whyD: Seniority does not decide it; the Constitution requires an election by majority vote of all Members.
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 16(1) ng 1987 Constitution, ang mga Members mismo ng House ang nag-e-elect ng Speaker, by majority vote of all Members. Ganun din sa Senate, sila ang pumipili ng Senate President.
hintTl: Isipin mo: sino ang pumipili ng leader ng bawat chamber ng Congress?

text: The main function of the Office of the Ombudsman is to:
optionA: Investigate complaints against public officials and employees
optionD: Decide questions on the constitutionality of laws
explanation: Under Art. XI, Secs. 12-13 of the 1987 Constitution, the Ombudsman acts on complaints against public officials and employees and investigates any illegal, unjust, improper or inefficient act or omission.
hint: The Ombudsman is called the 'protector of the people' against abuse in government.
whyB: Enacting laws belongs to Congress and local legislative bodies (Art. VI, Sec. 1).
whyC: Auditing government funds is the job of the Commission on Audit (Art. IX-D).
whyD: Ruling on constitutionality is a power of the Supreme Court (Art. VIII, Sec. 5).
explanationTl: Sa Art. XI, Secs. 12-13, ang Ombudsman ang nag-a-act sa complaints laban sa public officials at employees, at nag-iimbestiga ng illegal o improper na acts nila.
hintTl: Siya ang 'protector of the people' laban sa abuso sa gobyerno.

text: Republic Act No. 9262 is also known as the:
optionA: Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004
explanation: RA 9262 is the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004 (Anti-VAWC Act), which defines and penalizes violence against women and their children.
hint: Its common short name is 'VAWC'.
whyB: The Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act is RA 3019.
whyC: The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act is RA 9003.
whyD: The Labor Code is Presidential Decree No. 442, not a Republic Act.
explanationTl: Ang RA 9262 ay ang Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004, o mas kilala bilang Anti-VAWC Act. Pinoprotektahan nito ang mga babae at mga anak nila laban sa violence.
hintTl: Ang kilalang short name nito ay 'VAWC'.

text: The three major island groups of the Philippines are:
explanation: The Philippine archipelago is divided into three major island groups: Luzon in the north, the Visayas in the center, and Mindanao in the south. They are represented by the three stars on the national flag.
hint: Remember the three stars on the Philippine flag.
whyA: Palawan is a province under the Luzon group, not a separate major island group.
whyB: Sulu is an archipelago that belongs to the Mindanao group.
whyC: Samar is an island in the Visayas, not a major island group by itself.
explanationTl: Tatlo ang major island groups ng Pilipinas: Luzon sa north, Visayas sa gitna, at Mindanao sa south. Sila ang tatlong bituin sa watawat.
hintTl: Alalahanin ang tatlong bituin sa watawat ng Pilipinas.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, Members of the Supreme Court hold office during good behavior until they reach the age of:
explanation: Art. VIII, Sec. 11 provides that Members of the Supreme Court and judges of lower courts hold office during good behavior until they reach the age of seventy years or become incapacitated.
hint: It is the same age limit that applies to judges of lower courts.
whyA: 65 is the compulsory retirement age in the general civil service, not for justices.
whyC: 75 is not the constitutional limit; justices must leave earlier.
whyD: 60 is the optional retirement age for many government workers, not the justices' limit.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VIII, Sec. 11, ang Supreme Court justices at lower court judges ay nasa pwesto habang good behavior, until mag-70 years old sila o ma-incapacitate.
hintTl: Parehong age ito para sa justices at sa mga judge ng lower courts.

text: What is the main function of the Commission on Elections (COMELEC)?
optionA: Enforce and administer all laws on the conduct of elections
optionB: Audit the accounts of government agencies
explanation: Under Article IX-C, Section 2(1) of the 1987 Constitution, the COMELEC enforces and administers all laws and regulations relating to the conduct of elections, plebiscites, initiatives, referendums and recalls.
hint: The answer is in the commission's name.
whyB: Auditing government accounts is the job of the Commission on Audit (Art. IX-D).
whyC: Appointments belong mainly to the President; the Civil Service Commission handles the civil service, not COMELEC.
whyD: Making laws is the job of Congress (Art. VI), not a constitutional commission.
explanationTl: Sa Article IX-C, Section 2(1) ng 1987 Constitution, ang COMELEC ang nag-e-enforce at nag-a-administer ng lahat ng election laws, pati plebiscite, initiative, referendum at recall.
hintTl: Nasa pangalan na mismo ng commission ang sagot.

text: Republic Act No. 9003 is known as the:
explanation: RA 9003 is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000. It requires waste segregation at source and bans open dumpsites.
hint: This law is about garbage: segregation, recycling and materials recovery facilities.
whyB: The Philippine Clean Air Act is RA 8749 (1999).
whyC: The Water Code of the Philippines is PD 1067.
whyD: The Forestry Code (Revised Forestry Code) is PD 705.
explanationTl: Ang RA 9003 ay ang Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000. Dito nanggaling ang waste segregation at ang pagbabawal sa open dumpsites.
hintTl: Tungkol ito sa basura: segregation, recycling, at MRF.

text: What is the capital city of Brazil?
explanation: Brasilia is the capital city of Brazil, designed by Oscar Niemeyer and established in 1960.
hint: It is a planned city built inland in the 1950s to replace the old coastal capital.
whyA: Rio de Janeiro was the capital until 1960 and is still Brazil's most famous city.
whyC: Sao Paulo is Brazil's largest city, not its capital.
whyD: Salvador was Brazil's first colonial capital, not the present one.
explanationTl: Brasilia ang capital ng Brazil. Planned city ito na ginawang capital noong 1960, kapalit ng Rio de Janeiro.
hintTl: Planned city ito sa loob ng bansa na pumalit sa dating capital sa baybayin.

text: Who was the first president of the Philippines?
explanation: Emilio Aguinaldo was the first President of the Philippines, heading the First Philippine (Malolos) Republic inaugurated in January 1899.
hint: He led the revolutionary government that declared independence in Kawit, Cavite.
whyA: Rizal was a reformist writer executed in 1896; he never held office.
whyC: Quezon was the first President of the Commonwealth (1935), not the first President.
whyD: Marcos became President only in 1965.
explanationTl: Si Emilio Aguinaldo ang first President ng Pilipinas, head ng First Philippine (Malolos) Republic na na-inaugurate noong January 1899.
hintTl: Siya ang nag-declare ng independence sa Kawit, Cavite.

text: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system by both mass and diameter.
hint: It has the Great Red Spot.
whyA: Earth is the largest rocky planet but far smaller than the gas giants.
whyB: Mars is smaller than Earth.
whyD: Saturn is the second-largest planet.
explanationTl: Jupiter ang pinakamalaking planet sa solar system, sa mass man o sa diameter.
hintTl: Ito ang may Great Red Spot.

text: Which gas is most abundant in Earth’s atmosphere?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere by volume; oxygen is about 21%.
hint: It is not the gas we need to breathe, even though it is the one we inhale the most.
whyA: Oxygen is only about 21% of the atmosphere, second to nitrogen.
whyC: Carbon dioxide is only a tiny fraction (about 0.04%) of the atmosphere.
whyD: Argon is less than 1% of the atmosphere.
explanationTl: Mga 78% ng atmosphere ay nitrogen, habang ang oxygen ay mga 21% lang.
hintTl: Hindi ito ang gas na kailangan natin sa paghinga, pero ito ang pinakamarami sa hangin.

text: What is the national flower of the Philippines?
explanation: The sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) was proclaimed the national flower in 1934 by Governor-General Frank Murphy; it symbolizes purity and simplicity.
hint: Its small white blooms are strung into garlands sold outside churches.
whyA: Orchids such as the waling-waling are prized Philippine flowers, but the official national flower is the sampaguita.
whyC: The rose is not native and has no official status in the Philippines.
whyD: The sunflower has no official status in the Philippines.
explanationTl: Sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) ang national flower natin, idineklara noong 1934 ni Governor-General Frank Murphy. Simbolo ito ng purity at simplicity.
hintTl: Yung maliit na puting bulaklak na ginagawang kwintas at binebenta sa labas ng simbahan.

text: Which country hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics?
explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France, where Carlos Yulo won two gold medals for the Philippines.
hint: Think of where Carlos Yulo won his two gold medals.
whyB: Japan hosted the 2020 Games (held in 2021 in Tokyo).
whyC: Brazil hosted the 2016 Games in Rio de Janeiro.
whyD: Australia is set to host the 2032 Games in Brisbane.
explanationTl: Sa Paris, France ginanap ang 2024 Summer Olympics, kung saan nanalo si Carlos Yulo ng dalawang gold para sa Pilipinas.
hintTl: Saan nanalo ng dalawang gold si Carlos Yulo?

text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
explanation: Gold’s symbol is Au, from the Latin "aurum."
hint: The symbol comes from the Latin name of the metal, not the English one.
whyA: Ag is silver (Latin "argentum").
whyC: Fe is iron (Latin "ferrum").
whyD: Cu is copper (Latin "cuprum").
explanationTl: Ang symbol ng gold ay Au, galing sa Latin na "aurum."
hintTl: Galing ang symbol sa Latin name ng metal, hindi sa English.

text: Which ocean is the largest in the world?
explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of Earth’s surface.
hint: It is the ocean on the eastern side of the Philippines.
whyA: The Atlantic is the second-largest ocean, about half the size of the Pacific.
whyB: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean.
whyD: The Arctic is the smallest and shallowest of the major oceans.
explanationTl: Pacific Ocean ang pinakamalaki at pinakamalalim na ocean, halos one-third ng surface ng Earth. Ito rin ang ocean sa silangan ng Pilipinas.
hintTl: Ito yung ocean na nasa silangang side ng Pilipinas.

text: Who wrote the novel 'Noli Me Tangere'?
explanation: Jose Rizal wrote 'Noli Me Tangere,' a novel exposing Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.

text: What is the longest river in the world?
explanation: The Nile River, flowing through northeastern Africa, is considered the longest river globally at about 6,650 km.

text: Which element is essential for human respiration?
explanation: Oxygen is essential for human respiration, used in cellular processes to produce energy.

text: What is the currency of Japan?
explanation: The Yen is the official currency of Japan.
hint: Its symbol is written with a Y and two bars (the same sign is used by China's currency).
whyA: The yuan is the currency of China.
whyC: The won is the currency of South Korea (and North Korea).
whyD: The ringgit is the currency of Malaysia.
explanationTl: Yen ang currency ng Japan.
hintTl: Y na may dalawang guhit ang symbol nito.

text: Which mountain is the highest in the world?
explanation: Mount Everest, on the Nepal-China border in the Himalayas, is the highest mountain above sea level at about 8,849 meters.
hint: It is named after a British surveyor and sits on the Nepal-China border.
whyA: K2 is the second-highest mountain, about 240 m lower than Everest.
whyB: Kangchenjunga is the third-highest mountain.
whyD: Lhotse is the fourth-highest and is right next to Everest, which is why it gets confused with it.
explanationTl: Mount Everest ang pinakamataas na bundok sa mundo, mga 8,849 meters above sea level. Nasa Himalayas ito, sa border ng Nepal at China.
hintTl: Ipinangalan ito sa isang British surveyor, at nasa border ng Nepal at China.

text: Which scientist developed the theory of relativity?
explanation: Albert Einstein developed the special theory of relativity (1905) and the general theory of relativity (1915), which changed how science understands space, time and gravity.
hint: His famous equation is E = mc².
whyA: Isaac Newton gave the laws of motion and universal gravitation, which relativity later refined.
whyC: Galileo pioneered experiments and the telescope, centuries before relativity.
whyD: Niels Bohr is known for his model of the atom and quantum theory, not relativity.
explanationTl: Si Albert Einstein ang nag-develop ng theory of relativity, yung special relativity noong 1905 at general relativity noong 1915. Binago nito ang pagkaintindi natin sa space, time at gravity.
hintTl: Siya yung may sikat na equation na E = mc².

text: Which bird was declared the national bird of the Philippines in 1995?
explanation: Proclamation No. 615 (1995) declared the Philippine Eagle (Pithecophaga jefferyi) the national bird, replacing the maya.
hint: It is one of the largest eagles in the world and is critically endangered.
whyA: The maya was the earlier national bird, replaced in 1995.
whyC: The Philippine Cockatoo is an endangered native bird but not the national bird.
whyD: The Rufous Hornbill is a native bird but not the national bird.
explanationTl: Sa Proclamation No. 615 noong 1995, idineklarang national bird ang Philippine Eagle, at pinalitan nito ang maya.
hintTl: Isa ito sa pinakamalaking agila sa mundo at critically endangered.

text: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
explanation: Japan is called the 'Land of the Rising Sun' due to its eastern location where the sun rises.

text: What is the primary source of energy for Earth's climate system?
explanation: Solar radiation from the Sun supplies almost all the energy that drives Earth's climate, including winds, ocean currents and the water cycle.
hint: It is also the source of daylight.
whyA: Geothermal heat is real but far too small to drive the climate.
whyC: Heat from Earth's core adds only a tiny fraction of surface energy.
whyD: Tides come from the Moon's gravity and do not power the climate.
explanationTl: Ang solar radiation galing sa Sun ang nagbibigay ng halos lahat ng energy na nagpapatakbo ng climate, kasama ang hangin, ocean currents at water cycle.
hintTl: Ito rin ang source ng liwanag sa araw.

text: Which is the largest continent by land area?
explanation: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 30% of Earth's land area. The Philippines is part of Asia.
hint: It is the continent where the Philippines is located.
whyA: Africa is the second-largest continent.
whyC: North America is the third-largest continent.
whyD: Europe is one of the smallest continents, larger only than Australia.
explanationTl: Ang Asia ang pinakamalaking continent, mga 30% ng lupa sa mundo. Kasama ang Pilipinas dito.
hintTl: Ito ang continent kung nasaan ang Pilipinas.

text: What is the boiling point of water at sea level?
explanation: Water boils at 100°C at sea level under standard atmospheric pressure.
hint: The Celsius scale was set so that water freezes at 0 and boils at a round number.
whyA: 50 °C is only hot water; it is half the boiling point.
whyC: 150 °C is above boiling; water at sea level cannot get that hot as a liquid in an open pot.
whyD: 200 °C is a typical oven temperature, not the boiling point of water.
explanationTl: Sa sea level, kumukulo ang tubig sa 100 °C. Sa matataas na lugar, mas mababa ang pressure kaya mas mababa rin ang boiling point.
hintTl: Sa Celsius scale, 0 ang freezing ng tubig at round number ang boiling.

text: February 25 is commemorated in the Philippines as the anniversary of which event?
explanation: February 25 marks the 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution, which ended the Marcos regime and installed Corazon Aquino as President.
hint: Think of 1986 and a peaceful uprising along a highway in Metro Manila.
whyB: Independence was proclaimed in Kawit on June 12, 1898.
whyC: Bataan fell on April 9, 1942, now Araw ng Kagitingan.
whyD: The Cry of Pugad Lawin happened in August 1896.
explanationTl: Ang February 25 ay anniversary ng 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution, na nagpatalsik sa Marcos regime at naglagay kay Corazon Aquino bilang President.
hintTl: Isipin mo ang 1986 at ang mapayapang pag-aalsa sa isang highway sa Metro Manila.

text: What is the smallest country in the world by land area?
explanation: Vatican City, an independent city-state enclaved within Rome, is the smallest country in the world, with an area of only about 0.44 square kilometers (44 hectares).
hint: It is the home of the Pope.
whyA: Monaco is the second-smallest country, larger than Vatican City.
whyC: San Marino is small but much larger than Vatican City.
whyD: Liechtenstein is many times larger than Vatican City.
explanationTl: Ang Vatican City, na nasa loob ng Rome, ang pinakamaliit na bansa sa mundo, mga 0.44 square kilometers (44 hectares) lang.
hintTl: Dito nakatira ang Pope.

text: Who discovered penicillin?
explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928, leading to modern antibiotics.
hint: He was a Scottish scientist who noticed mold killing bacteria in a petri dish.
whyB: Marie Curie is known for research on radioactivity (radium and polonium).
whyC: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization and early vaccines, not penicillin.
whyD: Jonas Salk developed the polio vaccine.
explanationTl: Si Alexander Fleming ang naka-discover ng penicillin noong 1928, at ito ang naging simula ng modern antibiotics.
hintTl: Scottish scientist siya na nakapansin na pinapatay ng amag ang bacteria sa petri dish.

text: What is the capital of Australia?
explanation: Canberra is the capital city of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
hint: The capital is a planned city built because two rival big cities could not agree which should be capital.
whyA: Sydney is Australia's largest city, not its capital.
whyB: Melbourne was the temporary seat of government (1901-1927) but is not the capital.
whyD: Brisbane is the capital of Queensland state, not of Australia.
explanationTl: Canberra ang capital ng Australia. Planned city ito na pinili bilang compromise sa pagitan ng Sydney at Melbourne.
hintTl: Hindi ito yung pinakamalaking city; ginawa ito bilang compromise ng dalawang malaking city.

text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
explanation: Mars is called the Red Planet due to its reddish appearance from iron oxide (rust).
hint: Think of the planet whose soil is full of rust.
whyA: Venus looks bright yellowish-white because of its thick clouds.
whyC: Jupiter is the largest planet and is known for its Great Red Spot, not as the Red Planet.
whyD: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun and looks grey.
explanationTl: Mars ang tinatawag na Red Planet kasi mapula ang itsura niya dahil sa iron oxide (kalawang) sa lupa niya.
hintTl: Isipin ang planetang puno ng kalawang ang lupa.

text: What is the national fruit of the Philippines?
explanation: The mango is the national fruit of the Philippines, known for its sweet varieties.

text: Which year did the Philippines gain independence from the United States?
explanation: The United States recognized Philippine independence on July 4, 1946 through the Treaty of Manila; June 12, 1898 was the declaration of independence from Spain.
hint: It happened the year after World War II ended.
whyB: 1898 is when independence from Spain was declared in Kawit, Cavite, not when the U.S. granted independence.
whyC: 1935 is when the Commonwealth was inaugurated, a transition period before independence.
whyD: 1965 has no link to independence; it is the year Ferdinand Marcos was first elected president.
explanationTl: Noong July 4, 1946, kinilala ng United States ang independence ng Pilipinas sa Treaty of Manila. Yung 1898 naman ay declaration of independence mula sa Spain.
hintTl: Nangyari ito isang taon pagkatapos ng World War II.

text: What is the chemical formula for water?
explanation: The chemical formula for water is H2O, representing two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
hint: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
whyA: CO2 is carbon dioxide, the gas we breathe out.
whyC: O2 is oxygen gas, not water.
whyD: N2 is nitrogen gas, the main gas in air.
explanationTl: H2O ang chemical formula ng tubig: dalawang hydrogen atoms at isang oxygen atom.
hintTl: Hydrogen at oxygen ang laman ng tubig.

text: Which country is known for the Great Wall?
explanation: The Great Wall of China is a historic fortification built to protect Chinese states.

text: Counting both hot and cold deserts, which is the largest desert in the world?
explanation: A desert is defined by very low precipitation, not heat. By that measure the Antarctic Desert (about 14 million sq km) is the largest; the Sahara is the largest hot desert.
hint: A desert is about lack of rain, not about high temperature.
whyA: The Sahara is the largest HOT desert, but it is smaller than the Antarctic.
whyB: The Gobi is a large cold desert in Asia, far smaller than the Antarctic.
whyD: The Kalahari in southern Africa is much smaller.
explanationTl: Ang desert ay base sa sobrang konting ulan, hindi sa init. Kaya ang Antarctic Desert (mga 14 million sq km) ang pinakamalaki; ang Sahara ang pinakamalaking hot desert.
hintTl: Ang desert ay tungkol sa kakulangan ng ulan, hindi sa init.

text: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa, a famous Renaissance artwork.
hint: He was an Italian Renaissance artist and inventor who also painted 'The Last Supper'.
whyA: Van Gogh was a 19th-century Dutch painter known for 'The Starry Night'.
whyC: Picasso was a 20th-century Spanish painter known for Cubism and 'Guernica'.
whyD: Michelangelo was a Renaissance artist too, but he is known for the Sistine Chapel ceiling and the statue of David.
explanationTl: Si Leonardo da Vinci ang nagpinta ng Mona Lisa, isang sikat na Renaissance painting. Si Michelangelo naman ang sa Sistine Chapel, kaya madalas silang napagpapalit.
hintTl: Siya rin ang nagpinta ng 'The Last Supper'.

text: What is the currency of the United Kingdom?
explanation: The Pound Sterling is the official currency of the United Kingdom.
hint: The UK kept its own currency and never adopted the currency of the eurozone.
whyA: The UK never adopted the euro, even while it was an EU member.
whyC: The dollar is used by the US, Canada, Australia and others, not the UK.
whyD: The yen is the currency of Japan.
explanationTl: Pound Sterling ang official currency ng United Kingdom. Hindi sila nag-adopt ng euro kahit noong member pa sila ng EU.
hintTl: Hindi nag-euro ang UK, may sarili silang pera.

text: Which inert gas is most commonly used to fill incandescent light bulbs to prevent the filament from oxidizing?
explanation: Argon is the gas most commonly used to fill incandescent bulbs because it is inert, cheap and plentiful (about 1% of air), so it keeps the hot tungsten filament from reacting with oxygen.
hint: It is the most abundant noble gas in Earth's air.
whyA: Helium is inert but conducts heat away too fast and is not the usual bulb fill.
whyC: Neon is known for glowing signs, not for filling ordinary incandescent bulbs.
whyD: Hydrogen is not inert; it is flammable and is not used as a bulb fill.
explanationTl: Argon ang karaniwang nilalagay sa incandescent bulb kasi inert ito, mura at marami sa hangin (mga 1%), kaya hindi nag-o-oxidize ang filament.
hintTl: Ito ang pinakamaraming noble gas sa hangin natin.

text: What is the capital of France?
explanation: Paris is the capital of France, home of the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.
hint: It hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics.
whyA: Lyon is a major city known for its cuisine, not the capital.
whyB: Marseille is France's main port city, not the capital.
whyD: Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera.
explanationTl: Ang Paris ang capital ng France, kung nasaan ang Eiffel Tower at ang Louvre.
hintTl: Dito ginanap ang 2024 Summer Olympics.

text: Which Philippine hero is known as the 'Sublime Paralytic'?
explanation: Apolinario Mabini, despite being paralyzed, was a key intellectual in the Philippine Revolution.
hint: This hero lost the use of his legs to polio but became Aguinaldo's chief adviser.
whyA: Jose Rizal is the national hero, known for 'Noli Me Tangere' and 'El Filibusterismo'.
whyC: Andres Bonifacio is the 'Father of the Philippine Revolution' and founder of the Katipunan.
whyD: Emilio Aguinaldo was the first President of the Philippine Republic; Mabini was his adviser.
explanationTl: Si Apolinario Mabini ang 'Sublime Paralytic'. Naparalisa siya dahil sa polio, pero siya ang utak sa likod ng revolutionary government ni Aguinaldo, kaya tinawag din siyang 'Brains of the Revolution'.
hintTl: Naparalisa siya pero naging chief adviser ni Aguinaldo.

text: What is the smallest planet in our solar system?
explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union in 2006, so it is no longer counted as a planet.
hint: It is also the planet closest to the Sun.
whyA: Venus is nearly the size of Earth.
whyC: Mars is larger than Mercury; it is the second-smallest planet.
whyD: Pluto has been classified as a dwarf planet since 2006, not a planet.
explanationTl: Mercury ang pinakamaliit na planet. Ang Pluto ay dwarf planet na mula 2006 ayon sa International Astronomical Union, kaya hindi na siya counted na planet.
hintTl: Ito rin ang pinakamalapit sa Sun.

text: Which continent is known as the 'Dark Continent'?
explanation: Africa was historically called the 'Dark Continent' due to its unexplored interior.
hint: The nickname came from Europeans who knew little about this continent's interior.
whyA: Asia was well known to European traders and was never given this nickname.
whyC: South America is sometimes linked to the Amazon jungle, but it was not called the 'Dark Continent'.
whyD: Australia is sometimes called the 'Island Continent' or 'Land Down Under', not the 'Dark Continent'.
explanationTl: Africa ang tinawag na 'Dark Continent' noon kasi halos hindi pa na-e-explore ng mga Europeo ang loob nito, hindi dahil sa kulay ng mga tao.
hintTl: Galing ang nickname sa mga Europeo na halos walang alam sa loob ng kontinenteng ito.

text: What is the primary source of vitamin D for humans?
explanation: Sunlight triggers vitamin D synthesis in the skin, the primary source for most people.

text: Kapeng barako is a strong coffee traditionally associated with which Philippine province?
explanation: Kapeng barako, from the Liberica coffee species, is traditionally associated with Batangas, especially Lipa City.
hint: Think of the Southern Tagalog province also famous for lomi and balisong.
whyA: Benguet grows highland Arabica coffee, not the traditional barako.
whyC: Bukidnon is a Mindanao coffee producer, but barako is identified with a Southern Tagalog province.
whyD: Davao del Sur is known for Mount Apo Arabica, not barako.
explanationTl: Ang kapeng barako, na Liberica coffee, ay tradisyonal na kilala sa Batangas, lalo na sa Lipa City.
hintTl: Isipin ang probinsya sa Southern Tagalog na sikat din sa lomi at balisong.

text: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
explanation: The chemical symbol for iron is Fe, from its Latin name ferrum.
hint: The symbol comes from the Latin name, not the English one.
whyB: Ir is iridium.
whyC: In is indium.
whyD: Io is not a chemical symbol; it is a moon of Jupiter.
explanationTl: Fe ang chemical symbol ng iron, galing sa Latin name nitong ferrum.
hintTl: Galing sa Latin name ang symbol, hindi sa English.

text: Which Philippine city is known as the 'City of Pines'?
explanation: Baguio is called the 'City of Pines' because of its cool highland climate and the Benguet pine trees that cover its hills.
hint: It is the cool mountain city that also serves as the Summer Capital of the Philippines.
whyA: Davao is known as the home of the durian and Mount Apo, not pine forests.
whyC: Cebu is known as the 'Queen City of the South'.
whyD: Manila is the national capital, a lowland city without pine forests.
explanationTl: Baguio ang 'City of Pines' dahil malamig doon at puno ng pine trees ang mga bundok.
hintTl: Ito rin ang tinatawag na Summer Capital ng Pilipinas.

text: What is the capital of Canada?
explanation: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, housing the Parliament of Canada.
hint: It is not Canada's biggest city; it sits in the province of Ontario on the border with Quebec.
whyA: Toronto is Canada's largest city, but not its capital.
whyC: Vancouver is a major west-coast city in British Columbia, not the capital.
whyD: Montreal is the largest city in Quebec, not the national capital.
explanationTl: Ottawa ang capital ng Canada, dito nakatayo ang Parliament nila. Madalas mapagkamalan ang Toronto kasi yun ang pinakamalaking city.
hintTl: Hindi ito ang pinakamalaking city ng Canada.

text: Who invented the telephone?
explanation: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone in 1876.
hint: He received the first U.S. patent for the telephone in 1876.
whyA: Thomas Edison is known for the phonograph and a practical light bulb, not the telephone.
whyC: Nikola Tesla is known for alternating current (AC) systems.
whyD: Guglielmo Marconi is known for radio (wireless telegraphy).
explanationTl: Si Alexander Graham Bell ang kinikilalang imbentor ng telephone; nakuha niya ang patent noong 1876.
hintTl: Siya ang nakakuha ng unang U.S. patent para sa telephone noong 1876.

text: Which river flows through Egypt?
explanation: The Nile River flows through Egypt, vital for its agriculture and history.
hint: Ancient Egypt grew up along the banks of this river.
whyA: The Amazon flows through South America, mainly Brazil.
whyC: The Mississippi flows through the United States.
whyD: The Yangtze flows through China.
explanationTl: Ang Nile River ang dumadaloy sa Egypt. Dito umasa ang agriculture at kabihasnan ng sinaunang Egypt.
hintTl: Sa tabi ng ilog na ito umusbong ang sinaunang Egypt.

text: What is the national language of the Philippines?
explanation: Art. XIV, Sec. 6 of the 1987 Constitution states that the national language of the Philippines is Filipino, which is to be further developed and enriched on the basis of existing Philippine and other languages.
hint: The Constitution names a language that is still being developed from many Philippine languages, not just one regional language.
whyA: Tagalog is the main base of Filipino, but the Constitution names Filipino, not Tagalog, as the national language.
whyC: English is an official language (with Filipino) for communication and instruction under Art. XIV, Sec. 7, not the national language.
whyD: Cebuano is a major regional language, not the national language.
explanationTl: Ayon sa Art. XIV, Sec. 6 ng 1987 Constitution, Filipino ang national language natin. Base ito sa Tagalog pero dine-develop pa gamit ang ibang Philippine languages, kaya hindi 'Tagalog' ang tamang sagot.
hintTl: Hindi lang isang regional language ang pinangalanan ng Constitution, kundi isang language na patuloy na dine-develop.

text: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, orbiting at about 58 million kilometers.
hint: It is also the smallest planet and is named after the Roman messenger god.
whyA: Venus is the second planet from the Sun (and the hottest), not the closest.
whyC: Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
whyD: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun.
explanationTl: Mercury ang pinakamalapit na planet sa Sun, mga 58 million kilometers ang layo. Second ang Venus, third ang Earth.
hintTl: Ito rin ang pinakamaliit na planet.

text: What is the currency of Russia?
explanation: The ruble is the official currency of Russia.
hint: Its name starts with the letter R, like the country.
whyB: The euro is used by many European Union members, but Russia is not one of them.
whyC: The dollar is used by the United States and several other countries, not Russia.
whyD: The yen is the currency of Japan.
explanationTl: Ruble ang official currency ng Russia.
hintTl: Nagsisimula rin sa letrang R ang pangalan nito, gaya ng bansa.

text: Which gas is essential for photosynthesis?
explanation: In photosynthesis, plants use carbon dioxide and water, with energy from sunlight, to make glucose and release oxygen.
hint: Plants take in the gas that humans breathe out.
whyA: Oxygen is a product released by photosynthesis, not the gas taken in to make food.
whyC: Plants cannot use nitrogen gas from the air for photosynthesis.
whyD: Hydrogen gas is not taken in during photosynthesis; plants get hydrogen from water.
explanationTl: Sa photosynthesis, gumagamit ang halaman ng carbon dioxide at tubig, kasama ang sikat ng araw, para gumawa ng glucose. Oxygen ang inilalabas nito.
hintTl: Ito ang gas na inilalabas natin kapag humihinga tayo.

text: What is the largest mammal in the world?
explanation: The blue whale is the largest mammal, and the largest animal known to have ever lived, reaching about 30 meters (about 100 feet) in length.
hint: The biggest mammal does not live on land.
whyB: The elephant is the largest LAND animal, but it is far smaller than the blue whale.
whyC: The giraffe is the tallest animal, not the largest.
whyD: The rhinoceros is large but smaller than both the elephant and the blue whale.
explanationTl: Ang blue whale ang pinakamalaking mammal, at pinakamalaking hayop na nabuhay kailanman, umaabot ng mga 30 meters ang haba.
hintTl: Hindi sa lupa nakatira ang pinakamalaking mammal.

text: Which country is known for the Taj Mahal?
explanation: The Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in Agra, India.
hint: It is in the city of Agra, built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
whyB: Pakistan has Mughal monuments like the Badshahi Mosque, but not the Taj Mahal.
whyC: Bangladesh is a neighbor of India but the Taj Mahal is not there.
whyD: Nepal is known for Mount Everest and Himalayan temples, not the Taj Mahal.
explanationTl: Ang Taj Mahal ay nasa Agra, India. Pinagawa ito ni Mughal emperor Shah Jahan para sa asawa niya, at UNESCO World Heritage Site na ito.
hintTl: Nasa Agra ito, pinagawa ni Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.

text: What is the freezing point of water at sea level?
explanation: Water freezes at 0°C at sea level under standard atmospheric pressure.

text: Boracay Island, famous for its white sand beaches, is part of which province?
explanation: Boracay Island belongs to the municipality of Malay in the province of Aklan, Western Visayas, off the northwest tip of Panay.
hint: It is the Panay province also known for the Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo.
whyB: Antique is a neighbouring Panay province on the west coast, but Boracay is not part of it.
whyC: Capiz is another Panay province, known as the seafood capital, not Boracay's province.
whyD: Palawan is famous for El Nido and Coron beaches, not Boracay.
explanationTl: Ang Boracay ay nasa bayan ng Malay, sa probinsya ng Aklan, Western Visayas, sa northwest tip ng Panay.
hintTl: Ito yung probinsya sa Panay na sikat din sa Ati-Atihan festival sa Kalibo.

text: Who wrote 'On the Origin of Species' (1859), which presented the theory of evolution by natural selection?
explanation: Charles Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859, setting out the theory of evolution by natural selection. Alfred Russel Wallace independently reached a similar idea, but he did not write that book.
hint: This naturalist sailed on HMS Beagle and studied the Galapagos finches.
whyB: Gregor Mendel is known for the laws of heredity from pea plant experiments.
whyC: Alfred Wallace independently proposed natural selection but did not write 'On the Origin of Species'.
whyD: Louis Pasteur is known for germ theory and pasteurization.
explanationTl: Si Charles Darwin ang sumulat ng 'On the Origin of Species' noong 1859, kung saan niya inilatag ang theory of evolution by natural selection. Si Alfred Wallace ay may kaparehong idea, pero hindi siya ang sumulat ng librong iyon.
hintTl: Sumakay siya sa HMS Beagle at pinag-aralan ang mga finch sa Galapagos.

text: Which city is the capital of the Philippines?
explanation: Presidential Decree No. 940 (1976) restored Manila as the capital of the Philippines; Quezon City had held that status since 1948 under RA 333.
hint: It is the city where Malacañang Palace stands.
whyA: Quezon City was the capital from 1948 to 1976, but PD 940 restored Manila.
whyC: Makati is the main business district, not the capital.
whyD: Pasay hosts government offices such as the Senate but is not the capital.
explanationTl: Sa Presidential Decree No. 940 (1976), ibinalik ang Manila bilang capital ng Pilipinas; dati, Quezon City ang capital mula 1948 under RA 333.
hintTl: Dito nakatayo ang Malacañang Palace.

text: Which element is the second most abundant in the universe?
explanation: Helium is the second most abundant element in the universe, after hydrogen.
hint: The two lightest elements are also the two most abundant in the universe.
whyA: Hydrogen is the MOST abundant element, not the second.
whyC: Oxygen is the third most abundant in the universe and the most abundant in Earth's crust.
whyD: Carbon is common in living things but far less abundant than helium in the universe.
explanationTl: Helium ang second most abundant element sa universe, kasunod ng hydrogen na number one.
hintTl: Yung dalawang pinakamagaang element ay sila ring pinakamarami sa universe.

text: What is the national sport of the Philippines?
explanation: Republic Act No. 9850 (2009) declared Arnis the national martial art and sport of the Philippines.
hint: It is a Filipino martial art that uses sticks.
whyA: Basketball is the most popular sport but is not the legally declared national sport.
whyC: Volleyball is popular but has no national-sport status.
whyD: Boxing has produced Filipino champions but is not the national sport.
explanationTl: Ang Republic Act No. 9850 (2009) ang nag-declare na Arnis ang national martial art at sport ng Pilipinas.
hintTl: Filipino martial art ito na gumagamit ng stick.

text: Which country is the largest by land area?
explanation: Russia is the largest country by land area, covering about 17.1 million square kilometers.
hint: This country spans both Eastern Europe and northern Asia.
whyA: Canada is the second-largest country, about 10 million square kilometers.
whyC: China is about 9.6 million square kilometers, much smaller than the largest.
whyD: The United States is about 9.8 million square kilometers, also much smaller.
explanationTl: Russia ang pinakamalaking bansa, mga 17.1 million square kilometers, at sakop nito ang Eastern Europe at northern Asia. Pangalawa lang ang Canada.
hintTl: Sakop ng bansang ito ang Eastern Europe at northern Asia.

text: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
explanation: The chemical symbol for oxygen is O on the periodic table.

text: Which monument is a symbol of freedom in the United States?
explanation: The Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor, a gift from France dedicated in 1886, is a world-famous symbol of freedom and democracy.
hint: It is a giant statue of a woman holding a torch.
whyA: The Lincoln Memorial honors President Abraham Lincoln.
whyC: The Washington Monument honors George Washington, the first U.S. president.
whyD: Mount Rushmore is a mountain carving of four U.S. presidents' faces.
explanationTl: Ang Statue of Liberty sa New York ay regalo ng France na itinayo noong 1886. Kilala ito sa buong mundo bilang simbolo ng kalayaan.
hintTl: Malaking estatwa ito ng babaeng may hawak na sulo (torch).

text: What is the longest mountain range in the Philippines?
explanation: The Sierra Madre is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, running along the eastern side of Luzon from Cagayan down to Quezon province.
hint: It runs along Luzon’s Pacific coast and helps shield the island from typhoons.
whyA: The Cordillera Central is the highest range in northern Luzon but shorter than the Sierra Madre.
whyB: The Caraballo Mountains are a short range linking the Cordillera and the Sierra Madre.
whyC: The Zambales Mountains run along western Luzon and are much shorter.
explanationTl: Ang Sierra Madre ang pinakamahabang mountain range sa Pilipinas; dumadaan ito sa eastern side ng Luzon mula Cagayan hanggang Quezon.
hintTl: Nasa Pacific side ito ng Luzon at nakakatulong mag-shield laban sa bagyo.

text: Which festival in Kalibo, Aklan is known as the 'Mother of All Philippine Festivals'?
explanation: The Ati-Atihan of Kalibo, Aklan, held every January in honor of the Santo Nino, is known as the 'Mother of All Philippine Festivals'; festivals such as Sinulog and Dinagyang were patterned after it.
hint: Its name means 'to be like the Ati.'
whyA: Sinulog is Cebu City's Santo Nino festival, patterned after Ati-Atihan.
whyB: Panagbenga is Baguio City's flower festival.
whyD: Dinagyang is Iloilo City's festival, also patterned after Ati-Atihan.
explanationTl: Ang Ati-Atihan ng Kalibo, Aklan, tuwing January para sa Santo Nino, ang tinatawag na 'Mother of All Philippine Festivals'. Ginaya rito ang mga festival tulad ng Sinulog at Dinagyang.
hintTl: Ang ibig sabihin ng pangalan ay 'magpanggap na Ati.'

text: What is the capital of India?
explanation: New Delhi is the capital city of India, serving as the seat of government.

text: Who was the first man to walk on the moon?
explanation: Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during NASA's Apollo 11 mission.
hint: He was the commander of Apollo 11.
whyA: Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon second, after Armstrong.
whyC: Yuri Gagarin was the first human in space (1961) but never went to the Moon.
whyD: John Glenn was the first American to orbit Earth, not to walk on the Moon.
explanationTl: Si Neil Armstrong ang first na tao na naglakad sa Moon noong July 20, 1969, sa Apollo 11 mission.
hintTl: Siya ang commander ng Apollo 11.

text: Which gas gives soda its fizz?
explanation: Carbon Dioxide is dissolved in soda, creating bubbles and fizz.
hint: It is the same gas we breathe out and plants take in.
whyA: Nitrogen is used in some beers and coffee for a creamy foam, but soda's fizz comes from another gas.
whyC: Oxygen is not what is dissolved in soft drinks to make them fizz.
whyD: Helium is used in balloons, not drinks.
explanationTl: Carbon dioxide ang naka-dissolve sa soda under pressure. Pagbukas mo ng bote, lumalabas ito bilang bubbles, kaya may fizz.
hintTl: Ito yung gas na nilalabas natin pag huminga tayo.

text: What is the national tree of the Philippines?
explanation: The narra was declared the national tree by Proclamation No. 652 (1934). Its hard, durable wood stands for the strength of the Filipino.
hint: Its hard reddish wood is prized for furniture.
whyB: The coconut is the 'tree of life' but is not the national tree.
whyC: The mango (carabao mango) is the national fruit, not the tree.
whyD: The acacia is a common shade tree that came from abroad.
explanationTl: Ang narra ang idineklarang national tree sa Proclamation No. 652 (1934). Simbolo ng tibay ng Pilipino ang matigas at matibay niyang kahoy.
hintTl: Matigas at mapulang kahoy nito ang paborito sa muwebles.

text: Which country is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'?
explanation: Finland is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' due to its numerous lakes.
hint: This Nordic country's capital is Helsinki.
whyA: Sweden has many lakes too but is not known by this nickname.
whyC: Norway is known as the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'.
whyD: Canada has a great many lakes but is not called by this nickname.
explanationTl: Finland ang tinatawag na 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' dahil sa dami ng lawa nito.
hintTl: Helsinki ang capital ng Nordic country na ito.

text: What is the chemical symbol for silver?
explanation: The chemical symbol for silver is Ag, from its Latin name, argentum.
hint: The symbol comes from the Latin name argentum.
whyB: Au is gold (from aurum).
whyC: Si is silicon.
whyD: Sr is strontium.
explanationTl: Ag ang chemical symbol ng silver, galing sa Latin name nitong argentum.
hintTl: Galing sa Latin na argentum ang symbol.

text: Which ocean borders the eastern coast of the United States?
explanation: The Atlantic Ocean borders the eastern coast of the United States.
hint: This ocean lies between the Americas and Europe/Africa.
whyA: The Pacific borders the WEST coast of the United States.
whyC: The Indian Ocean lies between Africa, Asia and Australia.
whyD: The Arctic Ocean is at the North Pole, north of Alaska.
explanationTl: Atlantic Ocean ang nasa eastern coast ng United States. Pacific naman ang nasa west coast.
hintTl: Ito ang karagatan sa pagitan ng Americas at ng Europe/Africa.

text: Who composed the music of the Philippine national anthem?
explanation: Julian Felipe composed the music of the national anthem in 1898; the original Spanish lyrics came later from Jose Palma's poem 'Filipinas'.
hint: He was a composer from Cavite, commissioned by Aguinaldo.
whyA: Jose Palma wrote the original Spanish lyrics, not the music.
whyC: Claro M. Recto was a statesman and writer, not the anthem's composer.
whyD: Lope K. Santos was a writer and Tagalog grammarian.
explanationTl: Si Julian Felipe ang nag-compose ng music ng national anthem noong 1898; ang Spanish lyrics ay galing sa tula ni Jose Palma na 'Filipinas'.
hintTl: Composer siya galing Cavite, inutusan ni Aguinaldo.

text: What is the largest island in the Philippines?
explanation: Luzon is the largest island of the Philippines (about 109,000 sq km), followed by Mindanao.
hint: It is the island where Metro Manila is.
whyB: Mindanao is the second-largest island.
whyC: Samar is the third-largest island, much smaller than Luzon.
whyD: Palawan is long but far smaller than Luzon.
explanationTl: Ang Luzon ang pinakamalaking island sa Pilipinas (mga 109,000 sq km), sunod ang Mindanao.
hintTl: Dito nakalagay ang Metro Manila.

text: Which scientist proposed the heliocentric model of the solar system?
explanation: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed the heliocentric model, in which the Earth and planets revolve around the Sun, in his 1543 book 'On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres'.
hint: He was a Polish astronomer whose book came out in 1543.
whyA: Ptolemy taught the opposite: the geocentric (Earth-centered) model.
whyB: Galileo supported the heliocentric model with his telescope, but did not first propose it.
