hintTl: Isipin mo yung obscure na detalye, yung tago o malabo. Hanapin mo yung word na baligtad nun.

text: Complete the sentence: Her speech was so _______ that the audience was captivated.
explanation: Eloquent means fluent and persuasive in speech, fitting the context of captivating an audience.
hint: Which kind of speech would make people listen closely and not want it to end?
whyA: Monotonous means dull and in one flat tone; it would bore an audience, not captivate it.
whyC: Vague means unclear; an unclear speech loses listeners instead of holding them.
whyD: Abrupt means sudden or curt; it describes how a speech ends or its tone, not why it captivates.
explanationTl: Ang 'eloquent' ay magaling at malinaw magsalita, kaya na-captivate ang audience. Yung ibang choices (monotonous, vague, abrupt) ay negative, kaya hindi sila tugma sa 'captivated'.
hintTl: Anong klaseng speech ang gugustuhin mong pakinggan hanggang dulo?

text: Select the word that best completes the analogy: Big is to small as tall is to ______.
explanation: Big and small are opposites, so tall (a measure of height) has the opposite short.

text: Choose the word that means the opposite of 'frugal'.
explanation: Frugal means economical or avoiding waste, so its antonym is wasteful.
hint: A frugal person stretches every peso. Who does the reverse?
whyA: Thrifty is a synonym of frugal, not an antonym.
whyC: Cautious describes being careful; it is not the opposite of saving money.
whyD: Modest means simple or humble, which fits a frugal person rather than opposing one.
explanationTl: Ang frugal ay matipid, ayaw mag-aksaya. Kaya ang opposite niya ay wasteful, yung gastador o maaksaya.
hintTl: Ang frugal na tao ay pinapahaba ang bawat piso. Sino yung kabaligtaran nun?

text: Which word best fits in the blank? The novel’s plot was so _______ that readers couldn’t predict the ending.
explanation: Intricate means very complex and full of detail, which is why readers could not predict the ending.
hint: The clue is 'couldn't predict the ending'. What kind of plot is hard to predict?
whyB: A simple plot is easy to predict, the opposite of what the sentence describes.
whyC: A boring plot is dull, but dullness does not make an ending unpredictable.
whyD: A familiar plot follows patterns readers know, so it is easier to predict.
explanationTl: Ang intricate ay sobrang complex at maraming detalye, kaya hindi mahulaan ng readers ang ending.
hintTl: Ang clue ay 'couldn't predict the ending'. Anong klaseng plot ang mahirap hulaan?

passage: In 2019 the town of San Isidro started a simple rule: no segregation, no collection. Households had to separate biodegradable waste, recyclables and residual waste before the garbage truck would take them. At first many residents complained, and some left bags on vacant lots. The municipal office answered with weekly barangay assemblies, free compost bins, and a buy-back program for plastic bottles. Within two years the volume sent to the landfill fell by almost half, and the money saved on hauling was used to repair two health centers.
text: What is the passage mainly about?
optionB: How a town's segregation rule reduced landfill waste
optionC: The cost of repairing health centers
optionD: The history of landfills in the Philippines
explanation: Every sentence builds toward one point: a segregation rule, the town's response to complaints, and the result (landfill volume fell by almost half).
hint: The main idea must cover the WHOLE passage, from the first sentence to the last.
whyA: Complaints are mentioned once, as a stage the town went through — not the main point.
whyC: The health centers are only where the savings went, a detail at the end.
whyD: The passage is about one town since 2019, not landfill history.
explanationTl: Ang buong passage ay tungkol sa 'no segregation, no collection' na rule at ang naging resulta nito — nabawasan ng halos kalahati ang basura sa landfill.

passage: In 2019 the town of San Isidro started a simple rule: no segregation, no collection. Households had to separate biodegradable waste, recyclables and residual waste before the garbage truck would take them. At first many residents complained, and some left bags on vacant lots. The municipal office answered with weekly barangay assemblies, free compost bins, and a buy-back program for plastic bottles. Within two years the volume sent to the landfill fell by almost half, and the money saved on hauling was used to repair two health centers.
text: How did the municipal office respond to residents who resisted the rule?
optionA: It fined every household that complained.
optionC: It held assemblies and gave practical help such as compost bins.
optionD: It moved the landfill to another town.
explanation: The passage says the office 'answered with weekly barangay assemblies, free compost bins, and a buy-back program'.
hint: Find the sentence right after the complaints are mentioned.
whyA: Fines are never mentioned.
whyB: Collection continued — only unsegregated waste was refused.
whyD: Nothing in the passage says the landfill moved.
explanationTl: Sinabi mismo sa passage: nagkaroon ng weekly assemblies, libreng compost bins, at buy-back ng plastic bottles.

passage: In 2019 the town of San Isidro started a simple rule: no segregation, no collection. Households had to separate biodegradable waste, recyclables and residual waste before the garbage truck would take them. At first many residents complained, and some left bags on vacant lots. The municipal office answered with weekly barangay assemblies, free compost bins, and a buy-back program for plastic bottles. Within two years the volume sent to the landfill fell by almost half, and the money saved on hauling was used to repair two health centers.
text: Which statement can be inferred from the passage?
optionA: Hauling garbage to the landfill had been costing the town money.
optionB: All residents supported the rule from the start.
optionD: The rule was ordered by the national government.
explanation: Money was 'saved on hauling' once less waste went to the landfill, so hauling must have been a real cost before.
hint: An inference is not written directly, but the text must support it.
whyB: The passage says many residents complained at first.
whyC: The town ran a buy-back program for bottles — they were being recovered.
whyD: The passage says the town started the rule; nothing about the national government.
explanationTl: Kung may natipid sa hauling nang mabawasan ang basura, ibig sabihin may gastos talaga ang hauling dati.

passage: In 2019 the town of San Isidro started a simple rule: no segregation, no collection. Households had to separate biodegradable waste, recyclables and residual waste before the garbage truck would take them. At first many residents complained, and some left bags on vacant lots. The municipal office answered with weekly barangay assemblies, free compost bins, and a buy-back program for plastic bottles. Within two years the volume sent to the landfill fell by almost half, and the money saved on hauling was used to repair two health centers.
text: As used in the passage, the word 'residual' most nearly means:
explanation: Residual waste is what remains after biodegradables and recyclables are taken out — the leftover.
hint: It is the third group after two other kinds have been separated out.
whyA: Valuable items would be the recyclables, a separate group.
whyB: Nothing in the passage describes this waste as dangerous.
whyC: 'Fresh' has nothing to do with what remains after sorting.
explanationTl: Ang 'residual' ay ang natira — ang hindi nabubulok at hindi na ma-recycle.

passage: Many government offices now let citizens book appointments online. Supporters say this cuts the long lines that once started before dawn. Critics point out that not everyone has a smartphone or a stable connection, especially in rural areas, and that an online-only system can shut out the very people who most need public services. Several offices have therefore kept a small number of walk-in slots each day, and some barangay halls now lend a computer and a staff member to help residents book.
text: What is the author's attitude toward online appointment systems?
optionB: Balanced — seeing benefits and also the need for alternatives
explanation: The author gives the supporters' view, the critics' view, and then describes compromises (walk-in slots, assisted booking).
hint: Count the sides the author presents.
whyA: The author reports benefits too, like shorter lines.
whyC: The author spends half the passage on the problems.
whyD: The author describes solutions in detail, which shows interest.
explanationTl: Ipinakita ng author ang magkabilang panig at ang solusyon — balanced ang tono.

passage: Many government offices now let citizens book appointments online. Supporters say this cuts the long lines that once started before dawn. Critics point out that not everyone has a smartphone or a stable connection, especially in rural areas, and that an online-only system can shut out the very people who most need public services. Several offices have therefore kept a small number of walk-in slots each day, and some barangay halls now lend a computer and a staff member to help residents book.
text: According to the critics, who could be left out by an online-only system?
optionC: People without smartphones or stable internet
explanation: The critics say 'not everyone has a smartphone or a stable connection' and that such people could be shut out.
hint: Look for the sentence that starts with 'Critics'.
whyA: Employees are not mentioned as being shut out.
whyB: The early lines were the old problem that online booking tries to fix.
whyD: Barangay halls are part of the solution, not the people left out.
explanationTl: Ayon sa critics, maiiwan ang mga walang smartphone o maayos na internet, lalo na sa probinsya.

passage: Many government offices now let citizens book appointments online. Supporters say this cuts the long lines that once started before dawn. Critics point out that not everyone has a smartphone or a stable connection, especially in rural areas, and that an online-only system can shut out the very people who most need public services. Several offices have therefore kept a small number of walk-in slots each day, and some barangay halls now lend a computer and a staff member to help residents book.
text: The word 'therefore' in the last sentence shows that the walk-in slots are:
optionA: a response to the critics' concern
optionB: a reason to stop online booking
explanation: 'Therefore' signals a result: because some people could be shut out, offices kept walk-in slots.
hint: 'Therefore' = 'because of that'.
whyB: Online booking continues; walk-ins are added alongside it.
whyC: 'Therefore' links the sentence directly to what came before.
whyD: Supporters favour online booking; walk-ins answer the critics.
explanationTl: Ang 'therefore' ay nagpapakita ng resulta — dahil sa concern ng critics, nagtira ng walk-in slots.

passage: Coconut farmers in Quezon have watched yields drop after stronger typhoons and longer dry spells. Older trees, many planted more than sixty years ago, bear fewer nuts and break more easily in high winds. A cooperative in one town began replacing its oldest trees with a dwarf variety that fruits in about three years instead of six to eight, while planting coffee and cacao between the rows. The members say the mixed crops keep money coming in during the years the new coconuts are still too young to harvest.
text: Why did the cooperative plant coffee and cacao between the rows?
optionA: Coconut trees need shade from coffee plants.
optionB: To earn income while the young coconut trees are not yet bearing fruit
optionC: Because coffee is protected by law
explanation: The last sentence says the mixed crops 'keep money coming in during the years the new coconuts are still too young to harvest'.
hint: The reason is stated in the final sentence.
whyA: The passage does not say coconuts need shade.
whyC: No law is mentioned.
whyD: They are replanting coconuts, not abandoning them.
explanationTl: Para may kita habang hindi pa namumunga ang bagong niyog — nakasulat ito sa huling pangungusap.

passage: Coconut farmers in Quezon have watched yields drop after stronger typhoons and longer dry spells. Older trees, many planted more than sixty years ago, bear fewer nuts and break more easily in high winds. A cooperative in one town began replacing its oldest trees with a dwarf variety that fruits in about three years instead of six to eight, while planting coffee and cacao between the rows. The members say the mixed crops keep money coming in during the years the new coconuts are still too young to harvest.
text: Which is NOT given as a cause of lower coconut yields?
explanation: Typhoons, dry spells and old trees are all named. Market prices are never mentioned.
hint: Tick off each choice against the first two sentences.
whyA: Named in the first sentence.
whyB: Named in the first sentence.
whyC: The second sentence says old trees bear fewer nuts.
explanationTl: Ang presyo sa merkado ay hindi binanggit. Ang binanggit lang: bagyo, tagtuyot, at lumang puno.

text: Piliin ang tamang salita: Tumakbo siya ___ mabilis papunta sa paaralan.
explanation: Use 'nang' before an adverb that describes HOW an action is done (tumakbo nang mabilis).
hint: Is the word after the blank describing how he ran?
whyA: 'Ng' marks a noun object or possession (bumili ng tinapay), not manner.
whyC: 'Nag' is a verb prefix, not a separate word here.
whyD: 'Na' is a linker, but manner after a verb takes 'nang'.
explanationTl: 'Nang' ang ginagamit kapag inilalarawan kung PAANO ginawa ang kilos — tumakbo nang mabilis.

text: Piliin ang tamang salita: Bumili si Ana ___ bigas sa palengke.
explanation: 'Ng' introduces the object of the verb: bumili ng bigas.
hint: Bigas is the thing she bought.
whyB: 'Nang' is for manner, time or 'when' — not for an object.
whyC: 'Nina' is used before plural names of people.
whyD: 'Kay' is used before a person's name, not a thing.
explanationTl: 'Ng' ang ginagamit bago ang pangngalang layon ng pandiwa — bumili ng bigas.

text: Alin ang tama?
explanation: Use 'raw/rin' after a word ending in a vowel (or w/y), and 'daw/din' after a consonant. 'Pupunta' ends in a vowel → 'raw'.
hint: Look at the last letter of the word before raw/daw.
whyA: 'Aalis' ends in the consonant s, so it should be 'daw'.
whyB: 'Pupunta' ends in the vowel a, so it should be 'raw'.
whyD: 'Ikaw' ends in w, which counts like a vowel, so it should be 'rin'.
explanationTl: Kapag patinig (o w/y) ang dulo ng salita, 'raw/rin'. Kapag katinig, 'daw/din'. Pupunta → raw.

text: Ano ang kahulugan ng sawikaing 'bukas-palad'?
explanation: 'Bukas-palad' (open palm) describes someone generous.
hint: Picture an open hand that is ready to give.
whyB: Hardworking is 'masipag', not 'bukas-palad'.
whyC: Being generous does not mean being rich.
whyD: Talkative would be 'madaldal' or 'mabunganga'.
explanationTl: Ang 'bukas-palad' ay taong mapagbigay — bukas ang kamay sa pagtulong.

text: Ano ang kahulugan ng 'balat-sibuyas'?
explanation: Someone with 'onion skin' gets hurt easily — sensitive (maramdamin).
hint: Onion skin is very thin.
whyA: Brave is the opposite of easily hurt.
whyC: The idiom is about feelings, not skin colour.
whyD: Thrifty is 'matipid'; unrelated to the idiom.
explanationTl: Ang 'balat-sibuyas' ay taong madaling masaktan ang damdamin — maramdamin.

text: Ang 'nagbibilang ng poste' ay tumutukoy sa taong:
explanation: 'Counting lamp posts' is an idiom for someone without a job, wandering around with nothing to do.
hint: Why would someone have time to count posts?
whyB: It is an idiom, not about real counting skill.
whyC: Literal reading — idioms are figurative.
whyD: Someone with a job wouldn't be described this way.
explanationTl: Ang 'nagbibilang ng poste' ay taong walang trabaho — palakad-lakad lang.

text: Sa pamilyang Pilipino, sino ang tinatawag na 'ilaw ng tahanan'?
explanation: 'Ilaw ng tahanan' (light of the home) refers to the mother; 'haligi ng tahanan' (pillar) refers to the father.
hint: Light vs pillar — which parent is which?
whyA: The father is 'haligi ng tahanan'.
whyB: The eldest child has no standard idiom here.
whyD: The idiom refers to the mother of the household.
explanationTl: Ang ina ang 'ilaw ng tahanan'; ang ama ang 'haligi ng tahanan'.

text: Ano ang kasalungat ng 'maramot'?
explanation: 'Maramot' means stingy; its opposite is 'mapagbigay' (generous).
hint: Two of the choices mean the same as 'maramot'.
whyA: 'Madamot' is a synonym of maramot.
whyB: 'Kuripot' also means stingy — a synonym, not an antonym.
whyD: 'Masungit' means grumpy, not the opposite of stingy.
explanationTl: Ang 'maramot' ay kuripot o madamot. Ang kasalungat ay 'mapagbigay'.

text: Ano ang kasingkahulugan ng 'masikap'?
explanation: 'Masikap' means diligent or hardworking — the same as 'masipag'.
hint: Think of a student who never gives up studying.
whyA: 'Tamad' (lazy) is the opposite.
whyC: 'Mabagal' means slow, not hardworking.
whyD: 'Mayabang' means boastful.
explanationTl: Ang 'masikap' ay kapareho ng 'masipag' — hindi sumusuko sa trabaho.

text: Piliin ang tamang salita: Mag-aral ka ___ mabuti para pumasa sa exam.
explanation: 'Mabuti' describes how to study, so the manner marker 'nang' is used.
hint: Does 'mabuti' describe HOW you study?
whyA: 'Ng' marks an object, but 'mabuti' is manner.
whyB: 'Na' would not connect a verb to its manner here.
whyD: 'Ang' marks the subject.
explanationTl: Inilalarawan ng 'mabuti' kung PAANO mag-aral, kaya 'nang'.

text: Ano ang ibig sabihin ng 'itaga sa bato'?
explanation: 'Itaga sa bato' (carve it in stone) means the promise is firm and should be remembered.
hint: Something carved in stone lasts a very long time.
whyA: Literal reading of the words — the idiom is figurative.
whyC: Also literal; the idiom is about promises.
whyD: Anger is not the meaning.
explanationTl: Ang 'itaga sa bato' ay pangakong hindi magbabago — tandaan mo.

text: Ang 'butas ang bulsa' ay nangangahulugang:
explanation: A 'pocket with a hole' holds no money — the person is broke.
hint: What happens to coins in a pocket with a hole?
whyB: A literal reading; the idiom is about money.
whyC: Unrelated to the image.
whyD: The opposite of the meaning.
explanationTl: Ang 'butas ang bulsa' ay walang pera.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the term of office of the President is:
explanation: Article VII, Section 4: the President serves six years and is not eligible for any re-election.
hint: Six years, and only once.
whyA: That is the US-style term, not the Philippine one.
whyB: The President cannot be re-elected at all.
whyD: The term is six years, not five.
explanationTl: Art. VII, Sec. 4: anim na taon ang termino ng Presidente at hindi na pwedeng ma-reelect.

text: How many consecutive terms may a Senator serve under the 1987 Constitution?
explanation: Article VI, Section 4: Senators serve six-year terms and may not serve more than two consecutive terms.
hint: Senators: 6 years × 2.
whyB: They may be re-elected once.
whyC: Three consecutive terms is the limit for House members, not Senators.
whyD: The Constitution sets a limit.
explanationTl: Art. VI, Sec. 4: 6 taon kada termino, hindi hihigit sa dalawang magkasunod na termino.

text: Members of the House of Representatives serve a term of:
optionA: 6 years, no more than two consecutive terms
optionB: 4 years, no more than two consecutive terms
optionD: 3 years, no more than three consecutive terms
explanation: Article VI, Section 7: three years per term, and no more than three consecutive terms.
hint: House = 3 × 3.
whyA: That describes Senators.
whyB: Four-year terms do not exist for Congress here.
whyC: The term is three years and there is a limit.
explanationTl: Art. VI, Sec. 7: 3 taon kada termino, hanggang tatlong magkasunod na termino.

text: What is the minimum age to be elected President of the Philippines?
explanation: Article VII, Section 2: at least forty years old on the day of the election (plus natural-born, registered voter, able to read and write, 10 years' residency).
hint: It is older than the age for Senators.
whyA: 35 is the minimum age for a Senator.
whyC: 30 is too young under the Constitution.
whyD: 45 is not the constitutional minimum.
explanationTl: Art. VII, Sec. 2: dapat 40 taong gulang man lang sa araw ng eleksyon.

text: What is the minimum age to be a Senator?
explanation: Article VI, Section 3: at least thirty-five years old on election day.
hint: Between the House (25) and the President (40).
whyA: 25 is the minimum for House members.
whyB: 30 is not a constitutional minimum for any of these posts.
whyD: 40 is the minimum for President and Vice President.
explanationTl: Art. VI, Sec. 3: 35 taong gulang man lang ang Senador.

text: Which article of the 1987 Constitution contains the Bill of Rights?
explanation: The Bill of Rights is Article III.
hint: It comes right after the Declaration of Principles.
whyA: Article I is National Territory.
whyB: Article II is the Declaration of Principles and State Policies.
whyC: Article VI is the Legislative Department.
explanationTl: Ang Bill of Rights ay nasa Article III.

text: Which body has the exclusive power to INITIATE all cases of impeachment?
explanation: Article XI, Section 3: the House initiates; the Senate has the sole power to try and decide.
hint: One chamber accuses, the other judges.
whyB: The Senate tries and decides impeachment cases; it does not initiate them.
whyC: The Supreme Court Chief Justice presides only when the President is tried.
whyD: The Ombudsman can be impeached but does not initiate impeachment.
explanationTl: Art. XI, Sec. 3: ang House ang nagsisimula ng impeachment; ang Senado ang nagdedesisyon.

text: The three independent Constitutional Commissions are:
explanation: Article IX names the Civil Service Commission, the Commission on Elections and the Commission on Audit.
hint: Personnel, elections, and money.
whyA: CHR is created under Article XIII and NEDA is an executive agency.
whyC: CHR is not one of the three Article IX commissions.
whyD: DBM is an executive department.
explanationTl: Art. IX: Civil Service Commission, COMELEC, at Commission on Audit.

text: The Civil Service Commission is headed by a Chairman and how many Commissioners?
explanation: Article IX-B, Section 1: a Chairman and two Commissioners, each serving seven years without reappointment.
hint: Three people in total.
whyB: Four is not the number in Article IX-B.
whyC: COMELEC has six commissioners plus a Chairman; CSC is smaller.
whyD: There are two Commissioners.
explanationTl: Art. IX-B, Sec. 1: isang Chairman at dalawang Commissioner, 7 taon ang termino.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, martial law may initially be proclaimed for a period not exceeding:
explanation: Article VII, Section 18: not more than sixty days, unless Congress extends it.
hint: Two months.
whyA: Thirty days is too short; the limit is sixty.
whyB: Ninety days exceeds the constitutional limit.
whyD: Any extension needs Congress; the initial period is sixty days.
explanationTl: Art. VII, Sec. 18: hindi hihigit sa 60 araw, maliban kung i-extend ng Kongreso.

text: Justices of the Supreme Court must retire upon reaching the age of:
explanation: Article VIII, Section 11: Justices hold office until age seventy.
hint: A round number above 65.
whyA: 65 is the usual government retirement age, not the Justices'.
whyB: 60 is too early for Justices.
whyC: 75 is not in the Constitution.
explanationTl: Art. VIII, Sec. 11: magreretiro ang mga Justice sa edad na 70.

text: 'Public office is a public trust' is a principle found in the article on:
explanation: Article XI, Section 1 opens with 'Public office is a public trust.'
hint: The article is about holding officials responsible.
whyB: Article IV covers who is a Filipino citizen.
whyC: Article V covers the right to vote.
whyD: Article XII covers the economy and natural resources.
explanationTl: Art. XI (Accountability of Public Officers), Sec. 1: 'Public office is a public trust.'

text: What is the minimum voting age under the 1987 Constitution?
explanation: Article V, Section 1: Filipino citizens at least eighteen years old may vote.
hint: The age of majority.
whyA: 21 was the old age of majority, not the voting age.
whyB: 16 is too young to vote in national elections.
whyD: 17 is too young.
explanationTl: Art. V, Sec. 1: 18 taong gulang pataas ang pwedeng bumoto.

text: Under RA 6713, public officials must respond to letters and requests from the public within:
explanation: Section 5(a) of RA 6713 requires action on letters and requests within fifteen working days from receipt.
hint: Half a month of working days.
whyA: Thirty days is the period for other duties, such as divestment.
whyC: The law counts working days, and the number is fifteen.
whyD: Too short — Section 5(a) sets fifteen working days.
explanationTl: RA 6713, Sec. 5(a): kailangang aksyunan ang sulat o request sa loob ng 15 working days.

text: The Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) must be filed annually on or before:
explanation: RA 6713, Section 8: on or before April 30 of every year (and within 30 days after assuming office).
hint: Same month as the income tax deadline.
whyA: January 31 is not the SALN deadline.
whyB: June 30 is too late.
whyD: December 31 is the end of the period covered, not the filing deadline.
explanationTl: RA 6713, Sec. 8: ang SALN ay ifa-file bago o sa April 30 bawat taon.

text: Which of the following is NOT one of the norms of conduct under RA 6713?
explanation: The eight norms are: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living.
hint: Three of the choices are on the list of eight.
whyA: Political neutrality is one of the eight norms.
whyB: Simple living is one of the eight norms.
whyC: Responsiveness to the public is one of the eight norms.
explanationTl: Walo ang norms: public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, simple living. Wala ang 'seniority above merit'.

text: RA 6713 is formally known as the:
optionA: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
explanation: RA 6713 (1989) is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.
hint: Think 'conduct and ethics'.
whyB: That is RA 3019.
whyC: That is RA 9485, amended by RA 11032.
whyD: Civil service rules are in other laws and the Administrative Code.
explanationTl: Ang RA 6713 ay ang Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.

text: A government employee receives an expensive gift from a person with a pending application in her office. Under RA 6713 this is:
optionA: Allowed if she declares it in her SALN
optionB: Allowed if the gift is given after office hours
optionC: Prohibited, because it is in connection with her official duties
explanation: Section 7(d) prohibits soliciting or accepting gifts of monetary value in the course of official duties or from anyone whose transaction may be affected by the office.
hint: Ask: is the giver affected by her work?
whyA: Declaring it does not make accepting it legal.
whyB: Office hours do not matter — the link to her duties does.
whyD: A supervisor cannot waive the prohibition.
explanationTl: Bawal tumanggap ng regalo mula sa taong may transaksyon sa opisina mo (Sec. 7(d)).

text: Which law punishes acts such as causing undue injury to the government through manifest partiality or gross negligence?
explanation: RA 3019, the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, lists corrupt practices including causing undue injury (Section 3(e)).
hint: It's the anti-graft law.
whyA: RA 9003 is about solid waste.
whyC: RA 8749 is the Clean Air Act.
whyD: RA 9262 is the Anti-VAWC law.
explanationTl: RA 3019 ang Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.

text: RA 11032, which amended the Anti-Red Tape Act, is also known as the:
optionA: Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act
explanation: RA 11032 (2018) is the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act.
hint: It's about faster, simpler government transactions.
whyB: RA 11032 is about faster government transactions, not access to information.
whyC: The Data Privacy Act is RA 10173.
whyD: The Safe Spaces Act is RA 11313.
explanationTl: RA 11032 ang Ease of Doing Business Act — pinalakas nito ang Anti-Red Tape Act.

text: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly on:
explanation: The UDHR was adopted on December 10, 1948 — now celebrated as Human Rights Day.
hint: It is Human Rights Day.
whyB: June 12, 1898 is Philippine Independence Day.
whyC: October 24, 1945 is when the UN Charter took effect (UN Day).
whyD: February 25, 1986 is the end of the EDSA People Power Revolution.
explanationTl: Ang UDHR ay inaprubahan noong December 10, 1948 — Human Rights Day.

text: The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) was created by:
explanation: Article XIII, Section 17 of the 1987 Constitution created the independent Commission on Human Rights.
hint: It came after the EDSA revolution.
whyA: The 1935 Constitution had no CHR.
whyC: RA 6713 is the code of conduct for public officials.
whyD: The CHR is a Philippine constitutional body.
explanationTl: Art. XIII, Sec. 17 ng 1987 Constitution ang lumikha sa CHR.

text: 'No person shall be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law' is found in:
explanation: This due process clause is the first section of the Bill of Rights (Article III, Section 1).
hint: It is the very first right listed in the Bill of Rights.
whyA: The Preamble states purposes, not specific rights.
whyB: Article II lists state principles and policies.
whyC: Article VII is the Executive Department.
explanationTl: Ito ang due process clause — Art. III, Sec. 1 ng Bill of Rights.

text: RA 9262 protects:
optionC: Women and their children against violence
explanation: RA 9262 is the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004.
hint: Known as the Anti-VAWC law.
whyA: Senior citizens are covered by RA 9994.
whyB: Indigenous peoples are covered by RA 8371 (IPRA).
whyD: Overseas workers are covered by RA 8042 and its amendments.
explanationTl: RA 9262 = Anti-VAWC: proteksyon sa kababaihan at kanilang mga anak laban sa karahasan.

text: Which of these is a right of a person under custodial investigation?
optionA: To remain silent and to have competent, independent counsel
optionC: To refuse to be photographed in public
optionD: To be released after 24 hours in all cases
explanation: Article III, Section 12 guarantees the right to remain silent and to competent and independent counsel, preferably of one's own choice.
hint: Think of the 'Miranda' rights.
whyB: No such right exists.
whyC: Not a right listed for custodial investigation.
whyD: No automatic release rule like this is in the Constitution.
explanationTl: Art. III, Sec. 12: karapatang manahimik at magkaroon ng abogado.

text: RA 11313, the Safe Spaces Act, penalizes:
optionB: Gender-based sexual harassment in streets, public places, online and workplaces
explanation: RA 11313 (2019), the 'Bawal Bastos' law, covers gender-based sexual harassment in public spaces, online, workplaces and schools.
hint: Also called the 'Bawal Bastos' law.
whyA: Logging is covered by forestry laws.
whyC: Vote buying is an election offense under the Omnibus Election Code.
whyD: Smoking is covered by other laws and ordinances.
explanationTl: Ang RA 11313 ('Bawal Bastos' law) ay laban sa gender-based sexual harassment sa kalye, online at trabaho.

text: RA 9003 is the:
explanation: RA 9003 (2000) is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act — segregation at source, materials recovery facilities, and closing open dumps.
hint: It is the law about garbage.
whyA: The Clean Air Act is RA 8749.
whyB: The Clean Water Act is RA 9275.
whyC: The Climate Change Act is RA 9729.
explanationTl: RA 9003 ang Ecological Solid Waste Management Act — tungkol sa basura at segregation.

text: Which law is the Philippine Clean Air Act?
explanation: RA 8749 (1999) is the Philippine Clean Air Act.
hint: The oldest of these environmental laws.
whyB: RA 9275 is the Clean Water Act.
whyC: RA 9003 is about solid waste.
whyD: RA 10121 is the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act.
explanationTl: RA 8749 ang Clean Air Act (1999).

text: RA 9275 aims to protect the country's:
explanation: RA 9275 (2004) is the Philippine Clean Water Act.
hint: Clean ___ Act, 2004.
whyA: Forests are covered by forestry laws.
whyB: Air is covered by RA 8749.
whyD: Wildlife is covered by RA 9147.
explanationTl: RA 9275 = Clean Water Act — proteksyon sa mga katubigan.

text: Under RA 9003, waste should first be segregated:
optionB: at the source, such as households
optionC: by the garbage truck crew only
explanation: RA 9003 requires segregation at source — the household, school or business that produces the waste.
hint: Where is the waste produced?
whyA: By then it is too late to sort efficiently; the law requires sorting at source.
whyC: Collectors may refuse unsegregated waste — sorting is the producer's job.
whyD: The law applies nationwide.
explanationTl: Segregation at source — sa bahay pa lang, hinihiwalay na ang basura.

text: Which law created the Climate Change Commission?
explanation: RA 9729, the Climate Change Act of 2009, created the Climate Change Commission.
hint: The Climate Change Act, 2009.
whyB: RA 8749 is the Clean Air Act.
whyC: RA 9147 is the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act.
whyD: RA 6713 is the code of conduct for public officials.
explanationTl: RA 9729 (Climate Change Act of 2009) ang lumikha sa Climate Change Commission.

text: Which agency is primarily responsible for the conservation and management of the country's environment and natural resources?
explanation: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) is the lead agency.
hint: Look for 'Environment' in the name.
whyA: DOH handles health.
whyB: DPWH handles public works and highways.
whyC: DA handles agriculture.
explanationTl: DENR — Department of Environment and Natural Resources.

text: Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the State shall protect the right of the people to:
explanation: 'The State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.'
hint: It is the constitutional basis of environmental protection.
whyA: Not in the Constitution.
whyC: Not a constitutional right in the Philippines.
whyD: Free tertiary education comes from a law (RA 10931), not Art. II, Sec. 16.
explanationTl: Art. II, Sec. 16: karapatan ng tao sa 'balanced and healthful ecology'.

text: In 2024, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) and the DICT rolled out the Digital National ID. Aside from the national ID website, through which government mobile application can registered PhilSys holders access it?
explanation: As of November 2026, the Digital National ID can be accessed through the national ID website or the eGovPH app, according to PSA advisories and reports from June to August 2024 on the PSA-DICT rollout.
hint: Think of the single 'super app' that bundles many government services.
whyB: The LTMS portal is the LTO's system for licenses and vehicle registration. It does not issue the national ID.
whyC: The PhilHealth portal handles health insurance membership, not PhilSys identity credentials.
whyD: The DFA system is only for booking passport appointments.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, makukuha ang Digital National ID sa national ID website o sa eGovPH app. Ito ang ni-roll out ng PSA at DICT noong 2024, ayon sa PSA advisories at news reports noong June hanggang August 2024.
hintTl: Isipin mo yung isang 'super app' na pinagsama-sama ang maraming government services.

text: PhilHealth launched YAKAP (Yaman ng Kalusugan Program) on July 25, 2025 as its revitalized primary care benefit package. It is an evolution of which earlier PhilHealth package?
explanation: As of November 2026, PhilHealth describes YAKAP, launched July 25, 2025, as an evolution of the Konsulta (Konsultasyong Sulit at Tama) primary care package, now with more medicines, laboratory tests and cancer screening (PhilHealth news release, July 2025).
hint: The older package's name sounds like a doctor's check-up.
whyA: The Z Benefits Package covers catastrophic illnesses like cancer treatment. It is not a primary care package.
whyC: Malasakit Centers are one-stop shops for medical assistance in hospitals. They are not a PhilHealth primary care package.
whyD: The Point-of-Service program enrolls unregistered patients at the point of care. It is not the predecessor of YAKAP.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ayon sa PhilHealth news release noong July 2025, ang YAKAP (inilunsad July 25, 2025) ay evolution ng Konsulta package. Mas marami na itong libreng gamot, lab tests at cancer screening.
hintTl: Yung dating pangalan, parang pagpapa-check-up sa doktor.

text: The Department of Health's Zero Balance Billing policy, declared nationwide after the July 28, 2025 State of the Nation Address, means patients pay no hospital bill for which of the following?
optionA: Private rooms in any government or private hospital
optionB: All admissions in PhilHealth-accredited private hospitals
optionD: Outpatient consultations in LGU rural health units only
explanation: As of November 2026, Zero Balance Billing covers patients admitted to basic or ward accommodation in DOH-run hospitals. It was soft-launched in May 2025 and made nationwide after the July 28, 2025 SONA (PTV News, July 31, 2025).
hint: It is limited to the hospitals the DOH itself operates, and not the fancier rooms.
whyA: Private rooms are excluded. Only basic or ward accommodation is covered.
whyB: Private hospitals still charge fees. The policy applies to DOH-run hospitals.
whyD: The policy is about hospital admissions in DOH hospitals, not LGU outpatient consultations.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sakop ng Zero Balance Billing ang mga pasyenteng naka-admit sa basic o ward accommodation sa DOH-run hospitals. Na-soft launch ito noong May 2025 at naging nationwide pagkatapos ng SONA noong July 28, 2025 (PTV News, July 31, 2025).
hintTl: Sa mga ospital lang ng DOH mismo, at hindi yung mga mamahaling kwarto.

text: The DOH opened the first BUCAS center in Sto. Tomas, Pampanga in March 2024 to provide urgent and outpatient care without hospital admission. What does BUCAS stand for?
optionA: Barangay Urgent Care and Ambulance Service
optionB: Bagong Universal Clinic and Ambulatory Support
optionC: Bayanihan Urgent Care and Assistance Service
optionD: Bagong Urgent Care and Ambulatory Service
explanation: As of November 2026, BUCAS stands for Bagong Urgent Care and Ambulatory Service. The first center opened on March 6, 2024 at Jose B. Lingad Memorial General Hospital in Sto. Tomas, Pampanga (GMA News, March 6, 2024).
hint: The acronym starts with the 'Bagong' of the administration's slogan and ends with outpatient-type service.
whyA: BUCAS centers are DOH facilities, not barangay ambulance services.
whyB: The 'U' stands for Urgent, not Universal, and the 'S' is Service, not Support.
whyC: The 'B' stands for Bagong, not Bayanihan.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang BUCAS ay Bagong Urgent Care and Ambulatory Service. Binuksan ang unang center noong March 6, 2024 sa Jose B. Lingad Memorial General Hospital, Sto. Tomas, Pampanga (GMA News).
hintTl: Nagsisimula sa 'Bagong' at tungkol sa outpatient o 'ambulatory' na serbisyo.

text: Under DepEd Order No. 10, s. 2024, the MATATAG Curriculum began its phased implementation in School Year 2024-2025 in which grade levels?
explanation: As of November 2026, DepEd's MATATAG Curriculum FAQ and DO 10, s. 2024 (July 2024) state that implementation started in SY 2024-2025 for Kindergarten and Grades 1, 4 and 7. Grades 2, 5 and 8 followed in SY 2025-2026.
hint: The rollout started at the first year of each key stage.
whyB: Grades 2 and 3 come later in the phasing (SY 2025-2026 and SY 2026-2027).
whyC: MATATAG is a revised K to 10 curriculum. Grade 11 is senior high school and is not part of it.
whyD: Only Grade 4 started in SY 2024-2025. Grades 5 and 6 come in later years.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ayon sa DepEd MATATAG FAQ at DO 10, s. 2024 (July 2024), nagsimula ang MATATAG noong SY 2024-2025 sa Kinder, Grade 1, Grade 4 at Grade 7. Sumunod ang Grades 2, 5 at 8 noong SY 2025-2026.
hintTl: Sinimulan sa unang baitang ng bawat key stage.

text: MULA (Multispectral Unit for Land Assessment), the Philippines' biggest satellite yet at about 130 kilograms, is being built by the Philippine Space Agency together with a satellite company from which country?
explanation: As of November 2026, MULA is being built by PhilSA with Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd (SSTL) of the United Kingdom and was undergoing space environment testing in the UK. PhilSA eyed a possible April 2027 launch (SSTL news, 2025; Manila Bulletin, August 29, 2026).
hint: The partner company is named after an English county.
whyA: Japanese universities helped build the earlier Diwata microsatellites, not MULA.
whyC: The US company SpaceX is only the planned launch provider, not the co-builder.
whyD: South Korea is not MULA's development partner.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, binubuo ng PhilSA ang MULA kasama ang Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd (SSTL) ng United Kingdom. Nasa space environment testing pa ito sa UK, at April 2027 ang tinitingnang launch (SSTL news, 2025; Manila Bulletin, August 29, 2026).
hintTl: Ang partner company ay ipinangalan sa isang county sa England.

text: What is the theme of the Philippines' 2026 ASEAN Chairmanship, launched on November 14, 2025?
explanation: As of November 2026, the Philippines' ASEAN 2026 theme is 'Navigating Our Future, Together', unveiled at the chairship launch on November 14, 2025 (Philstar and Manila Bulletin, November 2025).
hint: The theme is a seafaring image that fits an archipelago.
whyA: This was Lao PDR's theme for its 2024 chairmanship.
whyB: This was Indonesia's theme for its 2023 chairmanship.
whyD: This was Malaysia's theme for its 2025 chairmanship.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang theme ng ASEAN 2026 chairship ng Pilipinas ay 'Navigating Our Future, Together'. Inilabas ito sa launch noong November 14, 2025 (Philstar at Manila Bulletin, November 2025).
hintTl: Parang paglalayag o pag-navigate sa dagat, bagay sa isang archipelago.

text: The 48th ASEAN Summit, the first leaders' summit under the Philippines' 2026 chairship, was held on May 8, 2026 in which city?
explanation: As of November 2026, the 48th ASEAN Summit was held in Cebu on May 8, 2026, according to the Chair's Statement published on asean.org (May 9, 2026). The 49th Summit followed in Metro Manila in November 2026.
hint: It is the Queen City of the South.
whyA: Davao City did not host the 48th Summit.
whyB: Iloilo City did not host the 48th Summit.
whyC: Baguio City did not host the 48th Summit.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ginanap ang 48th ASEAN Summit sa Cebu noong May 8, 2026, ayon sa Chair's Statement sa asean.org. Sumunod ang 49th Summit sa Metro Manila noong November 2026.
hintTl: Ito yung tinatawag na Queen City of the South.

text: Which country takes over the ASEAN Chairmanship from the Philippines for 2027?
explanation: As of November 2026, Singapore takes over the ASEAN chair from the Philippines for 2027, as PM Lawrence Wong confirmed after meeting President Marcos on July 15, 2026 (The Star and Inquirer, July 2026).
hint: ASEAN rotates the chair alphabetically, and this country comes right after 'Philippines'.
whyB: Thailand comes after Singapore in the alphabetical rotation.
whyC: Myanmar deferred its turn. That is why the Philippines took the 2026 chair.
whyD: Malaysia was the 2025 chair, the year before the Philippines.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, Singapore ang papalit sa Pilipinas bilang ASEAN chair sa 2027. Kinumpirma ito ni PM Lawrence Wong matapos ang meeting nila ni President Marcos noong July 15, 2026 (The Star, Inquirer).
hintTl: Alphabetical ang rotation ng ASEAN chair. Sino ang kasunod ng 'Philippines'?

text: At the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur on October 26, 2025, which country was formally admitted as ASEAN's 11th member state?
explanation: As of November 2026, Timor-Leste is ASEAN's 11th member. It was formally admitted on October 26, 2025 at the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur, the bloc's first expansion since Cambodia in 1999 (The ASEAN Magazine; The Star, October 26, 2025).
hint: It applied in 2011 and had been an ASEAN observer since 2022.
whyA: Papua New Guinea is an ASEAN observer, not a member.
whyC: Bangladesh is in South Asia and is not an ASEAN member.
whyD: Sri Lanka is in South Asia and is not an ASEAN member.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang Timor-Leste ang 11th member ng ASEAN. Pormal itong tinanggap noong October 26, 2025 sa 47th ASEAN Summit sa Kuala Lumpur, ang unang expansion mula Cambodia noong 1999 (The ASEAN Magazine; The Star).
hintTl: Nag-apply ito noong 2011 at naging observer noong 2022.

text: On July 8, 2024, the Philippines signed a Reciprocal Access Agreement (RAA) in Manila that allows each country's forces to enter the other's territory for joint military exercises. With which country was it signed?
explanation: As of November 2026, the Philippines-Japan Reciprocal Access Agreement was signed in Manila on July 8, 2024 by Defense Secretary Teodoro and Japanese Foreign Minister Kamikawa (Inquirer and ABS-CBN, July 8, 2024).
hint: This country's Foreign Minister came to Malacanang to sign it, and it was the country's third such deal after the UK and Australia.
whyA: The Philippines' troop-access pact with the US is the 1998 Visiting Forces Agreement, not an RAA.
whyB: Australia's pact with the Philippines is the 2007 Status of Visiting Forces Agreement.
whyD: France did not sign an RAA with the Philippines on that date.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, pinirmahan ang Philippines-Japan Reciprocal Access Agreement sa Manila noong July 8, 2024 nina Defense Secretary Teodoro at Japanese Foreign Minister Kamikawa (Inquirer, ABS-CBN).
hintTl: Pangatlong ganitong kasunduan ito ng bansang ito, kasunod ng UK at Australia.

text: On November 14, 2026, during the 28th ASEAN Economic Community Council Meeting in Manila, ASEAN member states signed the bloc's first standalone, legally binding agreement setting common rules on digital trade, cross-border data flows and electronic payments. What is it?
explanation: As of November 2026, ASEAN signed the Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) in Manila on November 14, 2026. It replaces the 2019 ASEAN e-commerce agreement (The Star, November 14, 2026; Vera Files).
hint: Its name covers the whole digital economy, not just online selling.
whyA: RCEP is a free trade agreement signed in 2020 with ASEAN's partners such as China, Japan and Korea.
whyB: The ASEAN Agreement on Electronic Commerce dates from 2019. DEFA is set to replace it.
whyC: ATIGA covers trade in goods and dates from 2009.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, pinirmahan ng ASEAN ang Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) sa Manila noong November 14, 2026. Papalitan nito ang 2019 ASEAN e-commerce agreement (The Star; Vera Files).
hintTl: Buong digital economy ang sakop ng pangalan, hindi lang online selling.

text: On December 9, 2024, PHIVOLCS raised Alert Level 3 after an explosive summit eruption sent a plume about 3,000 meters high, prompting evacuations within a 6-kilometer radius. Which volcano erupted?
explanation: As of November 2026, PHIVOLCS records that Kanlaon Volcano on Negros Island erupted at 3:03 p.m. on December 9, 2024, and its alert was raised from Level 2 to Level 3 (PHIVOLCS eruption update, December 10, 2024; Philstar).
hint: It straddles Negros Occidental and Negros Oriental.
whyB: Taal is in Batangas and was not raised to Alert Level 3 on that date.
whyC: Mayon in Albay was not the volcano that erupted on December 9, 2024.
whyD: Bulusan in Sorsogon was not raised to Alert Level 3 on that date.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ayon sa PHIVOLCS, pumutok ang Kanlaon Volcano sa Negros Island noong 3:03 p.m., December 9, 2024. Itinaas ang alert mula Level 2 papuntang Level 3 (PHIVOLCS update, December 10, 2024; Philstar).
hintTl: Nasa pagitan ito ng Negros Occidental at Negros Oriental.

text: PHIVOLCS identified which newly named fault as the source of the magnitude 6.9 earthquake that struck offshore northern Cebu on September 30, 2025, the strongest recorded in the province?
explanation: As of November 2026, PHIVOLCS confirmed in early October 2025 that the newly identified Bogo Bay Fault, a right-lateral strike-slip fault, generated the September 30, 2025 M6.9 offshore northern Cebu quake (PHIVOLCS earthquake poster; Manila Bulletin, October 3, 2025).
hint: The fault is named after the city closest to the epicenter.
whyA: PHIVOLCS did not name the Philippine Fault Zone as the source. It traced the quake to a newly identified local offshore fault.
whyC: The Manila Trench lies west of Luzon, far from Cebu.
whyD: The West Valley Fault is in Metro Manila and nearby provinces.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, kinumpirma ng PHIVOLCS noong early October 2025 na ang bagong tukoy na Bogo Bay Fault ang pinagmulan ng M6.9 na lindol sa northern Cebu noong September 30, 2025 (PHIVOLCS poster; Manila Bulletin, October 3, 2025).
hintTl: Ipinangalan ito sa city na pinakamalapit sa epicenter.

text: The magnitude 7.4 earthquake offshore Manay, Davao Oriental on October 10, 2025, which prompted a tsunami warning for eastern coastal provinces, originated along which structure according to PHIVOLCS?
explanation: As of November 2026, PHIVOLCS Director Teresito Bacolcol said on October 10, 2025 that the M7.4 offshore Davao Oriental quake originated along the Philippine Trench, east of Mindanao (SunStar, October 10, 2025; PHIVOLCS primer).
hint: It is the deep trench off the Pacific side of the country.
whyA: The Cotabato Trench lies off western Mindanao, on the opposite side from Davao Oriental.
whyB: The Manila Trench lies west of Luzon.
whyD: The West Valley Fault is an onland fault in Metro Manila, not off Mindanao.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sinabi ni PHIVOLCS Director Bacolcol noong October 10, 2025 na sa Philippine Trench nanggaling ang M7.4 na lindol offshore Davao Oriental (SunStar; PHIVOLCS primer).
hintTl: Yung malalim na trench sa Pacific side ng bansa.

text: In July 2024, the Philippines was selected from eight country offers to host the Board of which international climate fund?
optionD: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
explanation: As of November 2026, the Philippines hosts the Board of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage. It was selected on July 9, 2024 at the Board's meeting in Songdo, Korea, through a DENR-led inter-agency bid (UNFCCC and DFA releases, July 2024).
hint: The fund pays for climate impacts that adaptation can no longer prevent.
whyA: The Green Climate Fund is hosted in Songdo, South Korea, not the Philippines.
whyB: The Adaptation Fund is a separate older fund and was not part of this selection.
whyC: The GEF is based in Washington, D.C. and was not part of this selection.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, Pilipinas ang host ng Board ng Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage. Napili ito noong July 9, 2024 sa Board meeting sa Songdo, Korea, sa bid na pinangunahan ng DENR (UNFCCC at DFA, July 2024).
hintTl: Para sa pinsalang dulot ng climate change na hindi na kayang i-adapt.

text: The Philippines hosted the 2024 Asia-Pacific Ministerial Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction (APMCDRR) at the PICC in October 2024 in partnership with which United Nations office?
optionA: UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)
optionC: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Secretariat
explanation: As of November 2026, the 2024 APMCDRR (October 14-18, 2024, PICC) was hosted by the Philippines in partnership with UNDRR. It is the region's main platform for carrying out the Sendai Framework (UNDRR APMCDRR 2024 site; Daily Tribune, October 17, 2024).
hint: The UN office whose mandate matches the conference's own name.
whyB: UNEP handles environmental matters broadly and was not the conference partner.
whyC: The UNFCCC Secretariat runs the climate COPs, not the APMCDRR.
whyD: UNDP supports development work but was not the co-organizer.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang 2024 APMCDRR (October 14-18, 2024 sa PICC) ay hinost ng Pilipinas kasama ang UNDRR. Ito ang main platform sa region para sa Sendai Framework (UNDRR site; Daily Tribune).
hintTl: Yung UN office na kapareho ng pangalan ng conference.

text: Republic Act No. 12079, signed in December 2024, amended the National Internal Revenue Code to give a VAT refund on goods bought in the Philippines to which group?
optionA: Overseas Filipino workers on home vacation
optionB: Non-resident foreign tourists who take the goods out of the country
optionC: Senior citizens and persons with disabilities
optionD: Registered export enterprises in economic zones
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12079 (December 2024) adds Section 112-A to the NIRC: non-resident foreign passport holders get a VAT refund on goods bought in person at accredited stores (at least P3,000 per receipt) and taken out of the country within 60 days. The Department of Finance runs it through VAT refund operators.
hint: The law was meant to make the Philippines more attractive as a shopping destination.
whyA: OFWs are Filipinos, not the non-resident foreign passport holders the law covers.
whyC: Seniors and PWDs already have VAT exemptions under their own laws (RA 9994, RA 10754); RA 12079 is about tourists.
whyD: Export enterprises have their own zero-rating rules under CREATE; this law is a refund for shoppers, not businesses.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12079 (December 2024) ay nagdagdag ng Section 112-A sa NIRC: ang mga non-resident foreign tourist ay pwedeng mag-claim ng VAT refund sa goods na binili nila sa accredited stores (minimum P3,000 per receipt) basta mailabas nila ng bansa within 60 days. Ang Department of Finance ang nagpapatakbo nito kasama ang VAT refund operators.
hintTl: Ginawa ang batas para maging mas attractive ang Pilipinas bilang shopping destination.

text: In February 2025, the Philippines was removed from the 'grey list' of jurisdictions under increased monitoring, after being listed since June 2021. Which international body maintains this list?
optionB: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
explanation: As of November 2026, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) removed the Philippines from its grey list at its February 21, 2025 plenary in Paris. The Anti-Money Laundering Council welcomed the decision (Inquirer; Philstar, February 2025).
hint: It is the global watchdog on money laundering and terrorist financing.
whyA: The IMF lends to countries and monitors their economies. It does not keep the AML grey list.
whyB: The OECD keeps tax-cooperation lists, not the FATF grey list.
whyD: The World Bank finances development and does not keep the grey list.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, inalis ng Financial Action Task Force (FATF) ang Pilipinas sa grey list noong February 21, 2025 sa plenary sa Paris. Natuwa rito ang Anti-Money Laundering Council (Inquirer; Philstar).
hintTl: Global watchdog ito laban sa money laundering at terrorist financing.

text: Under Batas Pambansa Blg. 72, how did the results of the 2024 Census of Population (POPCEN) conducted by the PSA become official for all purposes?
optionA: By approval of Congress through a joint resolution
optionB: By certification of the Commission on Elections
optionC: By publication of the results on the PSA website
explanation: As of November 2026, the 2024 POPCEN count of 112,729,484 Filipinos (as of July 1, 2024) became official through Proclamation No. 973, signed July 11, 2025, as BP 72 requires (Lawphil text of Proclamation No. 973; Inquirer, July 2025).
hint: It takes the signature of the Chief Executive.
whyA: Congress does not approve census results. BP 72 requires executive action.
whyB: COMELEC uses census data but does not make it official.
whyC: The PSA releases the counts, but they are official only after the President's proclamation.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, naging official ang 2024 POPCEN count na 112,729,484 (as of July 1, 2024) sa pamamagitan ng Proclamation No. 973 na pinirmahan noong July 11, 2025, ayon sa BP 72 (Lawphil; Inquirer).
hintTl: Kailangan ng pirma ng Chief Executive.

text: The BSP unveiled the P500, P100 and P50 notes of the First Philippine Polymer Banknote Series in December 2024, each featuring native wildlife. Which animal appears on the P500 polymer note?
explanation: As of November 2026, the P500 polymer note shows the Visayan spotted deer, the P100 the Palawan peacock-pheasant and the P50 the Visayan leopard cat. The BSP unveiled them on December 19, 2024 and released them on December 23, 2024 (GMA News; Philstar).
hint: It is a hoofed mammal found in Panay and Negros.
whyA: The Philippine eagle is on the P1,000 polymer note introduced in 2022.
whyC: The Palawan peacock-pheasant is on the P100 polymer note.
whyD: The Visayan leopard cat is on the P50 polymer note.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, Visayan spotted deer ang nasa P500 polymer note, Palawan peacock-pheasant sa P100, at Visayan leopard cat sa P50. Inilabas ng BSP noong December 19, 2024 at umikot na noong December 23, 2024 (GMA News; Philstar).
hintTl: Hayop na may kuko (hoofed), makikita sa Panay at Negros.

text: At the Paris 2024 Olympics, Carlos Yulo became the first Filipino to win two Olympic gold medals. In which events did he win them?
optionB: Men's pommel horse and still rings
optionC: Men's parallel bars and horizontal bar
optionD: Men's individual all-around and floor exercise
explanation: As of November 2026, Yulo won the men's floor exercise on August 3, 2024 and the vault on August 4, 2024 at Paris 2024, the Philippines' first double Olympic gold (Philstar, August 5, 2024; ABS-CBN).
hint: One event uses the whole mat, and the other has a run and a springboard.
whyB: Yulo did not medal on pommel horse or rings in Paris.
whyC: Yulo did not medal on parallel bars or the horizontal bar in Paris.
whyD: Yulo did not win the all-around. His second gold was in vault.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, nanalo si Yulo ng gold sa men's floor exercise (August 3, 2024) at vault (August 4, 2024) sa Paris 2024, ang kauna-unahang double Olympic gold ng Pilipinas (Philstar; ABS-CBN).
hintTl: Yung isa, buong mat ang gamit. Yung isa, may takbo at springboard.

text: Besides Carlos Yulo's two golds, the Philippines won two bronze medals in boxing at the Paris 2024 Olympics, its best-ever Olympic haul. Who won them?
explanation: As of November 2026, Aira Villegas (women's 50 kg) and Nesthy Petecio (women's 57 kg) each won bronze at Paris 2024, giving the Philippines 2 golds and 2 bronzes, its best Olympic finish (GMA News; Philstar, August 2024).
hint: Both medalists were women, and one of them had already won silver in Tokyo.
whyA: Marcial and Paalam both competed in Paris but did not medal.
whyB: Bacyadan competed in Paris but did not win a medal. Only Petecio in this pair medaled.
whyD: Villegas medaled, but Marcial did not.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sina Aira Villegas (women's 50 kg) at Nesthy Petecio (women's 57 kg) ang nag-bronze sa Paris 2024. Kaya 2 gold at 2 bronze ang Pilipinas, ang best Olympic finish natin (GMA News; Philstar).
hintTl: Parehong babae, at yung isa may silver na noong Tokyo.

text: In August 2026, Alex Eala came from a set down to beat top seed Jessica Pegula, 4-6, 6-4, 6-0, and win her first-ever WTA 500 singles title. Which tournament did she win?
explanation: As of November 2026, Eala won the Mubadala DC Open in Washington in early August 2026, her first WTA 500 title, which the WTA called her first WTA Tour title (Philstar, August 4, 2026; GMA News).
hint: The tournament is in the US capital.
whyA: At the 2025 Miami Open, Eala lost to Pegula in the semifinals.
whyB: Her 2025 Guadalajara title was a lower-tier WTA 125 event, not a WTA 500.
whyC: Her Birmingham title was also a WTA 125 event, not a WTA 500.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, napanalunan ni Eala ang Mubadala DC Open sa Washington noong early August 2026. Ito ang first WTA 500 title niya, na tinawag ng WTA na first WTA Tour title niya (Philstar, August 4, 2026; GMA News).
hintTl: Nasa capital ng US ang tournament na ito.

text: Which Lav Diaz film, starring Gael Garcia Bernal and premiered in the Cannes Premiere section in May 2025, was chosen as the Philippines' official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards?
explanation: As of November 2026, the Film Academy of the Philippines picked 'Magellan' as the country's entry to the 98th Oscars in early September 2025, after its world premiere at Cannes on May 18, 2025 (Manila Bulletin and GMA News, September 2025).
hint: The film is about the Portuguese explorer who died in Mactan in 1521.
whyA: 'Green Bones' was considered, but it is not a Lav Diaz film and was not chosen.
whyB: 'Hello, Love, Again' was considered but not chosen, and it is not a Lav Diaz film.
whyD: 'Sunshine' was considered but not chosen, and it is not a Lav Diaz film.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, 'Magellan' ang pinili ng Film Academy of the Philippines na entry sa 98th Oscars noong early September 2025, matapos ang world premiere nito sa Cannes noong May 18, 2025 (Manila Bulletin; GMA News).
hintTl: Tungkol sa Portuguese explorer na namatay sa Mactan noong 1521.

text: Republic Act No. 12009, the New Government Procurement Act signed on July 20, 2024, expressly repealed which earlier law?
optionA: RA 6713, the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
optionB: RA 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act
optionC: RA 11032, the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act
optionD: RA 9485, the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act, signed July 20, 2024) is the procurement law; its repealing clause (Sec. 115) expressly repeals RA 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act of 2003.
hint: Think of the law the new act was written to replace, the one that used to govern bidding.
whyA: RA 6713 is the ethics code for public servants; it was not repealed by the procurement law.
whyC: RA 11032 covers red tape and processing time in government transactions, not procurement, and it remains in force.
whyD: RA 9485 was already amended by RA 11032 in 2018; it was never the procurement law.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act, pinirmahan noong July 20, 2024) na ang batas sa government procurement. Sa Sec. 115 nito, ni-repeal nito ang RA 9184 o Government Procurement Reform Act.
hintTl: Isipin mo kung anong lumang batas ang dating sinusunod sa bidding ng gobyerno.

text: Which law signed in November 2024 declares the Philippines' internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial sea, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone, and continental shelf in line with UNCLOS?
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12064, the Philippine Maritime Zones Act signed on November 8, 2024, defines the country's maritime zones (e.g., 12-nautical-mile territorial sea, 24-nautical-mile contiguous zone, EEZ, continental shelf) consistent with UNCLOS.
hint: The answer's name literally describes the areas being declared.
whyA: The Archipelagic Sea Lanes Act (RA 12065), signed the same day, designates routes for foreign ships and aircraft; it does not declare the maritime zones.
whyB: The Baselines Law is an earlier law that draws the baselines from which zones are measured; it is not the 2024 law that declares the zones.
whyD: The Fisheries Code governs fisheries and aquatic resources; it does not declare maritime zones.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12064 o Philippine Maritime Zones Act (pinirmahan November 8, 2024) ang nagde-declare ng maritime zones natin, gaya ng territorial sea, contiguous zone, EEZ at continental shelf, ayon sa UNCLOS.
hintTl: Yung pangalan mismo ng batas, sinasabi na kung ano ang dine-declare.

text: How many archipelagic sea lanes, with corresponding air routes, are designated by the Philippine Archipelagic Sea Lanes Act (RA 12065) of 2024?
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12065 (signed November 8, 2024) designates three archipelagic sea lanes and their air routes through Philippine archipelagic waters for foreign ships and aircraft, per reports on the signing (Inquirer, Philstar).
hint: The lanes cut across the archipelago roughly north to south; count fewer than four.
whyB: Two is too few; the law names three lanes.
whyC: Four is more than what the law designates.
whyD: Five is more than what the law designates.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12065 (pinirmahan November 8, 2024) ay nag-designate ng tatlong archipelagic sea lanes kasama ang air routes nito para sa foreign ships at aircraft.
hintTl: Mas kaunti sa apat ang sea lanes na itinakda ng batas.

text: Under the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA) of 2024, a person who knowingly lets his or her bank or e-wallet account be used to receive and transfer proceeds of scams is punished as a:
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12010 (AFASA, signed July 20, 2024), Sec. 4(a), penalizes as a money mule anyone who uses, lends, buys, rents, or sells a financial account to receive, transfer, or withdraw proceeds of crimes or scams.
hint: The term compares the person to an animal that carries loads for others.
whyA: A social engineering scheme is obtaining confidential information through deception (Sec. 4(b)), not lending one's account.
whyB: A mass mailer is a tool that sends messages to 50 or more recipients; it is a circumstance that makes the offense economic sabotage, not the name of the offender.
whyC: Account takeover means getting into someone else's account; lending your own account is a different act.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 12010 o AFASA (pinirmahan July 20, 2024), Sec. 4(a), money mule ang tawag sa nagpapagamit, nagpapahiram, bumibili o nagbebenta ng account para tumanggap o maglipat ng pera galing sa scam.
hintTl: Hayop na tagabuhat ng karga ng iba ang pinagkunan ng term.

text: Republic Act No. 12023, signed on October 2, 2024, subjects digital services supplied by nonresident digital service providers (such as streaming platforms) and consumed in the Philippines to:
optionA: A 5% percentage tax on gross receipts
optionD: A 10% excise tax on digital content
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12023 (signed October 2, 2024) amended the Tax Code so that digital services, whether by resident or nonresident providers, are subject to 12% VAT; nonresident providers must register with the BIR (implemented by RR No. 3-2025).
hint: It is the same consumption tax already on most goods and services in the country.
whyA: The law did not create a percentage tax; it brought digital services under VAT.
whyC: No separate digital services tax was created; the law used the existing VAT system.
whyD: Excise taxes apply to specific goods like alcohol and tobacco, not to digital services under this law.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, dahil sa RA 12023 (pinirmahan October 2, 2024), ang digital services ng foreign providers na ginagamit dito sa Pilipinas ay may 12% VAT na, at kailangan nilang mag-register sa BIR.
hintTl: Parehong tax na nakapatong na sa karamihan ng binibili natin.

text: Republic Act No. 12021, signed on September 23, 2024 to protect the rights and welfare of domestic and overseas Filipino seafarers, is known as the:
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12021 (signed September 23, 2024) is the Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers, covering seafarers' rights, welfare, grievance system, and reintegration; MARINA issued its IRR.
hint: Its title borrows the name of a famous 13th-century English charter of rights.
whyB: No law with this title was enacted; it is an invented name.
whyC: This sounds plausible but is not the official short title of RA 12021.
whyD: The law covers both domestic and overseas seafarers, and this is not its title.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12021 (pinirmahan September 23, 2024) ay ang Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers, para sa karapatan at welfare ng mga Pinoy seafarer, local man o abroad.
hintTl: Hiniram ang pangalan sa sikat na charter ng England noong 1215.

text: Under the Expanded Centenarians Act of 2024 (RA 11982), Filipinos receive a P10,000 cash gift upon reaching which ages?
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 11982 (signed February 26, 2024) amended the Centenarians Act of 2016 to give P10,000 at ages 80, 85, 90, and 95, while keeping the P100,000 gift at age 100.
hint: It starts at octogenarians and goes every five years until just before 100.
whyA: These ages are not covered; the law starts at 80.
whyB: The intervals are every five years, not ten, and 70 is not included.
whyD: The law starts at 80, and 99 is not one of the milestone ages.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 11982 (pinirmahan February 26, 2024), may P10,000 cash gift pagdating ng 80, 85, 90 at 95 years old, at P100,000 pa rin pag umabot ng 100.
hintTl: Nagsisimula sa 80, tapos every five years.

text: Under the No Permit, No Exam Prohibition Act (RA 11984), a student's status as 'disadvantaged' must be certified by:
optionA: The school registrar or guidance counselor
optionB: The barangay captain where the student resides
optionC: The DepEd schools division superintendent or CHED regional director
optionD: The local social welfare and development officer or the DSWD regional office
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 11984 (approved March 11, 2024), Sec. 4, requires certification by a municipal, city, or provincial social welfare and development officer or the DSWD regional office before covered schools must let the student take exams despite unpaid fees.
hint: The certifier is the office that assesses families in crisis, not the school.
whyA: The school is the party being required to allow the exam; it does not certify the student's status.
whyB: The barangay captain is not named as a certifying authority under the law.
whyC: DepEd, CHED, and TESDA impose sanctions on violating schools; they do not certify disadvantaged status.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 11984 (approved March 11, 2024), Sec. 4, ang magse-certify na disadvantaged ang estudyante ay ang MSWDO, CSWDO o PSWDO, o ang DSWD regional office.
hintTl: Hindi school ang nagse-certify; yung opisinang tumutulong sa pamilyang nasa crisis.

text: Aside from Negros Occidental (including Bacolod City) and Negros Oriental, which province is part of the Negros Island Region created by RA 12000 in 2024?
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12000 (Negros Island Region Act, signed June 13, 2024) forms the NIR from Negros Occidental with Bacolod City, Negros Oriental, and Siquijor.
hint: It is a small island province that was in Central Visayas, just off Negros Oriental.
whyA: Guimaras stays in Western Visayas; it is not part of the NIR.
whyC: Bohol remains in Central Visayas.
whyD: Antique is on Panay and remains in Western Visayas.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 12000 (pinirmahan June 13, 2024), ang Negros Island Region ay binubuo ng Negros Occidental (kasama ang Bacolod), Negros Oriental at Siquijor.
hintTl: Maliit na island province malapit sa Negros Oriental.

text: Under RA 12027, which lapsed into law in October 2024, the primary media of instruction from Kindergarten to Grade 3 generally revert to:
optionA: Filipino and English, with regional languages as auxiliary media
optionB: The learners' mother tongue in all public schools
optionC: English only, to improve international test scores
optionD: The dominant regional language, with Filipino as auxiliary
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12027 (lapsed into law October 10, 2024) discontinued the mother tongue as the main medium of instruction in K to 3; Filipino and English are used, regional languages serve as auxiliary media, and mother tongue stays optional only in monolingual classes.
hint: The law moved away from the policy that used each child's home language.
whyB: That was the old MTB-MLE policy that RA 12027 discontinued as the default.
whyC: The law did not make English the sole medium; Filipino is also used.
whyD: Regional languages are only auxiliary under the law, not the primary medium.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, dahil sa RA 12027 (nag-lapse into law October 10, 2024), Filipino at English na ulit ang medium of instruction sa K to 3, at auxiliary na lang ang regional languages.
hintTl: Tinanggal ng batas ang mother tongue bilang main na gamit sa pagtuturo.

text: The Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program Act, RA 12028 of 2024, establishes:
optionA: Free tuition in state universities and colleges
optionB: An alternative learning system for out-of-school youth and adults
optionC: A national learning intervention and tutorial program for learners below minimum proficiency
optionD: A daily school-based feeding program for undernourished learners
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12028 (dated October 16, 2024) sets up DepEd's ARAL Program of tutorial sessions in reading, mathematics, and science for learners below minimum proficiency, using teachers, para-teachers, and pre-service teachers as tutors.
hint: The acronym itself is the Filipino word for 'study'; think of catching up on learning gaps.
whyA: Free tuition in SUCs comes from a separate free higher education law, not the ARAL law.
whyB: The Alternative Learning System is governed by its own separate law, not RA 12028.
whyD: School-based feeding is under a separate feeding-program law, not RA 12028.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12028 o ARAL Program Act ay nag-establish ng national tutorial program ng DepEd sa reading, math at science para sa mga learner na below minimum proficiency.
hintTl: Ang acronym mismo, salitang Filipino na ibig sabihin ay mag-study.

text: Republic Act No. 11996, known as the 'Eddie Garcia Law' signed in May 2024, primarily protects:
optionA: National Artists and their surviving heirs
optionB: Professional athletes in national sports events
optionD: Workers in the movie and television industry
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 11996 (signed May 24, 2024) sets work hours, written contracts, wages, social protection, and safety standards for movie and television workers; it was named after actor Eddie Garcia, who died after an accident on a TV set in 2019.
hint: Recall the veteran actor it was named after and where his fatal accident happened.
whyA: National Artists' benefits come from separate laws and proclamations, not RA 11996.
whyB: The law does not cover athletes.
whyC: It covers film and TV production workers, not specifically journalists.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 11996 o Eddie Garcia Law (pinirmahan May 24, 2024) ay para protektahan ang mga worker sa movie at TV industry, gaya ng work hours, kontrata at safety sa set.
hintTl: Alalahanin kung saan naaksidente si Eddie Garcia noong 2019.

text: The Kabalikat sa Pagtuturo Act (RA 11997) of 2024 provides public school teachers with:
optionB: An annual teaching allowance raised to P10,000 and exempt from income tax
optionD: A one-time service recognition incentive every five years
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 11997 (dated May 31, 2024; signed in ceremony June 3, 2024) institutionalized the teaching allowance for supplies, raising it from P5,000 to P10,000 starting SY 2025-2026, exempt from income tax.
hint: It is the yearly cash teachers use for chalk, paper, and classroom materials.
whyA: The law is about the teaching (supplies) allowance, not salary.
whyC: Housing loans are not part of this law.
whyD: The benefit is yearly, not a one-time incentive.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 11997 o Kabalikat sa Pagtuturo Act, ang teaching allowance ng public school teachers ay ginawang P10,000 kada taon simula SY 2025-2026, at tax-exempt pa.
hintTl: Pambili ng chalk, papel at gamit sa classroom.

text: Under the Civil Service Commission's 2025 Omnibus Rules on the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), which earlier requirement was removed from the SALN?
optionA: Filing of the SALN every year
optionB: Filing of the SALN upon assumption of office
optionC: The signature of the declarant's spouse
explanation: As of November 2026, the CSC Omnibus Rules on SALN (CSC MC No. 14, s. 2025; applying from 2026) removed the spouse's signature requirement, allowed digital filing and online oath-taking, and replaced CSC MC No. 2, s. 2013.
hint: The change involves a person other than the employee filing the form.
whyA: Annual filing remains required.
whyB: Filing upon assumption of office remains required under the rules.
whyD: Liabilities are still declared; it is part of the SALN's very name.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa bagong Omnibus Rules on SALN ng CSC (MC No. 14, s. 2025), hindi na kailangan ang pirma ng spouse sa SALN, at puwede na rin ang digital filing.
hintTl: May kinalaman sa ibang tao, hindi sa mismong empleyadong nagfa-file.

text: The Konektadong Pinoy Act, which lapsed into law in August 2025, allows data transmission industry participants to build and operate networks:
optionA: Without a legislative franchise, subject to registration with the National Telecommunications Commission
optionB: Only after obtaining a congressional franchise and a CPCN
optionD: Under licenses issued by local government units instead of the NTC
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12234 (Konektadong Pinoy Act, lapsed into law August 24, 2025) lets data transmission players set up networks without a legislative franchise, subject to registration with the NTC (Sec. 8).
hint: The law aimed to open the market to new players by removing a step that required Congress.
whyB: That was the old barrier the law removed for data transmission.
whyC: The law does not impose 100% Filipino ownership; foreign participation follows existing laws like the Foreign Investments Act and Public Service Act.
whyD: Registration is with the NTC, not with LGUs.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, dahil sa RA 12234 o Konektadong Pinoy Act (nag-lapse into law August 24, 2025), puwede nang mag-operate ang data transmission providers kahit walang legislative franchise, basta naka-register sa NTC.
hintTl: Tinanggal ng batas yung requirement na dumaan pa sa Congress.

text: Republic Act No. 12022 of 2024, which replaced the Anti-Agricultural Smuggling Act of 2016, mainly:
optionA: Sets mandatory price ceilings on rice and vegetables
optionB: Creates a separate Department of Fisheries
optionC: Replaces rice import quotas with tariffs
optionD: Treats large-scale smuggling, hoarding, profiteering, and cartels of agricultural and fishery products as economic sabotage
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12022 (Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act, signed September 26, 2024) repealed RA 10845 and penalizes smuggling, hoarding, profiteering, and cartels of agricultural and fishery products as economic sabotage, with a council chaired by the President.
hint: Look for the option that matches the 'economic sabotage' in the law's popular name.
