whyA: Price ceilings fall under the Price Act, not RA 12022.
whyB: RA 12022 does not create a new department.
whyC: Rice tariffication was done by an earlier, separate law, not RA 12022.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 12022 (pinirmahan September 26, 2024), ang malakihang smuggling, hoarding, profiteering at cartel ng agri at fishery products ay economic sabotage na, at ni-repeal nito ang RA 10845.
hintTl: Tingnan yung option na tugma sa salitang 'economic sabotage' sa pangalan ng batas.

text: The Anti-POGO Act of 2025 (RA 12312) repealed which law that had imposed taxes on offshore gaming operations?
optionA: RA 9487, extending the franchise of PAGCOR
optionC: RA 10927, covering casinos under the Anti-Money Laundering Act
optionD: RA 9287, increasing penalties for illegal numbers games
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12312 (signed October 23, 2025) bans offshore gaming operations and repeals RA 11590, the 2021 law that taxed POGOs, making permanent the ban under Executive Order No. 74 (2024).
hint: It is the newest of the four laws, passed in 2021.
whyA: RA 9487 concerns PAGCOR's franchise and was not the POGO tax law.
whyC: RA 10927 brought casinos under AMLA coverage; it is not the POGO tax law.
whyD: RA 9287 deals with illegal numbers games like jueteng.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12312 o Anti-POGO Act (pinirmahan October 23, 2025) ay nag-ban sa POGO at ni-repeal ang RA 11590, yung 2021 law na nagpataw ng tax sa POGO.
hintTl: Pinakabago sa apat na batas, 2021 pa lang ipinasa.

text: Which agency leads the implementation of the Free Funeral Services Act (RA 12309), which lapsed into law in 2025?
optionB: Department of the Interior and Local Government
optionC: Department of Social Welfare and Development
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12309 (lapsed into law September 2025) provides free funeral services to poor families and families in crisis; the DSWD implements it, paying accredited funeral establishments through its AICS program.
hint: The same agency that gives burial aid to families in crisis.
whyA: DOH handles health services, not funeral assistance under this law.
whyB: DILG supervises LGUs but is not the lead agency for this law.
whyD: PhilHealth covers health insurance, not funeral services.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang DSWD ang nagpapatupad ng RA 12309 o Free Funeral Services Act, sa pamamagitan ng AICS program nila para sa mahihirap na pamilya.
hintTl: Yung ahensyang nagbibigay ng burial assistance sa mga pamilyang nasa crisis.

text: Under RA 12145 signed in April 2025, the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) was reorganized into the:
optionA: Department of Economy, Planning, and Development
optionD: Department of Economic Coordination and Development
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12145 (Economy, Planning, and Development Act, signed April 10, 2025) converted NEDA into the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) and reconstituted the NEDA Board as the Economy and Development Council.
hint: Its acronym is DEPDev.
whyB: No department with this name was created.
whyC: NEDA became an executive department, not a commission.
whyD: This is an invented name; the official name uses 'Economy, Planning, and Development'.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, dahil sa RA 12145 (pinirmahan April 10, 2025), naging Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) na ang NEDA.
hintTl: DEPDev ang acronym.

text: Which 2025 law authorizes the President to merge, restructure, or abolish redundant agencies of the Executive Branch and grants separation or retirement incentives to affected plantilla personnel?
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12231, the Government Optimization Act signed on August 4, 2025, lets the President streamline Executive Branch agencies and GOCCs not under RA 10149, through a committee chaired by the Executive Secretary.
hint: The law's name is about making government work at its best, not about cutting.
whyA: No law by this name was enacted.
whyB: This describes what the law does but is not its title.
whyD: No law by this name was enacted.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12231 o Government Optimization Act (pinirmahan August 4, 2025) ang nagbibigay ng power sa President na i-streamline ang mga ahensya ng Executive Branch, may incentives pa sa maaapektuhang empleyado.
hintTl: Tungkol sa pagpapahusay ng gobyerno ang pangalan, hindi sa pagbabawas.

text: Under the CSC's Revised Dress Code for Government Officials and Employees (CSC MC No. 16, s. 2024), what attire is prescribed on the first Monday of each month?
explanation: As of November 2026, CSC MC No. 16, s. 2024 (CSC Resolution No. 2400766, August 29, 2024) prescribes ASEAN-inspired attire on the first Monday and Filipiniana-inspired attire on the second to fourth Mondays; it also allows attire matching one's gender identity and expression.
hint: The first Monday honors the country's regional neighbors.
whyA: Filipiniana-inspired attire is for the second to fourth Mondays.
whyB: Agency uniforms are for Tuesday to Friday.
whyC: Smart casual is for days without an agency-prescribed uniform.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa CSC MC No. 16, s. 2024, ASEAN-inspired attire ang suot tuwing first Monday ng buwan, at Filipiniana-inspired naman sa second hanggang fourth Monday.
hintTl: Para sa mga kapitbahay na bansa natin sa rehiyon ang first Monday.

text: In 2025, the Civil Service Commission amended the education requirements for first-level government positions to formally recognize:
optionA: Only holders of a bachelor's degree
optionB: Junior high school (Grade 10) and senior high school (Grade 12) completers under K to 12
optionC: Only applicants with at least two years of college
optionD: Only TESDA National Certificate II holders
explanation: As of November 2026, CSC MC No. 7, s. 2025 (CSC Resolution No. 2500229, March 6, 2025) recognizes K to 12 completers as meeting the education requirement for first-level positions, subject to other qualification standards such as eligibility.
hint: The change aligned civil service rules with the current basic education system.
whyA: A bachelor's degree is generally a second-level requirement, not the new first-level standard.
whyC: The amendment opened first-level posts to K to 12 completers, not only to those with college units.
whyD: TESDA certification was not made the sole education requirement.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa CSC MC No. 7, s. 2025, kinikilala na ang Grade 10 at Grade 12 completers para sa first-level positions sa gobyerno, basta pasok sa ibang qualification standards gaya ng eligibility.
hintTl: In-align ng CSC ang rules sa K to 12 system.

text: The 2025 Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service (2025 RACCS), promulgated by the CSC on April 30, 2025, replaced the:
optionA: 2017 Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service
optionB: 1999 Uniform Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service
optionC: 2011 Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service
optionD: 2025 Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Human Resource Actions
explanation: As of November 2026, the 2025 RACCS (promulgated April 30, 2025, effective August 4, 2025) repealed and replaced the 2017 RACCS and added grave sexual harassment among offenses punishable by dismissal.
hint: Pick the most recent set of disciplinary rules before 2025.
whyB: The 1999 URACCS had long been superseded, first by the 2011 RRACCS.
whyC: The 2011 RRACCS was already replaced by the 2017 RACCS.
whyD: The Omnibus Rules on Appointments cover appointments, not administrative cases.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang 2025 RACCS ng CSC (promulgated April 30, 2025, effective August 4, 2025) ang pumalit sa 2017 RACCS, at isinama na ang grave sexual harassment sa mga offense na dismissal ang parusa.
hintTl: Piliin yung pinakahuling disciplinary rules bago mag-2025.

text: CSC Resolution No. 2600111, issued in January 2026, expanded the prohibition on gambling by government officials and employees to expressly cover:
optionA: Only gambling done during official working hours
optionB: Only unlicensed or illegal gambling houses
optionC: Online gambling such as online casinos, e-bingo, and e-sabong, even outside office hours
optionD: Only elective officials and their immediate families
explanation: As of November 2026, CSC Resolution No. 2600111 (January 19, 2026; published April 2026) bans government personnel from all forms of gambling, including online casinos, e-bingo, and e-sabong, and even mere presence in licensed casinos unless on official duty, during or beyond office hours.
hint: The update targeted gambling that can be done on a phone.
whyA: The ban applies during and beyond official working hours.
whyB: The ban covers licensed casinos too, not only illegal ones.
whyD: It covers officials and employees regardless of status across government, not only elective officials.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa CSC Resolution No. 2600111, bawal na sa government workers ang lahat ng sugal, kasama ang online casino, e-bingo at e-sabong, kahit labas na ng office hours.
hintTl: Yung sugal na kaya nang gawin sa cellphone ang dinagdag.

text: Under CSC Resolution No. 2600596, starting with the August 9, 2026 Career Service Examination, overseas Filipino workers may receive additional rating points if they have at least how many years of overseas employment?
explanation: As of November 2026, CSC Resolution No. 2600596 grants additional CSE rating points to OFWs with at least five years of overseas employment (continuous or intermittent, counted from January 1, 2000) who obtain a general rating of at least 70.00.
hint: It is half a decade of work abroad.
whyA: Two years is below the minimum set by the CSC.
whyB: Three years is below the minimum set by the CSC.
whyC: Ten years is more than what the CSC requires.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa CSC Resolution No. 2600596, may additional points sa CSE ang OFW na may at least five years na trabaho abroad, basta naka-70.00 man lang ang general rating.
hintTl: Kalahating dekada ng trabaho sa abroad.

text: In a certain code, PASIG is written as QBTJH. How is TAGUM written in the same code?
explanation: Each letter of PASIG moves one place forward in the alphabet (P→Q, A→B, S→T, I→J, G→H). Applying the same shift to TAGUM gives UBHVN.
steps:
1. Compare PASIG with QBTJH letter by letter: P→Q, A→B, S→T, I→J, G→H.
2. The rule is: move each letter one place forward.
3. Apply to TAGUM: T→U, A→B, G→H, U→V, M→N.
4. The code is UBHVN.
hint: Compare each letter of PASIG with the letter directly below it in the code.
whyA: SZFTL moves each letter one place backward; the code moves letters forward.
whyC: The third letter G becomes H, not I; this option shifts G by two.
whyD: VCIWO shifts every letter by two places, but the code shifts by only one.
explanationTl: Bawat letter ng PASIG ay inusog ng isa pasulong sa alphabet: P naging Q, A naging B, at iba pa. Kapag ginawa natin 'yan sa TAGUM, lalabas na UBHVN.
hintTl: Itapat mo ang bawat letter ng PASIG sa katapat niyang letter sa code. Ilang hakbang ang inusog?

text: In a certain code, CEBU is written as XVYF. How is DAVAO written in the same code?
explanation: Each letter is replaced by its mirror letter in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, C↔X, and so on). DAVAO becomes W-Z-E-Z-L.
steps:
1. C (3rd letter) → X (3rd from the end); E (5th) → V (5th from the end); B → Y; U (21st) → F (6th).
2. The rule: a letter in position n becomes the letter in position 27 − n.
3. D (4) → 23 = W; A (1) → 26 = Z; V (22) → 5 = E; A → Z; O (15) → 12 = L.
4. The code is WZEZL.
hint: Check where C and X sit: one counted from the start of the alphabet, the other from the end.
whyA: D pairs with W, not X; X is the mirror of C.
whyB: V (22nd letter) pairs with E (5th), not F; 22 + 5 = 27.
whyD: O (15th letter) pairs with L (12th), not M; 15 + 12 = 27.
explanationTl: Ang bawat letter ay pinapalitan ng 'kabaligtad' niya sa alphabet: A at Z, B at Y, C at X. Kaya ang DAVAO ay nagiging WZEZL.
hintTl: Pansinin mo kung pang-ilan ang C mula sa simula, at pang-ilan ang X mula sa dulo ng alphabet.

text: In a certain code, LIPA is written as 13-11-19-5. Following the same pattern, how is ILOG written?
explanation: Each number is the letter's position in the alphabet plus its position in the word. For ILOG: 9+1, 12+2, 15+3, 7+4 = 10-14-18-11.
steps:
1. LIPA in alphabet positions: L=12, I=9, P=16, A=1.
2. Code minus position: 13−12=1, 11−9=2, 19−16=3, 5−1=4. So the 1st letter gets +1, the 2nd +2, the 3rd +3, the 4th +4.
3. ILOG in alphabet positions: I=9, L=12, O=15, G=7.
4. Add 1, 2, 3, 4: 10, 14, 18, 11.
5. The code is 10-14-18-11.
hint: Subtract each letter's alphabet position from its code number. Does the difference stay the same?
whyA: These are only the plain alphabet positions; the code also adds each letter's place in the word.
whyB: This adds 1 to every letter, but the amount added grows by one for each letter.
whyC: The last letter G (7) is 4th in the word, so it becomes 7 + 4 = 11, not 12.
explanationTl: Ang code ay alphabet position ng letter plus kung pang-ilan siya sa salita. Sa ILOG: 9+1, 12+2, 15+3, 7+4, kaya 10-14-18-11.
hintTl: Ibawas mo ang alphabet position ng bawat letter sa code number niya. Pareho ba lagi ang difference?

text: What number comes next in the series? 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ___
explanation: Each term is the previous term times 2, plus 1. So 63 × 2 + 1 = 127.
hint: Look at how the differences between terms grow.
whyA: 125 adds 62, but the differences double each time (4, 8, 16, 32, so next is 64).
whyB: 126 is only 63 × 2; the pattern also adds 1 each time.
whyD: 129 adds 66; the next difference should be exactly double 32, which is 64.
explanationTl: Bawat term ay doble ng nauna, plus 1. Kaya 63 × 2 + 1 = 127. Pwede mo ring tingnan ang differences: 4, 8, 16, 32, kaya 64 ang susunod.
hintTl: Tingnan mo ang agwat ng bawat number. Paano siya lumalaki?

text: What letter comes next in the series? A, C, F, J, O, ___
explanation: The gaps between letters grow by one: +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6. O is the 15th letter, and 15 + 6 = 21, which is U.
steps:
1. Convert to positions: A=1, C=3, F=6, J=10, O=15.
2. Differences: 2, 3, 4, 5.
3. The next difference is 6: 15 + 6 = 21.
4. The 21st letter is U.
hint: Count how many places the series jumps each time.
whyB: T is O + 5, repeating the last gap instead of increasing it to 6.
whyC: V is O + 7, which skips the +6 step.
whyD: S is O + 4; the gaps are growing, not shrinking.
explanationTl: Lumalaki ng isa ang agwat: +2, +3, +4, +5, kaya +6 ang susunod. Ang O ay pang-15, at 15 + 6 = 21, which is U.
hintTl: Bilangin mo kung ilang letters ang nilalaktawan sa bawat hakbang.

text: What number comes next in the series? 2, 6, 3, 9, 6, 18, 15, ___
explanation: The series alternates two operations: multiply by 3, then subtract 3. After 15 comes 15 × 3 = 45.
hint: Two different operations take turns. Check what happens from 2 to 6, then from 6 to 3.
whyA: 12 applies − 3 again, but the operations alternate and the next one is × 3.
whyB: 30 multiplies by 2; every multiplying step in this series uses 3.
whyC: 54 is 18 × 3, which skips the − 3 step that already produced 15.
explanationTl: Salitan ang dalawang operation: times 3, tapos minus 3. Galing sa 18 − 3 = 15, kaya times 3 na ulit: 15 × 3 = 45.
hintTl: Dalawang operation ang nagsasalitan dito. Tingnan mo muna kung paano naging 6 ang 2, tapos paano naging 3 ang 6.

passage:
Families served in a rice distribution drive
Barangay | Families served
San Isidro | 120
Poblacion | 185
Mabini | 95
Rizal | 150
text: How many more families were served in Poblacion than in Mabini?
explanation: Poblacion served 185 families and Mabini served 95, so the difference is 185 − 95 = 90.
steps:
1. Poblacion: 185 families.
2. Mabini: 95 families.
3. Difference: 185 − 95 = 90.
hint: Find the two barangays in the table and subtract the smaller number from the larger.
whyA: 80 is a subtraction slip; 185 − 95 is 90.
whyB: 65 is Poblacion minus San Isidro (185 − 120), the wrong barangay.
whyC: 35 is Poblacion minus Rizal (185 − 150), the wrong barangay.
explanationTl: Sa table, 185 families sa Poblacion at 95 sa Mabini. Ibawas lang: 185 − 95 = 90.
hintTl: Hanapin mo lang sa table ang Poblacion at Mabini, tapos i-subtract.

passage:
Monthly sales of a sari-sari store
Month | Sales (₱)
January | 24,000
February | 20,000
March | 30,000
April | 28,000
text: By what percent did sales increase from February to March?
explanation: The increase is ₱30,000 − ₱20,000 = ₱10,000. Divided by February's ₱20,000 (the starting value), that is 50%.
hint: Percent increase is always measured against the earlier (starting) month.
whyB: 33⅓% divides the increase by March's sales; the base must be February, the starting month.
whyC: 150% is March as a percent of February (30,000 ÷ 20,000), not the increase.
whyD: 40% has no basis in the table; 10,000 ÷ 20,000 is 50%.
explanationTl: Tumaas ng ₱10,000 ang sales (30,000 − 20,000). I-divide sa February na ₱20,000 kasi 'yun ang pinagsimulan, kaya 50%.
hintTl: Sa percent increase, laging ang naunang buwan ang base o divisor.

passage:
Results of a municipal qualifying exam
Year | Examinees | Passers
2021 | 400 | 60
2022 | 500 | 90
2023 | 600 | 96
2024 | 450 | 72
text: Which year had the highest passing rate?
explanation: Passing rate = passers ÷ examinees. 2022 has 90 ÷ 500 = 18%, higher than 2021 (15%), 2023 (16%) and 2024 (16%).
hint: A rate compares passers to examinees, so compute a percentage for each year.
whyA: 2021 has the lowest rate of all, 60 ÷ 400 = 15%.
whyC: 2023 has the most passers (96), but out of 600 examinees that is only 16%.
whyD: 2024's rate is 72 ÷ 450 = 16%, lower than 2022's 18%.
explanationTl: Ang passing rate ay passers divided by examinees. Sa 2022, 90 ÷ 500 = 18%, 'yan ang pinakamataas. Ang 2023 ang may pinakamaraming pumasa, pero 16% lang dahil mas marami rin ang nag-exam.
hintTl: Huwag lang tingnan kung saan pinakamaraming pumasa. I-compute mo ang percent bawat taon.

passage:
Budget of a municipality (total ₱50 million)
Sector | Share of budget
Health | 24%
Education | 30%
Infrastructure | 26%
Agriculture | 12%
Others | 8%
text: The council cuts the Infrastructure budget by one-fourth and gives the entire amount cut to Agriculture. How much will Agriculture now receive?
explanation: Infrastructure gets 26% of ₱50 million = ₱13 million; one-fourth of that is ₱3.25 million. Agriculture's original ₱6 million plus ₱3.25 million is ₱9.25 million.
steps:
1. Infrastructure: 26% × ₱50 million = ₱13 million.
2. Amount cut: ₱13 million ÷ 4 = ₱3.25 million.
3. Agriculture originally: 12% × ₱50 million = ₱6 million.
4. New Agriculture budget: ₱6 million + ₱3.25 million = ₱9.25 million.
hint: Turn the percentages into peso amounts first, then move the cut.
whyA: ₱3.25 million is only the amount moved; Agriculture's original ₱6 million must be added.
whyB: 6.5 is one-fourth of 26 percentage points, read as millions of pesos; it is not Agriculture's total.
whyD: ₱7.5 million raises Agriculture's own budget by one-fourth instead of adding one-fourth of Infrastructure's.
explanationTl: Ang Infrastructure ay 26% ng ₱50M = ₱13M. One-fourth niyan ay ₱3.25M, at 'yan ang ililipat. Ang Agriculture ay dating ₱6M, kaya ₱6M + ₱3.25M = ₱9.25M.
hintTl: I-convert mo muna sa peso ang mga percent bago mo ilipat ang na-cut.

text: Carpenter : Hammer :: Tailor : ___
explanation: A hammer is a tool a carpenter uses. In the same way, a needle is a tool a tailor uses.
steps:
1. Relationship: a hammer is a tool used by a carpenter.
2. Find the tool used by a tailor.
3. Cloth is a material, a shop is a workplace, and a dress is a product; only the needle is a tool.
4. Answer: Needle.
hint: Ask what the hammer is to the carpenter: a tool, a material, a place, or a product?
whyB: Cloth is the material a tailor works on, not the tool; a hammer is a tool.
whyC: A shop is where a tailor works; the first pair is about a tool.
whyD: A dress is what a tailor makes, the product rather than the tool.
explanationTl: Ang martilyo ay gamit o tool ng karpintero. Ganoon din, ang karayom ang tool ng sastre. Ang tela ay materyales, ang shop ay lugar, at ang damit ay produkto.
hintTl: Ano ba ang martilyo sa karpintero: tool, materyales, lugar, o produkto?

text: Drought : Water :: Famine : ___
explanation: A drought is a severe shortage of water. A famine is a severe shortage of food.
steps:
1. Relationship: a drought is an extreme lack of water.
2. A famine is an extreme lack of something; find what.
3. A famine is an extreme lack of food.
4. Answer: Food.
hint: Complete the sentence: 'A drought is a severe shortage of ___.' Then do the same for famine.
whyA: Hunger is the result of a famine, not the thing that is lacking.
whyB: Crop failure can cause a famine, but a famine is defined as a shortage of food in general.
whyC: Rain relates to drought, not to the famine side of the pair.
explanationTl: Ang drought ay matinding kakulangan sa tubig. Ang famine naman ay matinding kakulangan sa pagkain. Ang gutom ay resulta lang ng famine, hindi 'yung kulang.
hintTl: Buuin mo: 'Ang drought ay kakulangan sa ___.' Tapos gawin mo rin sa famine.

explanation: 64 is the cube of 4 (4 × 4 × 4). The cube of 6 is 6 × 6 × 6 = 216.
steps:
1. Find how 4 becomes 64: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so 64 is 4 cubed.
2. Apply the same rule to 6: 6 × 6 × 6.
3. 6 × 6 = 36; 36 × 6 = 216.
4. Answer: 216.
hint: Try multiplying 4 by itself more than once.
whyA: 36 is 6 squared, but 4 squared is 16, not 64, so squaring does not fit the first pair.
whyB: 125 is the cube of 5, not of 6.
whyD: 196 is 14 squared; it does not follow any rule that turns 4 into 64.
explanationTl: Ang 64 ay 4 cubed, ibig sabihin 4 × 4 × 4. Kaya sa 6, 6 × 6 × 6 = 216. Hindi 36 kasi square 'yon, at ang square ng 4 ay 16 lang.
hintTl: Subukan mong i-multiply ang 4 sa sarili niya nang higit sa isang beses.

text: All employees of the municipal hall are residents of the town. Ana is an employee of the municipal hall. Which conclusion follows?
optionA: Ana is a resident of the town.
optionB: All residents of the town are employees of the municipal hall.
optionC: Ana is not a resident of the town.
optionD: Some residents of the town are not employees of the municipal hall.
explanation: Every municipal hall employee is a town resident, and Ana is one of those employees, so Ana must be a resident.
steps:
1. Premise 1: every municipal hall employee is a town resident.
2. Premise 2: Ana is a municipal hall employee.
3. So Ana belongs to the group that is entirely inside the residents group.
4. Conclusion: Ana is a resident of the town.
hint: Picture the circle of employees sitting inside the circle of residents. Where is Ana?
whyB: This reverses the first statement; 'all employees are residents' does not mean all residents are employees.
whyC: This contradicts the premises: Ana is an employee, and every employee is a resident.
whyD: This may be true in real life, but nothing in the statements says so.
explanationTl: Lahat ng empleyado ng munisipyo ay residente ng bayan, at empleyado si Ana. Kaya siguradong residente si Ana. Hindi ibig sabihin na lahat ng residente ay empleyado.
hintTl: Isipin mo na ang bilog ng mga empleyado ay nasa loob ng bilog ng mga residente. Nasaan si Ana?

text: If it rains, the outdoor program is moved to the gym. The outdoor program was not moved to the gym. Which conclusion is valid?
optionD: It may or may not have rained.
explanation: Rain always leads to the move. Since the move did not happen, it could not have rained (if P then Q; not Q, so not P).
steps:
1. Let P = it rains, Q = the program is moved to the gym.
2. Rule: if P, then Q.
3. Fact: not Q.
4. If P were true, Q would have to be true. Q is false, so P is false.
5. Conclusion: it did not rain.
hint: Suppose it had rained. What would have happened to the program?
whyA: If it had rained, the program would have been moved, and it was not.
whyC: Nothing in the statements mentions cancellation.
whyD: This would be right if we only knew the program was moved; knowing it was NOT moved rules rain out.
explanationTl: Kapag umulan, sigurado na ililipat sa gym. Hindi inilipat, kaya hindi umulan. Ito 'yung tinatawag na modus tollens: if P then Q, not Q, kaya not P.
hintTl: Ipagpalagay mo na umulan. Ano sana ang nangyari sa program?

text:
Statements: All auditors are accountants. Some accountants are lawyers.
Conclusions: I. Some auditors are lawyers. II. Some lawyers are accountants.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
explanation: Conclusion II simply restates 'some accountants are lawyers' in reverse, so it must be true. Conclusion I does not follow, because the accountants who are lawyers may all be outside the auditor group.
steps:
1. Draw the auditors circle entirely inside the accountants circle.
2. The lawyers circle overlaps the accountants circle somewhere.
3. That overlap can lie completely outside the auditors circle, so 'some auditors are lawyers' is not certain: I does not follow.
4. 'Some accountants are lawyers' means at least one person is both, so at least one lawyer is an accountant: II follows.
5. Only II follows.
hint: Draw the circles. Can the lawyers touch the accountants without touching the auditors?
whyA: I is not certain: the lawyers may overlap only with accountants who are not auditors.
whyC: II follows, but I does not, since the overlap with lawyers might miss the auditors entirely.
whyD: II does follow: if some accountants are lawyers, then those same people are lawyers who are accountants.
explanationTl: Ang II ay binaligtad lang na 'some accountants are lawyers', kaya sure 'yan. Ang I hindi sigurado, kasi pwedeng ang mga accountant na lawyer ay hindi auditor. Kaya Only II.
hintTl: I-drawing mo ang mga bilog. Pwede bang magdikit ang lawyers at accountants nang hindi tumatama sa auditors?

text: If Marco passes the exam, he will be hired. If he is hired, he will move to Cebu. Marco did not move to Cebu. Which of the following must be true?
optionB: Marco was not hired, but he may have passed the exam.
optionC: Marco did not pass the exam.
optionD: Marco passed the exam but was not hired.
explanation: Passing leads to being hired, and being hired leads to moving to Cebu. Since he did not move, he was not hired; since he was not hired, he did not pass.
steps:
1. Chain: pass → hired → move to Cebu.
2. Fact: he did not move to Cebu.
3. If he had been hired, he would have moved. So he was not hired.
4. If he had passed, he would have been hired. So he did not pass.
5. Marco did not pass the exam.
hint: Work backward along the chain from the fact you are given.
whyA: If he had been hired, he would have moved to Cebu, and he did not.
whyB: Not being hired rules out passing, because passing would have led to being hired.
whyD: This contradicts the first statement: passing guarantees being hired.
explanationTl: Ang kadena: pumasa → na-hire → lilipat sa Cebu. Hindi siya lumipat, kaya hindi siya na-hire. Hindi siya na-hire, kaya hindi rin siya pumasa.
hintTl: Balikan mo pabalik ang kadena simula sa alam nating nangyari.

text: Liza is the daughter of Ramon. Ramon's only sister is Carmen. What is Carmen to Liza?
explanation: Carmen is the sister of Liza's father, which makes her Liza's aunt.
steps:
1. Ramon is Liza's father.
2. Carmen is Ramon's sister.
3. The sister of one's father is one's aunt.
4. Carmen is Liza's aunt.
hint: Carmen is related to Liza through Liza's father.
whyA: Carmen is Ramon's sister, not his wife, so she cannot be Liza's mother.
whyB: Carmen is the sister of Liza's father, one generation above Liza.
whyC: A cousin would be Carmen's child, not Carmen herself.
explanationTl: Si Carmen ay kapatid ng tatay ni Liza. Ang kapatid na babae ng tatay mo ay tita o aunt mo.
hintTl: Sa tatay ni Liza dumadaan ang relasyon nila ni Carmen.

text: Pointing to a man in a photo, Jose said, "His mother is the only daughter of my mother." Jose is a man. How is Jose related to the man in the photo?
explanation: The only daughter of Jose's mother is Jose's sister, since Jose is male. The man's mother is Jose's sister, so Jose is the man's uncle.
steps:
1. 'The only daughter of my mother': Jose is male, so this is Jose's sister.
2. The man's mother is Jose's sister.
3. The brother of one's mother is one's uncle.
4. Jose is the man's uncle.
hint: First decide who 'the only daughter of my mother' is, remembering that Jose is a man.
whyA: The man's mother is Jose's sister, not Jose's wife, so Jose is not his father.
whyB: Jose and the man's mother are siblings; Jose is a generation above the man.
whyD: A cousin is a child of an aunt or uncle; Jose himself is the uncle.
explanationTl: Lalaki si Jose, kaya ang 'only daughter ng nanay ko' ay ang kapatid niyang babae. 'Yun ang nanay ng lalaki sa picture, kaya si Jose ay tito o uncle niya.
hintTl: Alamin mo muna kung sino ang 'only daughter ng nanay ko.' Tandaan na lalaki si Jose.

text: Statement: "The barangay posted the vaccination schedule in Filipino and Cebuano so that all residents would know it." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
optionA: The residents can read Filipino or Cebuano.
optionB: All residents want to be vaccinated.
optionC: Posting notices is the only way to inform residents.
explanation: The barangay expects the notices to inform everyone, which only works if the residents can read at least one of the two languages used.
steps:
1. Goal: all residents should know the schedule.
2. Method: post notices in Filipino and Cebuano.
3. The method works only if residents can read one of those languages.
4. So the statement assumes the residents can read Filipino or Cebuano.
hint: What must be true for the barangay's method to work?
whyB: The notice is about informing residents of the schedule, not about whether they want the vaccine.
whyC: Choosing notices does not mean the barangay thinks they are the only way.
whyD: Using Filipino and Cebuano does not imply that residents cannot read English.
explanationTl: Para gumana ang plano ng barangay na lahat ay makaalam, kailangang marunong magbasa ng Filipino o Cebuano ang mga residente. 'Yan ang assumption. Hindi naman sinasabi na hindi sila marunong mag-English.
hintTl: Ano ang dapat totoo para gumana ang ginawa ng barangay?

text: Statement: "The city government will add more buses on the route to reduce commuters' waiting time." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
optionB: Adding buses will shorten the time commuters wait.
optionC: This route has the most commuters in the city.
explanation: The plan adds buses in order to cut waiting time, so it takes for granted that more buses will actually shorten the wait.
steps:
1. Action: add more buses.
2. Goal: reduce waiting time.
3. The action makes sense only if more buses lead to shorter waits.
4. That link is the assumption.
hint: Look for the link between what the city will do and what it wants to achieve.
whyA: The statement does not compare buses with jeepneys.
whyC: The plan can make sense on any busy route; it need not be the busiest one.
whyD: Fares are not part of the goal, which is shorter waiting time.
explanationTl: Magdadagdag ng bus para bumilis ang paghihintay. Ibig sabihin, naniniwala ang city na mas maraming bus = mas maikling paghihintay. 'Yan ang assumption.
hintTl: Hanapin mo ang koneksyon ng gagawin ng city at ng gusto nitong mangyari.

text: Statement: "To speed up processing, the agency will now require applicants to submit their documents online." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
optionA: Online submissions can be processed faster than paper submissions.
optionB: Every applicant owns a personal computer.
optionC: Many paper documents submitted to the agency are fake.
optionD: Slow processing is the agency's only problem.
explanation: The agency switches to online submission in order to speed up processing, so it must believe online documents are faster to process than paper ones.
steps:
1. Action: require online submission.
2. Goal: faster processing.
3. The action serves the goal only if online documents are processed faster than paper.
4. That is the assumption.
hint: Which option, if false, would make the new rule pointless?
whyB: Applicants could submit using phones or internet cafés; owning a computer is not required.
whyC: The statement is about speed, not fake documents.
whyD: The agency can fix one problem without believing it is the only one.
explanationTl: Ginawa nilang online ang submission para bumilis ang proseso. So naniniwala sila na mas mabilis i-process ang online kaysa papel. Hindi kailangan na may sariling computer ang lahat, pwede namang cellphone o internet café.
hintTl: Alin sa mga option ang, kapag mali, mawawalan ng saysay ang bagong patakaran?

text: Which number does not belong to the group?
explanation: 17, 29 and 41 are prime numbers. 51 is not prime because 51 = 3 × 17.
steps:
1. 17: divisible only by 1 and 17, so prime.
2. 29: divisible only by 1 and 29, so prime.
3. 41: divisible only by 1 and 41, so prime.
4. 51: digit sum 5 + 1 = 6, so it is divisible by 3; 51 = 3 × 17, not prime.
5. 51 is the odd one.
hint: Try dividing each number by small numbers like 3 and 7.
whyA: 17 is prime, like 29 and 41.
whyC: 29 is prime, like 17 and 41.
whyD: 41 is prime, like 17 and 29.
explanationTl: Prime numbers ang 17, 29 at 41. Ang 51 ay mukhang prime pero hindi, kasi 3 × 17 = 51.
hintTl: Subukan mong i-divide ang bawat number sa maliliit na number gaya ng 3 at 7.

text: Which letter group does not belong?
explanation: In BDG, FHK and LNQ, the letters advance by 2 and then by 3. In PRV, they advance by 2 and then by 4 (R to V), which breaks the pattern.
hint: Write the alphabet position of each letter and check the gaps inside each group.
whyA: BDG follows the +2, +3 pattern (B, D, G).
whyB: FHK follows the +2, +3 pattern (F, H, K).
whyD: LNQ follows the +2, +3 pattern (L, N, Q).
explanationTl: Sa BDG, FHK at LNQ, ang agwat ay +2 tapos +3. Sa PRV, +2 tapos +4 (R papuntang V), kaya siya ang naiiba.
hintTl: Isulat mo ang alphabet position ng bawat letter, tapos tingnan ang agwat sa loob ng bawat group.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, a Senator must be at least how many years old on the day of the election?
explanation: Art. VI, Sec. 3 requires a Senator to be a natural-born citizen, at least 35 years old on the day of the election, able to read and write, a registered voter, and a resident of the Philippines for at least two years immediately before the election.
hint: It is higher than the age for a district representative but lower than the age for the President.
whyA: 25 is the minimum age for a member of the House of Representatives (Art. VI, Sec. 6), not a Senator.
whyB: 30 is not an age requirement for any member of Congress under Art. VI.
whyD: 40 is the minimum age for the President and Vice-President (Art. VII, Secs. 2 and 3).
explanationTl: Sa Art. VI, Sec. 3, ang Senator ay dapat natural-born citizen, at least 35 years old sa mismong araw ng election, marunong magbasa at magsulat, registered voter, at resident ng Pilipinas nang at least two years bago ang election.
hintTl: Mas mataas ito sa age ng congressman, pero mas mababa sa age ng President.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the President is elected for a term of six years. Which rule on reelection applies to the President?
optionA: The President may be reelected for one more consecutive term.
optionB: The President is not eligible for any reelection.
optionC: The President may be reelected once if Congress approves by a two-thirds vote.
optionD: The President may be reelected as long as total service does not exceed ten years.
explanation: Art. VII, Sec. 4 states that the President shall not be eligible for any reelection. The six-year term is a single term.
hint: Think of the six-year term as a one-time term.
whyA: Art. VII, Sec. 4 bars any reelection, so there is no second consecutive term.
whyC: Congress has no power to allow a presidential reelection; the bar is in the Constitution itself.
whyD: There is no ten-year cap rule; the Constitution simply bars reelection.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 4, malinaw na ang President ay hindi na pwedeng ma-reelect kahit kailan. Isang six-year term lang talaga.
hintTl: Isipin mo na ang six-year term ng President ay one-time lang.

text: The principle 'Public office is a public trust' is expressly stated in which Article of the 1987 Constitution?
optionA: Article II - Declaration of Principles and State Policies
optionD: Article XI - Accountability of Public Officers
explanation: Art. XI, Sec. 1 opens with 'Public office is a public trust' and requires public officers to be accountable to the people at all times.
hint: Look for the Article that deals with holding public officers answerable to the people.
whyA: Art. II has a related policy on honesty and integrity in the public service (Sec. 27), but the public-trust declaration is in Art. XI.
whyB: Art. III lists the rights of persons against the State, not the duties of public officers.
whyC: Art. IX creates the CSC, COMELEC and COA; it does not contain this declaration.
explanationTl: Nasa Art. XI, Sec. 1 ang 'Public office is a public trust.' Ibig sabihin, ang mga public officer ay dapat accountable sa taong-bayan sa lahat ng oras.
hintTl: Hanapin ang Article na tungkol sa pananagutan o accountability ng mga public officer.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the civil service covers government-owned or controlled corporations (GOCCs) that:
optionB: were organized under the general corporation law
optionC: are wholly owned by the government, whatever their charter
optionD: earn income from their own operations
explanation: Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(1) states that the civil service embraces all branches, subdivisions, instrumentalities and agencies of the Government, including GOCCs with original charters.
hint: The test is how the corporation was created, not how much the government owns.
whyB: GOCCs organized under the general corporation law do not have original charters, so they fall outside Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(1).
whyC: Ownership is not the test in the Constitution; the deciding factor is an original charter.
whyD: Whether a GOCC earns income has nothing to do with civil service coverage.
explanationTl: Sabi ng Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(1), sakop ng civil service ang lahat ng branches at agencies ng gobyerno, kasama ang mga GOCC na may original charter, ibig sabihin, nilikha ng sariling batas.
hintTl: Ang tanong dito ay kung paano nabuo ang corporation, hindi kung gaano kalaki ang share ng gobyerno.

text: Mario, a permanent clerk in a municipal treasurer's office, plans to campaign for a mayoral candidate after office hours. Under the 1987 Constitution, which statement is correct?
optionA: He may campaign as long as he does it outside office hours.
optionB: He may not engage, directly or indirectly, in any partisan political campaign.
optionC: He may campaign if he first files a leave of absence.
optionD: He may campaign only for candidates outside his own municipality.
explanation: Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(4) provides that no officer or employee in the civil service shall engage, directly or indirectly, in any electioneering or partisan political campaign. He keeps his right to vote.
hint: The ban covers both direct and indirect participation, with no exception for time or place.
whyA: The constitutional ban does not depend on office hours.
whyC: Going on leave does not lift the ban; he remains a civil service employee.
whyD: The ban covers any partisan political campaign, wherever the candidate runs.
explanationTl: Ayon sa Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(4), bawal sa kahit sinong civil service employee ang sumali, direct man o indirect, sa electioneering o partisan political campaign. Pwede pa rin siyang bumoto, pero bawal mangampanya.
hintTl: Sakop ng ban ang direct at indirect na pagsali, at walang exception kahit after office hours.

text: Ana ran for city councilor and lost. Under the 1987 Constitution, she may not be appointed to any office in the Government or in any GOCC or its subsidiaries within what period?
optionB: Until the term she ran for has ended
explanation: Art. IX-B, Sec. 6 provides that no candidate who has lost in any election shall, within one year after such election, be appointed to any office in the Government or any GOCC or in any of their subsidiaries.
hint: The ban is counted from the election date and is shorter than a full term of office.
whyA: Six months is too short; the Constitution sets a longer ban.
whyB: The ban is not tied to the term she ran for; it is a fixed period after the election.
whyC: Two years is longer than the period stated in Art. IX-B, Sec. 6.
explanationTl: Sa Art. IX-B, Sec. 6, ang natalong kandidato ay hindi pwedeng i-appoint sa kahit anong government office o GOCC sa loob ng one year after ng election. Para hindi gawing consolation prize ang pwesto sa gobyerno.
hintTl: Binibilang ito mula sa araw ng election, at mas maikli kaysa sa isang buong term.

text: In impeachment proceedings, what vote of all the Members of the House of Representatives is needed to affirm a favorable resolution with the Articles of Impeachment?
explanation: Art. XI, Sec. 3(3) states that a vote of at least one-third of all the Members of the House is necessary to affirm a favorable resolution with the Articles of Impeachment of the Committee, or to override its contrary resolution.
hint: The House only needs to send the case to trial, so its threshold is the lowest among the choices.
whyB: A majority is not the threshold; the Constitution sets a lower bar for the House.
whyC: Two-thirds of all the Senators is the vote needed to convict in the Senate (Art. XI, Sec. 3(6)), not to impeach in the House.
whyD: Three-fourths of all Members of Congress is the vote for proposing constitutional amendments (Art. XVII, Sec. 1), not for impeachment.
explanationTl: Sa Art. XI, Sec. 3(3), kailangan lang ng at least one-third ng lahat ng Members ng House para i-affirm ang Articles of Impeachment. Ang two-thirds ay para sa conviction sa Senate na.
hintTl: Ang House ay nagpapasa lang ng kaso papuntang trial, kaya pinakamababa ang kailangang boto dito.

text: Which of the following is NOT one of the norms of conduct listed in Section 4 of RA 6713?
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 4 lists eight norms: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living. Loyalty to the appointing authority is not among them.
hint: The norms point public servants toward the public, not toward a particular person.
whyA: Professionalism is a norm under Sec. 4(b).
whyB: Political neutrality is a norm under Sec. 4(d).
whyD: Simple living is a norm under Sec. 4(h).
explanationTl: Walo ang norms of conduct sa RA 6713, Sec. 4: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, at simple living. Walang 'loyalty to the appointing authority' diyan.
hintTl: Ang norms ay naka-focus sa publiko, hindi sa isang tao o boss.

text: A municipal engineer and her family avoid flashy cars and lavish parties and live within their means. Which norm of conduct under RA 6713 does this reflect?
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 4(h) requires public officials and employees and their families to lead modest lives appropriate to their positions and income and not to indulge in extravagant or ostentatious display of wealth.
hint: Focus on the lifestyle, not the work output.
whyA: Professionalism (Sec. 4(b)) is about performing duties with excellence and skill, not about lifestyle.
whyC: Responsiveness to the public (Sec. 4(e)) is about extending prompt and courteous service.
whyD: Nationalism and patriotism (Sec. 4(f)) is about loyalty to the Republic and the Filipino people.
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 4(h), ang public employees at ang family nila ay dapat mamuhay nang simple, ayon sa position at income nila, at hindi nagpapakita ng sobrang yaman o pagmamayabang.
hintTl: Tingnan mo ang lifestyle nila, hindi ang trabaho nila.

text: A resident sends a letter to a city office asking about her request. Under Section 5 of RA 6713, the office must respond to her letter within how many working days from receipt?
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 5(a) requires public officials and employees to respond within fifteen (15) working days from receipt to letters and other communications sent by the public, and the reply must state the action taken.
hint: It is about three working weeks.
whyA: 3 working days is not the period set in RA 6713, Sec. 5(a).
whyB: 7 working days is shorter than the period set in RA 6713, Sec. 5(a).
whyC: 10 working days is shorter than the period set in RA 6713, Sec. 5(a).
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 5(a), dapat sagutin ng government office ang sulat ng publiko within 15 working days mula nang matanggap ito, at dapat nakasulat sa reply kung anong action ang ginawa.
hintTl: Mga tatlong working weeks ito.

text: Liza processes business permits at the municipal hall. An applicant whose permit is still pending gives her a new cellphone 'as thanks in advance.' She did not ask for it. Under RA 6713, which is correct?
optionA: She may not accept it, because it comes from a person whose transaction may be affected by her office.
optionB: She may keep it, because she did not solicit it.
optionC: She may keep it, provided she declares it in her SALN.
optionD: She may keep it once the permit has been released.
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 7(d) prohibits public officials and employees from soliciting or accepting, directly or indirectly, any gift or anything of monetary value from any person in connection with any transaction which may be affected by the functions of their office.
hint: The law covers both asking for and receiving.
whyB: Sec. 7(d) prohibits accepting as well as soliciting, so not asking for it does not make it allowed.
whyC: Declaring a gift in the SALN does not cure a prohibited acceptance.
whyD: The gift is tied to her official transaction, so waiting until the permit is released does not make it allowed.
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 7(d), bawal mag-solicit o tumanggap ng regalo o anumang may monetary value mula sa taong may transaction na pwedeng maapektuhan ng trabaho mo. Kahit hindi niya hiningi, bawal pa ring tanggapin.
hintTl: Sakop ng batas hindi lang ang paghingi, kundi pati ang pagtanggap.

text: Carlo assumed office as an administrative aide on March 1. Under RA 6713, when must he file his first Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN)?
optionA: On or before April 30 of the following year
optionB: Within 15 days after assumption of office
optionC: Within 30 days after assumption of office
optionD: Within 60 days after assumption of office
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 8(A) requires the SALN to be filed within thirty (30) days after assumption of office, on or before April 30 of every year thereafter, and within thirty (30) days after separation from the service.
hint: The first filing is counted from the day he took office, not from a fixed calendar date.
whyA: April 30 is the deadline for the yearly filings after the first one, not for the first SALN.
whyB: 15 days is shorter than the period in Sec. 8(A).
whyD: 60 days is longer than the period in Sec. 8(A).
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 8(A), ang unang SALN ay dapat i-file within 30 days after mag-assume ng office. Pagkatapos noon, every year na on or before April 30, at within 30 days ulit pag umalis na sa service.
hintTl: Ang unang filing ay binibilang mula sa araw na nag-start siya, hindi sa fixed na date sa calendar.

text: Jun resigned from a government regulatory office. A private firm licensed by that office offers him a job as consultant. Under RA 6713, for how long after his resignation does the prohibition on such employment still apply to him?
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 7(b) bars employment as consultant or officer in a private enterprise regulated, supervised or licensed by one's office, and states that these prohibitions continue to apply for one (1) year after resignation, retirement or separation from public office.
hint: The cooling-off period is shorter than a typical elective term.
whyA: Six months is shorter than the period stated in Sec. 7(b).
whyC: Two years is longer than the period stated in Sec. 7(b).
whyD: Five years is far longer than the period stated in Sec. 7(b).
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 7(b), bawal maging consultant o employee sa private company na nire-regulate o nili-license ng dati mong office, at tuloy pa rin ang bawal na ito for one year after mag-resign, mag-retire o ma-separate sa service.
hintTl: Ang 'cooling-off' period ay mas maikli kaysa sa isang elective term.

text: The Bill of Rights is found in which Article of the 1987 Constitution?
explanation: Article III of the 1987 Constitution is the Bill of Rights. Its Sec. 1 provides that no person shall be deprived of life, liberty or property without due process of law, nor be denied the equal protection of the laws.
hint: It comes right after the Declaration of Principles and State Policies.
whyB: Article II is the Declaration of Principles and State Policies.
whyC: Article VI is the Legislative Department.
whyD: Article XIII is Social Justice and Human Rights, which creates the CHR, but it is not the Bill of Rights.
explanationTl: Ang Bill of Rights ay nasa Article III. Sa Sec. 1 nito, walang tao na pwedeng alisan ng life, liberty o property nang walang due process, at lahat ay may equal protection of the laws.
hintTl: Sumunod ito agad sa Declaration of Principles and State Policies.

text: Human Rights Day is observed every December 10 because on that date in 1948 the United Nations General Assembly adopted the:
optionD: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
explanation: The UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948 (Resolution 217 A (III)). Its Art. 1 declares that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.
hint: It is a declaration, not a treaty or a charter.
whyA: The UN Charter was signed in 1945 and created the UN itself.
whyB: The Geneva Conventions on the laws of war were concluded in 1949 at a diplomatic conference.
whyD: The ICCPR was adopted later, in 1966.
explanationTl: Noong December 10, 1948, inadopt ng UN General Assembly ang Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Sa Art. 1 nito, lahat ng tao ay ipinanganak na malaya at pantay sa dignity at rights.
hintTl: Declaration ito, hindi treaty o charter.

text: During custodial investigation, a suspect tells the police he no longer wants a lawyer. Under Art. III, Sec. 12 of the 1987 Constitution, his waiver of the right to counsel is valid only if it is:
optionA: made orally and recorded on video
optionB: made in writing before the investigating officer
optionD: made in writing and in the presence of counsel
explanation: Art. III, Sec. 12(1) gives a person under investigation the right to remain silent and to have competent and independent counsel, and states that these rights cannot be waived except in writing and in the presence of counsel.
hint: Two conditions must both be present, and one of them is the very right being waived.
whyA: An oral waiver is not enough; the Constitution requires writing.
whyB: Writing alone is not enough; counsel must also be present.
whyC: Notarization is not the constitutional requirement; the presence of counsel is.
explanationTl: Sa Art. III, Sec. 12(1), ang suspect ay may right to remain silent at right to counsel. Pwede lang niyang i-waive ang mga ito kung in writing at may abogado na kasama mismo noong nag-waive siya.
hintTl: Dalawang kondisyon ang kailangan, at ang isa ay mismong 'yung right na wina-waive.

text: Under Article XIII, Section 18 of the 1987 Constitution, the Commission on Human Rights may investigate, on its own or on complaint by any party, all forms of human rights violations involving:
optionA: economic, social and cultural rights only
optionC: all crimes, with power to try and convict the offenders
optionD: administrative offenses of all civil servants
explanation: Art. XIII, Sec. 18(1) empowers the CHR to investigate, on its own or on complaint by any party, all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights.
hint: Think of rights like life, liberty, free speech and voting.
whyA: Sec. 18(1) refers to civil and political rights, not only economic, social and cultural rights.
whyC: The CHR investigates; it is not a court and cannot try or convict offenders.
whyD: Administrative discipline of civil servants belongs to other bodies such as the CSC and the Ombudsman, not the CHR.
explanationTl: Sa Art. XIII, Sec. 18(1), ang CHR ay pwedeng mag-investigate, kusa man o dahil may nag-complain, ng lahat ng human rights violations na may kinalaman sa civil and political rights.
hintTl: Isipin ang mga rights gaya ng right to life, liberty, free speech at pagboto.

text: Under RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000), a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) shall be established in every:
explanation: RA 9003, Sec. 32 provides that a Materials Recovery Facility shall be established in every barangay or cluster of barangays.
hint: Think of the smallest political unit, working alone or together with its neighbors.
whyA: The law places MRFs at a much more local level than the province.
whyB: Sec. 32 assigns MRFs to barangays or clusters of barangays, not only to cities or municipalities.
whyC: Households segregate waste at source, but the MRF is a barangay-level facility.
explanationTl: Sa RA 9003, Sec. 32, dapat may Materials Recovery Facility o MRF sa bawat barangay o cluster ng mga barangay.
hintTl: Isipin ang pinakamaliit na political unit, mag-isa man o kasama ng mga kalapit nito.

text: In Barangay Malinis, residents segregate their garbage at the source. Under RA 9003, who is responsible for collecting the non-recyclable materials and special wastes?
optionD: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources
explanation: RA 9003, Sec. 10 assigns the barangay to collect biodegradable, compostable and reusable wastes, while the collection of non-recyclable materials and special wastes is the responsibility of the municipality or city.
hint: The barangay handles the wastes that can be composted or reused; the harder wastes go one level up.
whyA: The barangay collects biodegradable, compostable and reusable wastes, not non-recyclables and special wastes.
whyB: Sec. 10 does not give this collection duty to the province.
whyD: The DENR sets standards and oversees; it does not do the actual collection.
explanationTl: Sa RA 9003, Sec. 10, ang barangay ang kumokolekta ng biodegradable, compostable at reusable na basura. Pero ang non-recyclable at special wastes, responsibility na ng municipality o city.
hintTl: Ang barangay ang bahala sa nabubulok at reusable; ang mas mahirap na basura, isang level pataas.

text: Republic Act No. 9275 is known as the:
optionC: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
optionD: Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act of 1990
explanation: RA 9275, Sec. 1 states that the Act shall be known as the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004. It aims to protect the country's water bodies from pollution.
hint: Match the number to the most recent year among the choices.
whyB: The Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999 is RA 8749.
whyC: The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000 is RA 9003.
whyD: The Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act of 1990 is RA 6969.
explanationTl: Sa RA 9275, Sec. 1, ang batas na ito ay tinatawag na Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004. Layunin nitong protektahan ang mga katubigan ng bansa laban sa polusyon.
hintTl: Itugma ang number sa pinakabagong taon sa mga choices.

text: A sack of rice costs ₱1,200. During a sale it is sold at 15% off. What is the sale price?
hint: Find the discount first, then take it away from the original price.
whyA: ₱180 is only the discount, not the price you pay.
whyC: Subtracted ₱15 instead of 15% of the price.
whyD: Added the 15% instead of subtracting it.
explanationTl: Ang 15% ng ₱1,200 ay ₱180. Ibawas mo sa original price: ₱1,200 − ₱180 = ₱1,020 ang babayaran.
hintTl: Kunin muna ang discount, tapos ibawas sa original price.

text: A store raises the price of a ₱2,500 electric fan by 20%. A month later, it gives 20% off the new price. What is the final price?
explanation: After the increase the price is ₱3,000; 20% off ₱3,000 is ₱600, leaving ₱2,400. The two 20% changes do not cancel because they are taken from different bases.
hint: The 20% discount is taken from the raised price, not from ₱2,500.
whyA: Took the 20% discount from the original ₱2,500 and ignored the increase.
whyB: Assumed +20% and −20% cancel each other out.
whyD: Got the 4% net change right in size but treated it as an increase instead of a decrease.
explanationTl: Pagkatapos ng 20% increase, ₱3,000 na ang presyo. Ang 20% off ay kinukuha sa ₱3,000, kaya ₱600 ang bawas at ₱2,400 ang final. Hindi nagka-cancel ang +20% at −20% kasi magkaiba ang base.
hintTl: Sa bagong presyo kinukuha ang discount, hindi sa ₱2,500.

text: A barangay has 2,400 registered voters. If 1,800 of them voted, what percent did NOT vote?
hint: Find how many did not vote, then compare it with ALL registered voters.
whyB: 75% is the percent who DID vote.
whyC: Divided 600 by 1,800 (the voters) instead of by all 2,400 registered voters.
whyD: Misplaced the decimal point when converting 0.25 to a percent.
explanationTl: 600 ang hindi bumoto (2,400 − 1,800). Hatiin sa lahat ng registered voters: 600 ÷ 2,400 = 25%.
hintTl: Ilan ang hindi bumoto? Tapos i-compare sa kabuuang 2,400.

text: After a 25% increase, a kilo of pork now costs ₱400. What was the price before the increase?
explanation: The new price is 125% of the old price, so the old price is ₱400 ÷ 1.25 = ₱320. Check: ₱320 + 25% of ₱320 = ₱320 + ₱80 = ₱400.
hint: The 25% was computed on the OLD price, not on ₱400.
whyA: Took 25% off ₱400; the increase was based on the old price, not the new one.
whyB: Subtracted ₱25 instead of reversing a 25% increase.
whyC: Increased ₱400 by another 25% instead of working backward.
explanationTl: Ang ₱400 ay 125% ng lumang presyo. Kaya ₱400 ÷ 1.25 = ₱320. I-check: 320 + 80 = 400, tama.
stepsTl:
1. 1.25 × lumang presyo = ₱400
2. Lumang presyo = 400 ÷ 1.25 = ₱320
3. Check: 320 × 1.25 = 400
hintTl: Sa lumang presyo kinuha ang 25%, hindi sa ₱400. Mag-divide, huwag mag-subtract.

text: Simplify: 2/3 + 3/4 − 1/6
hint: Change all three fractions to twelfths first.
whyA: Added the 1/6 instead of subtracting it.
whyB: Left out the 1/6 term entirely.
whyD: Converted 1/6 to 4/12 instead of 2/12.
explanationTl: Gawin munang twelfths lahat: 8/12 + 9/12 − 2/12 = 15/12, na 1 1/4 kapag sinimplify.
hintTl: I-convert muna lahat sa twelfths bago mag-add o mag-subtract.

text: Juan spent 1/4 of his ₱800 weekly allowance on food and 1/5 of it on fare. How much does he have left?
explanation: Food is ₱200 and fare is ₱160, so he spent ₱360 and has ₱800 − ₱360 = ₱440 left.
hint: Both fractions are of the whole ₱800. Add what he spent, then subtract.
whyB: ₱360 is what he spent, not what is left.
whyC: Subtracted only the food money.
whyD: Subtracted only the fare.
explanationTl: ₱200 sa pagkain at ₱160 sa pamasahe, total ₱360 ang nagastos. Kaya ₱800 − ₱360 = ₱440 ang natira.
hintTl: Pareho silang fraction ng buong ₱800. Pagsamahin ang gastos, tapos ibawas.

text: Ana used 1/3 of a roll of cloth for curtains, then 1/4 of the remaining cloth for pillowcases. If 12 meters are left, how long was the roll?
explanation: After the curtains 2/3 of the roll remains; after the pillowcases 3/4 of that remains, which is 1/2 of the roll. Half the roll is 12 m, so the roll was 24 m.
steps:
1. After curtains: 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 of the roll left
2. Pillowcases use 1/4 of that, so 3/4 of it stays
3. Left = 3/4 × 2/3 = 1/2 of the roll
4. 1/2 of roll = 12 m, so roll = 24 m
5. Check: 24 − 8 = 16; 16 − 4 = 12
hint: The 1/4 is a fraction of what was LEFT, not of the whole roll.
whyA: Ignored the pillowcases and treated 12 m as 2/3 of the roll.
whyC: Took 1/4 of the whole roll instead of 1/4 of the remainder (1 − 1/3 − 1/4 = 5/12).
whyD: Treated the 12 m left as 1/3 of the roll.
explanationTl: Pagkatapos ng curtains, 2/3 ang natira. Sa pillowcases, 3/4 ng natira ang naiwan, kaya 3/4 × 2/3 = 1/2 ng roll. Kung 12 m ang kalahati, 24 m ang buong roll.
stepsTl:
1. Natira pagkatapos ng curtains = 2/3
2. Natira pagkatapos ng pillowcases = 3/4 × 2/3 = 1/2
3. 1/2 ng roll = 12 m, kaya roll = 24 m
hintTl: Ang 1/4 ay sa NATIRA kinuha, hindi sa buong roll.

text: Solve for x: 3x − 7 = 2x + 5
explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides and add 7 to both sides: x = 5 + 7 = 12. Check: 3(12) − 7 = 29 and 2(12) + 5 = 29.
hint: Move the x terms to one side and the numbers to the other, changing signs as you move them.
whyA: Moved the −7 without changing its sign (x = 5 − 7).
whyB: Changed the sign of the wrong number (x = −5 − 7).
whyC: Subtracted 5 from 7 instead of adding them.
explanationTl: Ilipat ang 2x sa kaliwa at ang −7 sa kanan (magiging +7). Kaya x = 5 + 7 = 12. Check: parehong 29 ang dalawang side.
hintTl: Kapag inilipat mo ang term sa kabilang side, palitan ang sign.

text: The sum of three consecutive even integers is 138. What is the largest of the three?
explanation: Let the numbers be n, n + 2 and n + 4. Then 3n + 6 = 138, so n = 44, and the numbers are 44, 46 and 48. The largest is 48.
hint: Consecutive even integers go up by 2. Dividing the sum by 3 gives the middle number.
whyA: 44 is the smallest of the three, not the largest.
whyB: 46 is the middle number (138 ÷ 3).
whyD: Used consecutive integers (45, 46, 47), which are not all even.
explanationTl: Let n, n + 2, n + 4. 3n + 6 = 138, kaya n = 44. Ang tatlo ay 44, 46, 48, at 48 ang pinakamalaki.
hintTl: Ang consecutive even ay pa-2 ang agwat. Ang 138 ÷ 3 ay ang nasa gitna.

text: A mother is three times as old as her daughter. In 12 years, she will be twice as old as her daughter. How old is the mother now?
explanation: Let the daughter be d, so the mother is 3d. In 12 years: 3d + 12 = 2(d + 12), so d = 12 and the mother is 36. Check: in 12 years they are 48 and 24.
steps:
1. Daughter = d, mother = 3d
2. In 12 years: 3d + 12 = 2(d + 12)
3. 3d + 12 = 2d + 24 → d = 12
4. Mother now = 3 × 12 = 36
5. Check: 48 = 2 × 24
hint: Add 12 to BOTH ages before setting up 'twice as old'.
whyB: 12 is the daughter's present age.
whyC: 48 is the mother's age 12 years from now.
whyD: 24 is the daughter's age 12 years from now.
explanationTl: Si daughter = d, si mother = 3d. Sa 12 years: 3d + 12 = 2(d + 12), kaya d = 12. Si mother ay 3 × 12 = 36 ngayon.
hintTl: Dagdagan ng 12 ang edad ng PAREHO bago i-set up ang 'twice as old'.

text: Tickets to a barangay fund-raising show cost ₱50 for children and ₱120 for adults. If 200 tickets were sold for a total of ₱18,400, how many adult tickets were sold?
explanation: If all 200 were children's tickets, sales would be ₱10,000. The extra ₱8,400 comes from adult tickets, each worth ₱70 more, so 8,400 ÷ 70 = 120 adults. Check: 120(₱120) + 80(₱50) = ₱14,400 + ₱4,000 = ₱18,400.
hint: Pretend all tickets were ₱50 and see how much extra money the adult tickets must explain.
whyA: 80 is the number of children's tickets.
whyC: Just split the 200 tickets evenly without using the prices.
whyD: Divided the extra ₱8,400 by 100 instead of by the ₱70 price difference.
explanationTl: Kung lahat ₱50, ₱10,000 lang sana. Ang sobrang ₱8,400 ay galing sa adult tickets na ₱70 ang dagdag bawat isa, kaya 8,400 ÷ 70 = 120 adults.
hintTl: Isipin na lahat ng ticket ay ₱50. Saan galing ang sobra?

text: What number comes next? 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ___
explanation: Each term is the previous term times 2, plus 1: 63 × 2 + 1 = 127. (The differences 4, 8, 16, 32 also double, so the next difference is 64.)
hint: Look at the differences between terms: 4, 8, 16, 32 …
whyA: Added 32 again instead of doubling the difference to 64.
whyB: Doubled 63 but forgot to add 1.
whyC: Jumped to the next power of 2; the terms are each 1 less than a power of 2.
explanationTl: I-double ang bawat term tapos +1: 63 × 2 + 1 = 127. Pansinin din, nagdo-double ang difference (4, 8, 16, 32, kaya 64 na ang kasunod).
hintTl: Tingnan ang difference ng bawat term: 4, 8, 16, 32…

text: What number comes next? 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ___
explanation: The multiplier goes up by one each time: ×2, ×3, ×4, ×5, so the next is ×6: 120 × 6 = 720.
hint: Divide each term by the one before it.
whyA: Multiplied by 2 only, ignoring that the multiplier grows.
whyB: Reused the last multiplier (×5) instead of moving to ×6.
whyD: Added the previous term (120 + 24) instead of multiplying.
explanationTl: Tumataas ng isa ang multiplier: ×2, ×3, ×4, ×5. Kaya ×6 na: 120 × 6 = 720.
hintTl: I-divide ang bawat term sa naunang term. Ano ang pattern?

text: A jeepney travels 45 km in 1.5 hours. What is its average speed?
explanation: Average speed = distance ÷ time = 45 km ÷ 1.5 h = 30 km/h.
steps:
1. Speed = distance ÷ time
2. 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h
hint: Speed = distance ÷ time.
whyB: Multiplied distance by time instead of dividing.
whyC: Ignored the extra half hour and divided by 1.
whyD: Divided by 2 hours instead of 1.5 hours.
explanationTl: Speed = distance ÷ time. 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h.
hintTl: Distance ÷ time ang speed.

text: A bus travels 120 km from one town to another at 60 km/h and returns along the same road at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole round trip?
explanation: Total distance is 240 km. The trip takes 2 h going and 3 h returning, 5 h in all, so the average speed is 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/h.
steps:
1. Time going = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 h
2. Time returning = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 h
3. Total distance = 240 km, total time = 5 h
4. Average speed = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/h
hint: Average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the two speeds.
whyA: Took the simple average of 60 and 40; the bus spends more time at the slower speed.
whyC: Divided only the one-way 120 km by the total 5 hours.
whyD: Used only the slower leg's speed.
explanationTl: 240 km ang total distance. 2 h papunta, 3 h pabalik, kaya 5 h lahat. 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/h. Hindi pwedeng i-average lang ang 60 at 40 kasi mas matagal ang byahe sa 40.
stepsTl:
1. Papunta: 120 ÷ 60 = 2 h
2. Pabalik: 120 ÷ 40 = 3 h
3. 240 km ÷ 5 h = 48 km/h
hintTl: Total distance ÷ total time, hindi average ng dalawang speed.

text: If 8 kilos of rice cost ₱416, how much do 13 kilos cost at the same price?
explanation: One kilo costs ₱416 ÷ 8 = ₱52, so 13 kilos cost 13 × ₱52 = ₱676.
hint: Find the price of one kilo first.
whyA: Set up the proportion upside down (416 × 8 ÷ 13).
whyB: Multiplied ₱416 by 13 without dividing by 8.
whyC: Multiplied the unit price by 12 instead of 13.
explanationTl: Isang kilo = 416 ÷ 8 = ₱52. Kaya 13 kilos = 13 × 52 = ₱676.
hintTl: Alamin muna ang presyo ng isang kilo.

text: Pedro can paint a classroom alone in 6 hours. Jose can paint the same classroom alone in 3 hours. How long will it take them working together?
explanation: Pedro paints 1/6 of the room per hour and Jose 1/3, so together they paint 1/6 + 2/6 = 1/2 per hour. The whole room takes 2 hours.
steps:
1. Pedro's rate = 1/6 room per hour
2. Jose's rate = 1/3 = 2/6 room per hour
3. Together = 3/6 = 1/2 room per hour
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/2 = 2 hours
hint: Add their hourly rates, not their times.
whyA: Averaged the two times.
whyB: Added the two times.
whyD: Halved Jose's time, as if Pedro worked as fast as Jose.
explanationTl: Si Pedro ay 1/6 ng kwarto kada oras, si Jose 1/3. Pagsamahin: 1/6 + 2/6 = 1/2 kada oras, kaya 2 hours lang tapos na.
hintTl: I-add ang rate nila kada oras, hindi ang oras mismo.

text: Pipe A can fill a water tank in 4 hours. Pipe B can empty the full tank in 6 hours. If both are opened when the tank is empty, how long will it take to fill the tank?
explanation: Pipe A adds 1/4 of the tank per hour and Pipe B removes 1/6, so the net rate is 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12 per hour. Filling the tank takes 12 hours.
steps:
1. Fill rate = 1/4 per hour
2. Drain rate = 1/6 per hour
3. Net rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12 per hour
4. Time = 12 hours
hint: The draining pipe works against the filling pipe, so subtract its rate.
whyB: Added the two rates as if both pipes were filling.
whyC: Subtracted the times (6 − 4) instead of the rates.
whyD: Added the two times.
explanationTl: Si Pipe A ay +1/4 kada oras, si Pipe B ay −1/6. Net: 1/4 − 1/6 = 1/12 kada oras, kaya 12 hours bago mapuno.
hintTl: Kalaban ng filling pipe ang draining pipe, kaya i-subtract ang rate nito.

text: Twelve workers can build the fence of a barangay covered court in 15 days. After 5 days of work, 4 workers leave. How many MORE days will the remaining workers need to finish the fence?
explanation: The job is 12 × 15 = 180 worker-days. After 5 days, 60 worker-days are done and 120 remain. Eight workers need 120 ÷ 8 = 15 more days.
steps:
1. Total work = 12 × 15 = 180 worker-days
2. Done in 5 days = 12 × 5 = 60 worker-days
3. Remaining = 180 − 60 = 120 worker-days
4. Workers left = 12 − 4 = 8
5. More days = 120 ÷ 8 = 15
hint: Count the job in worker-days and subtract what has already been done.
whyA: Used the original 10 remaining days and ignored that 4 workers left.
whyC: 20 is the total number of days including the first 5, not the additional days.
whyD: Divided the whole 180 worker-days by 8, forgetting the work already done.
explanationTl: 180 worker-days ang buong trabaho (12 × 15). Sa unang 5 araw, 60 na ang tapos, kaya 120 pa. Walo na lang ang workers: 120 ÷ 8 = 15 araw pa.
stepsTl:
1. 12 × 15 = 180 worker-days
2. Tapos na = 12 × 5 = 60
3. Natitira = 120
4. 120 ÷ 8 = 15 araw pa
hintTl: Bilangin ang trabaho bilang worker-days, tapos ibawas ang natapos na.

text: A rectangular lot measures 24 m by 15 m. Fencing costs ₱150 per meter. How much will it cost to fence the whole lot?
hint: Fencing goes around the edge, so you need the perimeter.
whyA: Used the area (360 m²) instead of the perimeter.
whyB: Used 24 + 15 = 39 m, only half the perimeter.
whyC: Fenced only three sides (24 + 24 + 15 = 63 m).
explanationTl: Sa paligid ang bakod, kaya perimeter ang kailangan: 2(24 + 15) = 78 m. 78 × ₱150 = ₱11,700.
hintTl: Sa gilid ng lote ang bakod, kaya perimeter, hindi area.

text: A rectangular garden 10 m long and 6 m wide is surrounded by a concrete path 2 m wide. What is the area of the path?
explanation: The garden plus path measures (10 + 4) by (6 + 4) = 14 m by 10 m = 140 m². Subtract the garden's 60 m² to get 80 m² for the path.
steps:
1. Outer length = 10 + 2 + 2 = 14 m
2. Outer width = 6 + 2 + 2 = 10 m
3. Outer area = 14 × 10 = 140 m²
4. Garden area = 10 × 6 = 60 m²
5. Path area = 140 − 60 = 80 m²
hint: The path adds 2 m on EACH side. Find the big rectangle, then remove the garden.
whyA: Covered only the four side strips and missed the four 2 m × 2 m corner squares.
whyB: 140 m² is the area of the garden plus the path.
whyD: Added only 2 m to each dimension instead of 2 m on each side.
explanationTl: Ang buong rectangle kasama ang path ay 14 m × 10 m = 140 m². Ibawas ang garden (60 m²), kaya 80 m² ang path.
hintTl: 2 m ang dagdag sa BAWAT gilid. Kunin ang malaking rectangle, tapos ibawas ang garden.

text: A student's scores in five quizzes are 88, 90, 76, 94 and 82. What is the average (mean) score?
explanation: The scores add up to 430, and 430 ÷ 5 = 86.
hint: Add all the scores, then divide by how many there are.
whyB: 88 is the median (middle score when sorted), not the mean.
whyC: Averaged only the highest and lowest scores (76 + 94) ÷ 2.
whyD: Divided the sum by 4 instead of 5.
explanationTl: I-add lahat: 430. Hatiin sa 5 quizzes: 430 ÷ 5 = 86.
hintTl: I-add lahat ng score, tapos i-divide sa dami ng quiz.

text: The average of five numbers is 24. When one of the numbers is removed, the average of the remaining four is 22. What number was removed?
explanation: The five numbers total 5 × 24 = 120 and the four left total 4 × 22 = 88. The removed number is 120 − 88 = 32.
steps:
1. Sum of 5 numbers = 5 × 24 = 120
2. Sum of 4 numbers = 4 × 22 = 88
3. Removed number = 120 − 88 = 32
hint: Turn each average back into a total.
whyA: Subtracted the two averages instead of the two totals.
whyB: Multiplied the drop in average (2) by 5.
whyC: Added the two averages.
explanationTl: Ang total ng lima ay 5 × 24 = 120, at ang total ng apat ay 4 × 22 = 88. Ang tinanggal: 120 − 88 = 32.
hintTl: Gawing total muna ang bawat average.

text: Ella has ₱1,000 made up of ₱20 and ₱50 bills only. She has 26 bills in all. How many ₱50 bills does she have?
explanation: If all 26 bills were ₱20, she would have ₱520. The extra ₱480 comes from ₱50 bills, each worth ₱30 more, so 480 ÷ 30 = 16. Check: 16(₱50) + 10(₱20) = ₱800 + ₱200 = ₱1,000.
hint: Use both facts: the number of bills and the total amount.
whyA: 10 is the number of ₱20 bills.
whyC: Split the 26 bills evenly without using the total amount.
whyD: Divided ₱1,000 by ₱50, as if all the money were in ₱50 bills.
explanationTl: Kung puro ₱20 ang 26 bills, ₱520 lang. Ang sobrang ₱480 ay galing sa ₱50 bills na ₱30 ang dagdag bawat isa: 480 ÷ 30 = 16.
hintTl: Gamitin pareho: ilan ang bills at magkano ang total.

text: A sari-sari store owner buys 5 dozen eggs at ₱90 per dozen. Six eggs break on the way, and he sells all the rest at ₱9 each. What is his profit?
hint: Profit = sales − cost. Only unbroken eggs can be sold.
whyA: Forgot the 6 broken eggs and sold all 60 (₱540 − ₱450).
whyB: ₱486 is the total sales, not the profit.
whyD: Subtracted the purchase cost of the broken eggs (6 × ₱7.50) instead of the sales lost on them (6 × ₱9).
explanationTl: Puhunan: 5 × ₱90 = ₱450. 54 na itlog lang ang nabenta (60 − 6), kaya 54 × ₱9 = ₱486. Kita: ₱486 − ₱450 = ₱36.
hintTl: Kita = benta − puhunan. Yung hindi basag lang ang mabebenta.

text: The mayor's speech was so VERBOSE that many residents left the covered court before it ended. VERBOSE most nearly means:
explanation: Verbose means using more words than needed. The residents leaving before the end fits a speech that dragged on.
hint: Why would people leave before a speech ends? Think about its length.
whyA: Brief is the opposite of verbose; a short speech would not make people leave early.
whyC: An inspiring speech would keep people in their seats, not drive them away.
whyD: Offensive could make people leave, but verbose is about too many words, not insulting content.
explanationTl: Ang 'verbose' ay sobrang daming salita, paligoy-ligoy. Kaya nag-alisan yung mga tao bago pa matapos, ang haba kasi ng speech.
hintTl: Bakit kaya umaalis ang mga tao bago matapos ang speech? Isipin mo yung haba nito.

text: The barangay captain remained IMPARTIAL while settling the dispute between the two neighbors. IMPARTIAL most nearly means:
explanation: Impartial means not favoring either side. A good mediator in a dispute treats both parties equally.
hint: Break the word apart: im- (not) + partial (favoring one part or side).
whyA: Unconcerned means not caring; an impartial person can care a lot and still not take sides.
whyB: Being strict is about firmness, not about refusing to favor either party.
whyD: Hesitant means unsure or slow to act, which has nothing to do with fairness.
explanationTl: Ang 'impartial' ay walang kinikilingan. Si kapitan ay patas sa dalawang magkapitbahay, hindi siya pumanig kahit kanino.
hintTl: Hatiin mo yung salita: im- (hindi) + partial (may kinikilingan).

text: The new records clerk was so METICULOUS that the auditors found no missing receipts. METICULOUS most nearly means:
explanation: Meticulous means paying close attention to every detail. That is why the auditors found nothing missing.
hint: What kind of worker leaves no missing receipts for the auditors to find?
whyA: Careless is the opposite; a careless clerk would leave gaps in the records.
whyB: Hurried work usually causes mistakes, not a clean audit.
whyC: Colorful describes style or appearance, not accuracy.
explanationTl: Ang 'meticulous' ay sobrang ingat at detalyado. Kaya walang nakitang kulang na resibo ang mga auditor.
hintTl: Anong klaseng empleyado ang walang naiiwang kulang na resibo?

text: The committee gave the proposal only a PERFUNCTORY review, so serious errors in the budget went unnoticed. PERFUNCTORY most nearly means:
optionA: done as a routine, with little care
explanation: Perfunctory means done only to get it over with, without real attention. Serious errors slipping through shows the review was careless.
hint: The result was that serious errors went unnoticed. What kind of review allows that?
whyB: A thorough review would have caught the budget errors; this is the opposite meaning.
whyC: A hostile, critical review would likely point out errors, not miss them.
whyD: Perfunctory is about the quality of attention, not about timing.
explanationTl: Ang 'perfunctory' ay ginawa lang for formality, walang tunay na effort. Kaya nakalusot yung malalaking error sa budget.
hintTl: Nakalusot ang malalaking error. Anong klaseng review ang ganun ang resulta?

text: The OSTENSIBLE purpose of the official's trip to Boracay was a three-day seminar, but he skipped every session. OSTENSIBLE most nearly means:
explanation: Ostensible describes a reason that is stated or appears to be true but may not be the real one. The skipped sessions show the seminar was only the declared excuse.
hint: The seminar was the reason he gave, but was it the real reason?
whyA: Hidden is nearly the opposite; the seminar was the openly declared reason, not a concealed one.
whyB: Legitimate means genuine and valid, but the sentence suggests the stated reason was not genuine.
whyD: Nothing in the sentence points to urgency; the word is about what is shown versus what is real.
explanationTl: Ang 'ostensible' ay yung dahilan na sinasabi o mukhang totoo, pero hindi talaga yun ang tunay na dahilan. Seminar daw, pero hindi naman umattend kahit isang session.
hintTl: Seminar ang sinabi niyang dahilan. Pero yun ba talaga ang tunay na pakay niya?

text: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to FRUGAL.
explanation: Frugal means careful and sparing in spending money or resources. Its opposite is wasteful.
hint: A frugal person stretches every peso. Who does the opposite?
whyA: Thrifty is a synonym of frugal, not an antonym.
whyB: Careful is close to the meaning of frugal, so it cannot be its opposite.
whyC: Poor describes how much money someone has, not how they spend it; a rich person can be frugal.
explanationTl: Ang 'frugal' ay matipid, marunong magtipid ng pera. Ang kabaligtaran niyan ay 'wasteful' o maaksaya.
hintTl: Ang frugal ay pinapahaba ang bawat piso. Sino ang gumagawa ng kabaligtaran?

text: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to EPHEMERAL.
explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time. Its opposite is enduring, meaning lasting a long time.
hint: Ephemeral describes things like a soap bubble or a trending post. What is the opposite of short-lived?
whyA: Fleeting is a synonym of ephemeral; both mean short-lived.
whyC: Fragile means easily broken; it is related in feel but is not about duration.
whyD: Brilliant means bright or very clever and has no link to how long something lasts.
explanationTl: Ang 'ephemeral' ay panandalian lang, mabilis mawala, parang bula. Kabaligtaran niyan ang 'enduring' na pangmatagalan.
hintTl: Parang bula o trending post ang ephemeral, saglit lang. Ano ang kabaligtaran ng panandalian?

text: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to EXACERBATE.
